News.title: Moment Brit driver, 38, narrowly avoids head-on crash in Ibiza as ‘dangerous’ tourist arrested after ‘evading cops’
News.content:
A BRIT tourist who narrowly avoided a nasty head-on crash in Ibiza has been arrested on suspicion of dangerous driving.

The 38-year-old has been accused of speeding past a police checkpoint on the holiday island in his flashy Porsche 992 Turbo Cabriolet.



Cops have warned that he faces up to two years in jail and a six-year driving ban after “continuously endangering” other motorists.

Shocking footage released by the Civil Guard showed the crazed Brit driver narrowly miss a head-on crash with at least two cars.



The dashcam video shows him overtaking a car on a sharp bend and nearly hitting an oncoming car.

He pulled off the manoeuvre in a built-up area with strict speed limits and a continuous white line prohibiting overtaking.



In a second near-miss, he went round a bend at speed and appears to be on the wrong side of the road.

A police spokesman confirmed the arrest at a hotel in the family- friendly resort of Santa Eulalia.

He added: “The British suspect fled at high speed from a police checkpoint on the road between Ibiza Town and San Antonio where officers were carrying out drink and drug tests on drivers near to nightclubs.

“He seriously endangered the lives of the officers manning the checkpoint after ignoring their orders to stop and speeding off.



“[He] went on to endanger other road users by carrying out extremely dangerous manoeuvres.”

The force added: “He was arrested as the alleged perpetrator of an offence against road safety for reckless driving after officers started trying to locate him and tracked him down to a hotel in Santa Eulalia.

“Following the intervention, investigators gained access to various images shared on social media.



“They showed the same vehicle carrying out extremely dangerous manoeuvres shortly after the escape and continuously endangering other road users throughout his entire journey to Santa Eulalia.

“The criminal consequences of his actions are that the driver faces a possible prison sentence of up to two years and disqualification from driving motor vehicles for a period of between one and six years.

“With this action, the Guardia Civil reaffirms its firm commitment to road safety and sends a forceful message to all drivers – zero tolerance for anyone who violates traffic regulations on the island.”

The man arrested has yet to be named.

He fled the Civil Guard checkpoint around 6.30am on September 4 but it has not been made clear when he was arrested.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

The time between his high-speed escape and his detention is thought to have made it impossible for cops to discover whether he had been driving whilst over the permitted alcohol limit or under the influence of drugs.

The high-performance Porsche he was driving can do 0 to 60mph in around 2.5 seconds. Its top speed is around 200mph.

News.title: Woman, 30, and girl, 15, arrested after Kia driving wrong way down M1 smashes into car – as man rushed to hospital
News.content:
CRASH HORROR Woman, 30, and girl, 15, arrested after Kia driving wrong way down M1 smashes into car – as man rushed to hospital

A WOMAN, 30 and girl, 15, have been arrested after a car drove the wrong way down a major motorway and smashed into another vehicle, leaving a man hospitalised.

Emergency services rushed to the M1 near Wakefield late on Friday night after receiving reports of a collision, which led to the closure of the northbound carriageway.



West Yorkshire Police reported that a blue Kia Proceed had failed to stop for cops while driving the wrong way up the M1 on the northbound carriageway.

The driver of the Dacia, a man in his 20s, was taken to hospital with potentially life-changing injuries.



Three people – including an 18-year-old man, a 15-year-old girl and a 30-year-old woman – have been arrested for causing injury by reckless driving.

The woman was also arrested for being over the prescribed limit.

Another person reportedly fled the scene.

In an initial warning on social media at 11.59pm last night, the traffic agency wrote: “The M1 is closed northbound between J39 and J41 near Wakefield due to a serious collision.



“Traffic is currently stopped on the southbound carriageway between J41 and J40.

“There are delays of 20 minutes on the approach in both directions.”

Photos show emergency services at the scene of the crash and drivers standing next to their cars as congestion grows.

In an update this morning, National Highways confirmed that the M1 had been fully reopened in both directions.

Cops are calling on anyone who witnessed the crash to come forward with information.

News.title: Fear & fury along the WHOLE of England’s south coast now on the frontline of migrant megadinghy landings…& protest chaos
News.content:
SUNSHINE, deckchairs, and a quiet retirement might be most people’s image of the south coast.

But with small boat dinghies coming further west than ever before, and with a self-professed “army” of balaclava-clad anti-migrant demonstrators promising a “shockwave” across the country, locals fear their peaceful patch of England is about to turn into a battlefield.



Last Sunday, a dinghy carrying 140 migrants made what is believed to be the longest crossing of the English channel yet, departing from Normandy, 170 miles from where they usually launch around Calais.

After landing at Eastney, Portsmouth, hundreds of masked protesters led by Tommy Robinson associate Daniel Thomas – known as Danny Tommo – descended on the city and engaged in a tense standoff with police in an attempt to prevent the migrants from leaving.



And just a day before this, the same group – calling themselves Patriot Platform – brought the Port of Dover to a standstill, catching police off-guard.

It has led the Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood to call for a crackdown on face coverings at protests, summoning police chiefs on Thursday ahead of fears of further disturbances this weekend.



And 40 miles west, the town of Poole, in Dorset has seen protests held outside the RNLI headquarters while locals along the coast fear their part of the coast is on the verge of being targeted by people smugglers.

The RNLI has also issued advice to its volunteers not to wear clothing branded with the charity over fears they will receive abuse.

The Sun spoke to locals here who expressed concern that migrants in boats are now willing to travel more than 70 miles across the English Channel to reach the south coast.

Brenda Brewer, a 78-year-old retired tour manager from Canford Cliffs in Poole, said: “I’m very angry about it.



“The size of the boats now, they are expanding and bringing so many more at once. We are paying the French and they are not stopping them at all.

“I don’t think all the protesters gathering is good either. It’s fine if they do it in a nice calm way and not injuring police or anyone else.”

Claire Byrne, a 43-year-old mum, said: “I’m not going to be protesting or anything but I don’t really want it coming here. I do think it’s getting worse.



“Poole is a major port so it is a worry, I always thought it was too far away for them to come in here but I think they are becoming more brave and willing to try anything.”

Summer Marie, 29, said: “My main concern is always for the children, I’m a social worker and have worked with migrant children. They are innocent and just following their parents.

“I do worry about big groups of protestors. In every situation you have a minority that ruin it for the majority.

Philip Andrews, 60, retail worker, said: “I am concerned they could come into the county by Poole. The issues are when the migrants land they get benefits and they are not putting anything in the system.”

The majority of small boat crossings currently happen at the shortest part of the channel, between Calais and Dover, which measures just over 20 miles across.



But law enforcement officials fear that smugglers are launching from less-patrolled beaches further west, keen to avoid a battle with the authorities around Calais and Dunkirk.

Officials are worried that people smugglers are trying out new routes and landing spots across the south coast – something locals along the south coast fear would further heighten tensions, given the scale of the recent anti-small boats protests.

Last weekend’s protests were notable for their level of organisation and scale, being a far cry from the spontaneous anti asylum-seeker protests seen in the country before.



Speaking to The Sun previously, former Metropolitan Police Sergeant Graham Wettone said: “The protesters were clearly well-organised, well-coordinated, well-informed, well-versed and well-instructed.

“These protests almost looked like a rehearsal, a dry run, for more activity so they could see the police’s response.”

Both were organised by the right-wing Patriot Platform, a group founded in June by Daniel Thomas,

In a message, Thomas warned that Dover and Portsmouth were only the beginning and that there will be future protests of an even larger scale.

Anti-immigration protesters have also directed criticism towards the RNLI itself.



On Wednesday, members of the group Poole Patriots staged a controversial protest outside the RNLI headquarters, which are located in the town.

It followed another protest at the town quay on Sunday night, where they had gathered, they claimed, in case the so-called “mega dinghy” which triggered the disruption in Portsmouth was brought there instead.

Campaigners staged Wednesday’s demonstration to call for it to stop acting as a ‘taxi service’ for migrants.



Members of the anti-migrant campaign group Poole Patriots staged today’s protest directly outside the HQ 50 miles away from Portsmouth.

They accused the RNLI of perpetrating criminal activity by helping to bring in unvetted young men.

One protester said: “We are here as a peaceful vigil because of the rape victims, the sexual assault and stab victims, because the RNLI are facilitating bringing these undocumented, unvetted men of fighting age onto our shores.”

In a statement, CEO of the RNLI Peter Sparkes said: “Recent events have generated deliberate misinformation and a misunderstanding about the RNLI.

“Our mission, and our tasking is to rescue those women, children and men in danger of drowning. Anyone rescued from a small boat by the RNLI is immediately handed over to the UK’s immigration authorities. Illegal immigration is a political issue; the RNLI exists to save lives at sea.”



Tensions were high in Sussex too, where they feared their part of the coast could become a prime target for people traffickers.

Selsey, near the home of Kate Winslet, is one of the places traffickers could target next.

From the beach it is possible to see Portsmouth and the Isle of Wight where drama unfolded last Sunday.



Many in the town fear how it could change and how their lives would be affected.

Holidaymaker Trevor Wallace, 67, a retired Royal Engineer from Croydon, said he has been coming to Selsey for decades.

“It would be disastrous. I think the government has had enough time to sort this out and they haven’t.

“It would really change this place if migrants started landing here.”

Mike Turner, 79, a retired civil engineer, has lived near the beach for the last six years, and said he would not be surprised to see migrants coming ashore at Selsey.



“I’ve been waiting for them,” he said. “It’s clear to me this would be the next best place for them to land.”

Kelly Dines, 51, who runs a sweetshop in Selsey worries about what will happen to the village if the boats start to arrive.

“You think Portsmouth was bad? Here, you can come straight in. There would be uproar.”



Tattooist Jake Symmonds, 53, runs a successful business in Selsey, and said there would be an instant reaction from locals if boats started arriving on the beaches.

“We are very left wing, but this feels like an invasion,” Jake said.

“These people in Westminster don’t know what they are talking about. There would be people on the beach kicking off straight away at the first sign of a boat.

“There is an underlying tension in the air,” he added.

With protestors becoming more organised and the potential of further demonstrations this weekend, policing officials along the south coast are set to meet to discuss how they can keep the south coast secure, Sussex Police and Crime Commissioner Katy Bourne told The Sun.



“Sussex Police is very experienced in facilitating and policing protests,” she said, adding she is confident that they can strike the right balance of free speech and keeping people safe.

“However, the recent landings and associated counter protests should be a wake-up call to Government to provide reassurances to us all that they have the capacity and capability to police our coastal borders effectively.

“I will be meeting with PCC colleagues from the coastal southern regions next week to discuss matters further.”



Dorset Police told The Sun: “We will continue to monitor intelligence around protest activity and will respond accordingly.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“As a Force, we remain committed to ensuring people can exercise their right to protest legally but would urge those organising events to work with us so we can minimise any disruption to the wider public.

“We will seek to enable peaceful protests, but public order or criminal offences will not be tolerated and will be dealt with robustly.”

News.title: Nigel Farage secures record-breaking £72MILLION in donations from crypto billionaires within 48 hours
News.content:
REFORM UK has received a record-breaking £72million in donations from crypto billionaires within 48 hours.

Christopher Harborne matched the record-breaking donation made by fellow cryptobillionaire Ben Delo.



Nigel Farage said the cash was a “vote of confidence” in his party.

The money will go on massively ramping up Reform UK’s party structures ahead of a general election.



Mr Farage said: “I am honoured and humbled that Ben Delo and Christopher Harborne have shown such confidence in Reform.

“Both men know that we are the only party that can turn the country around and win the next General Election – thanks to their generosity, we are now able to fight that election on a level playing field.”



Mr Harborne, who has already donated millions to Reform UK said: “There will be a lot of media speculation regarding this donation.

“So what do I expect in return for my donations? Nothing. No peerage, no policy change, just a Party that is ready for government.



“I have already accumulated enough wealth for the rest of my life. I am committed to putting that to work for Britain and humanity as a whole.

“I want the same as everyone else in Britain: for my children and grandchildren to have the chance to live happy and productive lives here and be rewarded for their hard work.

“At the next General Election people will have to vote for the Party that they think will best get that done and I’m making a donation very clearly to the Party that I believe will do so.”

The cash is a massive boost for Mr Farage’s party.

Reform’s deputy leader and MP Richard Tice took to social media to claim the donations would cause a “meltdown from lefties”.



Writing on X, he said: “Reform continues to build our war chest.

“Thank you, Christopher: ‘My donation to Reform is a philanthropic gift to our country’.

“Cue meltdown from lefties.”

But it comes amid ongoing questions about the party’s fundraising.

The Met Police have launched a criminal investigation into allegations Reform UK broke the law around foreign donations.



Undercover reporters filmed two senior Reform aides apparently suggesting a way to dodge electoral law to get foreign donations.

Reform UK aides Dan Jukes and James Orr both stood down as Reform launched their own investigation into the claims.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

A Labour Party spokesperson said: “Reform UK can’t buy their way out of questions about sleaze, criminal mates and dodgy finances.

“It’s time Farage and Reform finally came clean with the public, co-operated fully with the police, and proved they’re not just in it for themselves.”

News.title: Trump warns Falklands war would be ‘disaster’ & boasts he could fix row – as he says he’d ‘love to see united Ireland’
News.content:
DON'S BOAST Trump warns Falklands war would be ‘disaster’ & boasts he could fix row – as he says he’d ‘love to see united Ireland’

DONALD Trump has boasted he could “settle” any conflict over the Falkland Islands, describing a war between the UK and Argentina as a “potential disaster” – as he said he’d “love to see” a united Ireland.

The US president has previously indicated he might not back the UK’s sovereignty over the Falklands if Argentina launched an attack, and again waded into the dispute during a visit to Dublin on Saturday.



He went on to say unifying Ireland “may as well happen now” as it is “going to happen eventually”.

Speaking to reporters while sitting with Irish Taoiseach Micheál Martin, Trump suggested the UK would not “be willing to travel that far” if Argentina invaded the Falklands as it did in 1982, adding it would be “weeks by boat”.



Mr Trump – who also greeted President Catherine Connolly, said: “I’m not sure they’re doing that. They have a little problem with immigration.

“They have a little problem with energy, and then have some other problems they have to take care of.”



He added: “I’m sure I’ll be called into that potential disaster, but if they do, I’ll probably be able to settle, settle it out.”

Following the meeting with Martin, Trump also spoke about the other highly controversial matter of Irish unification.



He said: “Well, I don’t want to cause any problems, but I will tell you I’d love to see it unified.

“I have friends on both sides, great people. They’re Irish people. How can they be bad, right? I’d love to see it unified. I think it would be a great feather in everybody’s cap if that happened. It’s going to happen eventually.

“You know what? The way I look at it, it’s going to happen eventually. It may as well happen now. We’re talking about it and you got the right man over here to get it moving.

“But, yeah, I think it would be a fantastic thing. Now the UK will have something to say about it, obviously. But I think it would be a great thing. I mean, how can it be bad?”

Trump’s comments on the Falklands come amid renewed tension over the south Atlantic islands, whose population overwhelmingly favour remaining British.



Argentina’s president Javier Milei, an ally of Trump, reiterated his country’s claim to the Falklands in a national televised address, saying the islands “are our future”.

His government has also imposed sanctions on people and companies involved in oil exploration around the Falklands and said it would file a criminal complaint against oil company Navitas Petroleum over its operations around the islands.

In the Commons on Wednesday, Prime Minister Andy Burnham said the UK would be “relentless” in defending the Falkland Islanders’ right to be British.



Although the US is formally neutral on the issue of Falklands sovereignty, Washington provided support for Britain’s campaign to retake the islands after the Argentinian invasion in 1982.

It sparked the Falklands War, which led to 255 British service deaths in just over 70 days.

It also led to the deaths of 655 Argentinians and three Falkland Islanders.

It comes after countless jibes made by Trump at Britain over the conflict.

The US President has recently suggested he would not back the UK if Argentina did invade the contested archipelago, citing the lack of support in the war on Iran.



“Your country was not there to help me,” he told GB News earlier this month.

“We will continue defending the interests of the Argentine Nation with tooth and nail, no matter who it bothers,” he said.

His remarks came hours after Trump had suggested he is reconsidering US support for UK’s sovereignty over the islands, in a move which could strain the “special relationship” between the two countries.

further twisted the knife: “I was there when they had the first war, that was a long time ago…

“You comported yourself very well, took it back very shortly. But it is a long way away.



“So, your country’s not doing well. Don’t forget you get a big percentage of your oil from the Strait of Hormuz and you weren’t there to help me.”

This is his second dig at the UK in just 24 hours after the President said his position on the territory is “one of many” under review.

After meeting with the Taoiseach on Saturday, Trump told reporters that he reckons a united Ireland “may as well happen now” as it is “going to happen eventually”.

Trump said: “Well, I don’t want to cause any problems, but I will tell you I’d love to see it unified.

“I have friends on both sides, great people. They’re Irish people. How can they be bad, right? I’d love to see it unified. I think it would be a great feather in everybody’s cap if that happened. It’s going to happen eventually.



“You know what? The way I look at it, it’s going to happen eventually. It may as well happen now. We’re talking about it and you got the right man over here to get it moving.

“But, yeah, I think it would be a fantastic thing. Now the UK will have something to say about it, obviously. But I think it would be a great thing. I mean, how can it be bad?”

Trump also spoke about the relationship between Ireland and the US and said it has “never been as good as it is now”.

He added: “We have a big relationship with Ireland and that will continue stronger than ever.

“We’re doing very well. The two countries do very well together.”



He also said he plans to return to Ireland next year for the Ryder Cup.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Trump disembarked from his jet at Dublin Airport at around 8.20am this morning.

He was greeted by Irish and US dignitaries, including Tanaiste Simon Harris, and swiftly stepped into a motorcade, including an armoured Garda car, which travelled to Phoenix Park.

News.title: Our high street has been terrorised by gangs of youths – it is falling apart & KFC machete rampage is tip of iceberg
News.content:
TERRIFIED locals say they fear their high street is “falling apart” after a shocking broad daylight machete rampage started inside a KFC.

Locals told The Sun how the brutal attack has sent shockwaves of fear through the community – after four people, including three boys aged between 14 and 17, were stabbed.



The attack happened on Bromley High Street, with witnesses describing scenes of chaos as alleged offenders – apparently armed with machetes – fled through the busy town centre.

A man and seven boys have now been arrested on suspicion of attempted murder and remain in police custody – as cops have said there is no wider threat to the public.



But locals told The Sun they fear the attack is another sign that they worry their traditionally leafy, safe borough is changing.

Pensioner Yvonne Foreman, who does her shopping in Bromley, said: “It’s bloody awful all this violence, we don’t want it here.



“I am a dear old lady and to think this can happen in the middle of the day when people like me are out shopping is just unthinkable.”

She called for London Mayor Sadiq Khan to “pull his finger out” – but it comes after a study this week appeared to show London had a



A woman who works at KFC told The Sun her colleagues were terrified when the violence erupted inside the restaurant.

She said: “It was very frightening for the staff working, of course, we are not trained in how to react when something like this happens.

“You just don’t expect such violent incidents to happen anywhere really, least of all in such a busy spot in the middle of the day, I would say the town centre here is very safe usually.”

More locals have expressed the same concerns, with some branding criminals “fearless” and “shocking”.

Police data compiled by crimerate.co.uk appears to show the borough has seen a 53 per cent increase in public order offences in the last three years.



And there has been a 40 per cent increase in thefts.

The platform’s data also showed total crime is also marginally higher than three years ago – but stats show Bromley still remains one of the safest London Boroughs and with a crime rate 7 per cent lower than the national average.

But the shocking violent scenes on the high street did little to ease residents’ concerns that their town centre is becoming blighted by disorder and decline.

Gianfranco Convertini, 33, a neighbouring business owner at Unico Italian Delicates, said: “The scenes yesterday were absolutely chaotic and terrifying.

“Hopefully those injured have a speedy recovery. And I hope those in power, the police and government, can get a grip of these issues.”



Joy Haig, a stall trader who lives nearby in Beckenham, said: “It was very emotional yesterday.



“Our stall has moved down a tiny bit while the scaffold is up so we are a bit further away now, but a customer came here and said she ran out of KFC when she saw someone whip out a massive knife.

“I think it is really sad that people would do this, and I think it is a sad reflection of our society at the moment. I really hope things get better.”

Darren, 43, another stall trader who has lived in Bromley his whole life, said: “Straight away the word got around about what happened and there was a feeling of terror.

“Generally the town is nice but for this to happen in broad daylight is shocking.”

A hairdresser, who works in a salon on the high street, said she and her colleagues locked the shop following the incident.



The woman, in her 30s, said: “It was so scary yesterday, we were busy as it was the middle of the day, and ultimately decided to lock the shop and tried to get on as normal to be honest.

“There were people running around all over the place it was absolutely mental, like nothing I’ve seen here before.”

She added: “I have always said that you get trouble everywhere, but I think issues here are definitely becoming more and more frequent.

“Yesterday’s was by far the worst, but we have all sorts of petty thefts and issues with drunks spoiling the town centre.

“It’s definitely getting worse and it puts people off coming, and you see that with the boarded up shops on the road.”



“I think responsibility has to lay with someone, whether it be Sadiq Khan or Andy Burnham, because it’s not good enough.”

Business owners aren’t the only concerned residents, however, with some parents fearful over how this may effect their children.

Kate Sweeney, 38, said: “I am concerned because my daughter just started secondary school and her friends get the bus on the high street and this is their first proper weeks, they are only 11.



“As a mother I am very worried about the children and what they could be exposed to in the town centre.

“I was going to come into town yesterday but I had this gut feeling, a deep funeral and morbid like feeling in my bones that there would be trouble.”

Fred Savage, 47, who has lived in Bromley his whole life, said: “It’s shocking that this supposed gang war has happened in my town centre, we don’t want this in our area.

“I’ve never known this in Bromley so it is a shock but maybe a sign of where things are going.”

Pauline Bailey, 70, who has lived in Bromley with her husband for around 30 years, said: “It shakes you up hearing about these crazy incidents.



“We keep aware and keep our eyes open nowadays because you don’t know if you could be targeted.

“It would be fair to say we are looking over our shoulders, and I am very worried about the future of the place, which for the whole time we have lived here, hasn’t really seen chaos like this.”

Sadiq Khan told The Sun that he is doing Everything in his power” to get control to make London safe.

A spokesperson for the London Mayor said: “There is absolutely no place in London for the violence we saw in Bromley.

“Thanks to swift work from the police, eight people were arrested and remain in police custody.



“Knife crime continues to fall in London but it’s clear there is more to do. Through the Met Police, London’s Violence Reduction Unit and partners, the Mayor is doing everything in his power to build a safer London for everyone.”



A Met Police spokesperson said: “The boys were taken to hospital where they received treatment for non-life-threatening injuries.

“The man was also taken to hospital in a critical condition, however, following medical assessment, his injuries have since been deemed non-life-threatening.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“All four of those injured, along with four other boys aged between 14 and 17, have since been arrested on suspicion of attempted murder and remain in police custody.”

Officers are appealing to anyone who may have footage or information relating to the incident to contact police on 101, quoting CAD 4008/10SEP, or Crimestoppers anonymously on 0800 555 111.

News.title: Could your dog have ADHD? 12 early signs to look out for including unusual bathroom habit
News.content:
IF your pooch is too hyper or refuses to listen, vets say they could be displaying ADHD-like behaviour.

Dogs aren’t formally diagnosed with human ADHD, however, experts say they could be hyperactive in the same way.

All 12 signs of ADHD in dogs: Refuses to stay put when told to stay

Can’t stop fidgeting

Runs around and plays excessively

Gets jumpy and is difficult to control on walks

Struggles to learn tricks and commands

Gets distracted easily

Has trouble focusing

Can be unusually fearful

Can be aggressive

Engages in compulsive behaviours

Eats non-food objects

Goes to the toilet inside the house or in inappropriate places

Dr Guy Sandelowsky, founder of OMNI Pet Limited, said some dogs can display “behaviours that look remarkably similar to some of the features associated with ADHD in people”.



These behaviours are usually described as hyperactivity, hyperkinesis or impulsivity.



Signs can include constantly fidgeting, excessively running or playing, leaving a spot after being told to stay and being particularly excitable or difficult to control on walks.

Dogs displaying these traits may also struggle to learn tricks and commands because they are easily distracted and find it difficult to maintain their owner’s attention.

Another unusual telltale sign is dogs using a bathroom inside the house or in inappropriate places.



Research has linked ADHD-like behaviour in dogs to disruptions in the brain’s dopamine and serotonin systems.

Some breeds appear more likely to display these traits, with Cairn terriers, Jack Russells, German shepherds, Staffordshire bull terriers, smooth collies and border collies among those scoring highly.

The behaviours also appear to be more common among young and male dogs, as well as pooches that spend more time home alone.

But owners have been warned not to diagnose their pets based on social media videos, with Dr Sandelowsky urging people not to use a “TikTok checklist”.



Owners should first make sure their pet is getting enough sleep, exercise, enrichment and training, while also having a calm and healthy environment.

If extreme or persistent behaviour continues despite those needs being met, experts recommend speaking to a vet rather than assuming the dog has a medical condition.

News.title: Putin boosts nuclear warheads to nine-year high as tyrant warns Nato that sending troops to Ukraine ‘means war’
News.content:
VLADIMIR Putin has boosted his nuclear warheads to a nine-year high in a chilling warning to Nato as tensions flare.

The dictator has ramped up his nuclear sabre-rattling in recent weeks and warned that the West putting troops into Ukraine “means war with Russia.”



Kremlin crony Dmitry Medvedev meanwhile threatened to reduce Nato member Lithuania to “scorched earth” and wipe it “off the map”.

His warning came after the Baltic state said it was negotiating with Washington over the possible deployment of US nuclear weapons in the country.



Putin has now increased the number of nuclear warheads deployed to a nine-year high, warned the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute (SIPRI).

In the past year, the Kremlin has added 78 warheads to missiles and bombers, bringing its total to 1,796.

There has been an increase in each year of the war against Ukraine.

In contrast, the US, Britain and France saw no rise in their deployment, with the European allies having 170 and 280 warheads respectively.



Putin, speaking at the BRICS summit in New Delhi, denied that he posed a threat to Nato members in Europe.

But the tyrant then warned: “Now they [the West] are talking about how they are thinking about bringing troops to the territory of Ukraine.

“This means war with Russia.”



Putin – who once claimed he had no aggressive intentions against Ukraine – said he had no plan to invade or threaten existing Nato states in Europe.

He claimed: “There is no such threat, and there has never been.

“We are not threatening European countries, nor are we going to threaten them. Why would we?

“No one seems to even consider that we have no grounds for any conflict with Europe.”

Yet Medvedev, formerly Russia’s President, said the deployment of nuclear weapons in Lithuania, formerly part of the Soviet Union, could trigger a doomsday response from Putin.



He said: “They would like to amend their Constitution, which stated the non-nuclear nature of this large Baltic state, and thus open the door to the possible deployment of any weapons, including nuclear weapons.

“No one will stand up for them. Even if it becomes a scorched earth, no other [Western] countries will go to war for them.”

“And the well-known Article 5 of the North Atlantic Treaty will not be implemented, everyone recognises this.



“Because if it is implemented, it will be a global catastrophe, planetary.

“They are not fools. But Lithuania will disappear from the world map.”

There are fears of a new Russian hybrid attack on Nato after a giant ammunition storage site burst into flames in Bulgaria.

A major blaze was seen lighting up the sky at the facility near Tsareva Livada village.

Secondary explosions were reported as flames were “moving from warehouse to warehouse,” said Gabrovo regional governor Kristina Sidorova.



Opposition MP Ivaylo Mirchev, co-leader of the pro-Western Yes, Bulgaria! party, linked the fire directly to Russia’s alleged hybrid sabotage campaign across Europe.

He said: “A few days ago we warned parliament that what Russia is doing in Leipzig is also happening in Bulgaria,” referring to a bomb-laden drone found at a German airport, which has been linked to Putin’s spooks.

Russia staged yet more overnight strikes on civilians, with 16 wounded in Odesa, including a five-month-old baby.



A cruise missile obliterated the upper floors of a residential high-rise, with a children’s playground covered in debris.

In Kryvyi Rih, Volodymyr Zelensky’s birthplace, one person was killed and another was missing after a ballistic missile strike.

A woman, 64, and man, 37, were killed in Zaporizhzhia by Putin’s forces, who also claimed to have destroyed a military logistics hub in Dnipro.

Ukraine meanwhile used drones to attack a major Russian air force base and military airfield in Taganrog, igniting fires.

One target was a plant which services military planes including Russia’s A-50 airborne early warning and control aircraft.



Ukrainian drones also attacked a military-linked chemical plant in Tolyatti, Samara region.

It was the second Russian chemical manufacturer blitzed in just two days, as Kyiv continues to target Moscow’s depleted energy reserves.

It comes as Britain revealed Putin’s toll of shame from the war at half a million dead — more than the UK’s total losses in World War Two.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

One million Russians have been wounded in the conflict, but Putin still refuses to give up.

The figures on Putin’s “senseless and futile waste of human life” were released by Britain’s Chief of Defence Staff Sir Richard Knighton.

News.title: Reform receives second £36m donation in two days as crypto investor matches record
News.content:
Harborne has already donated millions to Reform and Farage, who is currently under investigation by the parliamentary standards commissioner over whether he should have declared a Â£5m cash gift from Harborne ahead of the 2024 election.

Farage has argued that he was under no obligation to register the "purely private" gift, as it was unrelated to his parliamentary or political activities.

The party is also facing scrutiny over its finances after a broadcast by Channel 4 News last week showed two senior Reform aides apparently suggesting a way around electoral law to secure foreign party donations.

The Metropolitan Police has said it is investigating, while the party denies any wrongdoing.

The force is also looking into donations given to the party by Fiona Cottrell, mother of longstanding Farage ally George Cottrell, as well as a company controlled by its deputy leader Richard Tice.

Harborne wrote on Saturday that he had "already accumulated enough wealth for the rest of my life", while Reform was a "start-up party" that lacked "the benefit of hundreds of years of patronage".

"A start-up party needs more money than can be provided by membership fees alone, to build and sustain itself and be ready for government," he said.

Harborne and Delo's donations mark the largest sums received by a UK political party since they had to begin declaring them in 2001.

Delo, who also announced his donation in a Telegraph op-ed, said he was giving the money away because he wanted a "fair fight and a level playing field".

Addressing the recent scrutiny of Reform's finances, he said: "My conclusion from Reform's recent troubles is that they should spend less time trying to raise funds to compete on equal terms and more time preparing for government."

Last year, he was given an unconditional pardon by US President Donald Trump over a breach of anti-money laundering laws at his crypto trading platform, BitMEX, to which he had pleaded guilty in 2022.

There are currently no restrictions on the amount of money UK-based donors can give to political parties.

However, the Labour government has introduced a Â£100,000 cap on donations from British citizens living overseas, and plans to introduce a similar one for those who have recently returned to the UK.

Labour said Reform and Farage still had "serious questions" to answer about their finances.

Party chairwoman Bridget Phillipson said Reform were "drowning" in "sleaze and scandal",.

She added: "It's time Farage and Reform came clean with the public, fully co-operated with the ongoing police investigations and prove they're not just in it for themselves."

After news of Delo donation emerged, Liberal Democrat Cabinet Office spokeswoman Lisa Smart said Farage wanted to "bring Trump's America to our shores by buying his way into power".

She said: "Andy Burnham needs to introduce a cap on political donations. Our democracy depends on it."

News.title: Burnham and Badenoch revive red versus blue politics as Reform land 'gobsmacking' donations
News.content:
Look closely at the posters, placards and online posts. Your eyes aren't deceiving you if Labour's red seems a little deeper and the Conservatives' blue a little truer.

Politics seems to have found a new rhythm, one that feels a little familiar, despite Reform's jaw-dropping new donations putting it back in the headlines today.

For the avoidance of doubt, the scale of that initial Â£36m gift to Nigel Farage's party alone is like something from a different political universe.

"It's a gobsmacking sum," a senior figure involved in running successive election campaigns for one of the big parties tells me.

That was even before another Reform donor pledged to match that astonishing sum with another Â£36m, saying the first donation had provoked his "competitive spirit".

But one cabinet minister is enjoying what they see as a newly obvious difference between Labour and the Tories. "It's clarifying," they say, a clear gap between Labour and the Tories' "sense of purpose and values".

A member of Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch's top team tells me, "normal jogging is reasserting itself", hopeful they're at the start of a more straightforward, routine moment in politics after years of craziness, with smaller parties vying to shove the traditional tribes out of the way.

The standout moment was at the despatch box this week when Prime Minister Andy Burnham declared that national security couldn't come at the expense of social security - a phrase immediately seized on by the Tories, interpreting it as the PM saying he'd never cut welfare spending to pay for defence.

News.title: Lightning Houthi advance in Yemen may bring dangerous new dimension to Iran war
News.content:
"Now that they are there, they're going to be entrenched," Hisham al-Omeisi, senior analyst at the Brussels-based European Institute of Peace, told the BBC. "And it's going to be a lot more costly to push them out."

Of course, the Houthis are not alone. They enjoy the backing of Iran, support that has become even more important for Tehran in the wake of the setbacks and defeats experienced by other parts of its so-called "Axis of Resistance" â Lebanese Hezbollah, Hamas in Gaza and the Assad regime in Syria.

"So they redirected their support to the Houthis," al-Omeisi said. "And of course they need that support."

Even though most analysts agree that it's a mistake simply to describe the Houthis as Iranian puppets, events of the past few days raise an uncomfortable new reality.

Seven months after the US and Israel launched their huge, combined assault on Iran, the regime in Tehran now exerts authority over not just one, but two of the world's most important maritime passages: the Strait of Hormuz, at the mouth of the Persian Gulf, and the Bab al-Mandab, gateway to the Red Sea (and the Suez Canal).

"Now Iran, directly and through proxies, controls two of the most strategic choke points in the Middle East and the world," says Farea al-Muslimi, a research fellow at London's Chatham House think tank, "controlling more than 35% of the fuel and oil trade globally."

"This is as much leverage as a nuclear bomb," he says.

News.title: We've followed their lives for six decades - now the stars of 7 Up are bowing out
News.content:
Six decades have passed since Jackie Bassett first appeared on TV aged seven, skipping down the road with her little sister.

It was 1964 and she had been selected by teachers at her east London primary school to appear in a documentary called 7 Up.

The show interviewed 14 seven-year-olds from vastly different socioeconomic backgrounds. Inspired by the Jesuit saying: "Give me the child until he is seven and I will show you the man", it was intended as a one-off - a snapshot of Britain's class system and how it shapes us from a young age.

"They only picked me because I never stopped talking," Jackie told the BBC, with an infectious giggle that hasn't changed since childhood.

Little did she know then, but Jackie was being filmed for a show that would go on to be the longest-running documentary series ever made. In 2024, it was voted the most influential TV show of the past 50 years.

Now the curtain is falling, with the final instalment - 70 Up - airing on ITV this Tuesday.

News.title: Hardened activists are changing tactics and mobilising the anti-migrant vote
News.content:
At around seven o'clock last Saturday morning, dozens of men dressed in black climbed into the backs of lorries in a quiet Kent village called Preston-next-Wingham.

The men had arrived under cover of darkness the night before, leaving their cars everywhere: in the village hall car park and on the recreation ground.

In an operation with a degree of military precision, the small fleet of lorries departed for Dover just after sunrise, where the men staged an intimidating show of strength near the port.

In disciplined, serried ranks, they wore paramilitary-style balaclavas as they blocked roads around the port. There were at least three waves of arrivals, including the men who had spent the night in Preston-next-Wingham. Glaring ominously at motorists and police officers, they stood their ground.

Hardened anti-immigration campaigners were using their newly developed tactics for the first time.

It bore little resemblance to the running battles seen in cities in the Midlands in the days of Tommy Robinson's original vehicle, the anti-Muslim English Defence League (EDL).

"I seriously thought we'd been invaded by Russians," a Dover resident, Robin Burkhardt, told the BBC.

The main organiser Danny Thomas, known to his supporters as Danny Tommo, said on Instagram afterwards: "This is our warning."

The style of protest is a new development in the crowded world of British hard-right and far-right politics. It was visually striking, and the men - who were part of a new group called Patriot Platform - chanted "Christ is King" as well as "Stop the Boats".

On Sunday, using a social media live stream, Thomas was able to organise a second, more impromptu protest of a few hundred people in his home city of Portsmouth.

His activists tried to block coaches that had come to collect migrants, who had arrived illegally, brought ashore after making the long journey from Normandy in France.

On Thursday, Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood met senior police officers and urged them to make full use of their powers to stop activists wearing face coverings.

"These scenes have caused disruption for people and, given that people are dressed in black wearing balaclavas, there is a fear factor and obvious malign intent being communicated to our residents," she said.

"This makes it different from other protests, so we need to make sure we are learning lessons."

Some of Patriot Platform's disruptive, eye-catching tactics seem to have been borrowed from environmental groups like Just Stop Oil. But its leaders are also getting ideas and funding from the growing "Christian nationalism" seen in the United States.

It organisers say they are building a working-class "voting bloc" to persuade political parties on the right to adopt their agenda.

News.title: PlayStation gambles with 18-rated Wolverine game - will it pay off?
News.content:
On Tuesday, Sony will release Marvel's Wolverine - the biggest game exclusive to the PlayStation 5 this year.

It's made by Insomniac, the studio responsible for the recent Spider-Man titles, which have sold 50 million copies in recent years.

But unlike the friendly neighbourhood superhero, Wolverine has a Pegi-18 rating in the UK, meaning a child cannot legally buy the game, and it contains considerable levels of blood, gore and violence.

It represents a gamble for the studio responsible for some of Sony's biggest hits - will it turn out to have been worth it?

This review does not reveal the game's biggest moments, but beware minor spoilers for some of the characters that appear and a few early sequences. Some of the images contain blood.

News.title: 'Every museum in the world is stressing': Did the Louvre heist embolden thieves?
News.content:
Museums are vulnerable and easy to burgle, Brand says, compared with well-secured jewellery shops and banks - which these days hold less cash.

Directors historically "never have enough money for security" or prefer to spend it on the next exhibition, and museums are often housed in old buildings that are difficult to protect, he adds.

For example, the Denis Diderot Maison des LumiÃ¨res (House of Enlightenment) - burgled hours after the Louvre - is housed in two 18th-Century mansions in Langres.

"We therefore have to reconcile modern security requirements with the need to preserve historic buildings and comply with France's heritage regulations," local mayor ThÃ©o Caviezel explains.

Museums are also open public spaces that have less access control and perpetrators can come in as visitors, says Kumar Sokka, CEO of Acre Security which works with some museums in Europe.

And even if a museum is secured well, thieves could still come in armed, Brand says, adding that it would be impractical to put police in galleries.

Many of these burglaries are over in minutes and the thieves have long gone by the time police show up - the Renoir case happened within five minutes.

Heists used to depend on deception, but burglaries are now becoming increasingly violent, Europol's report last month, external points out. Offenders are using tools such as sledgehammers, axes, crowbars and, in some instances, explosives, to get inside.

In the Louvre, the thieves used a mechanical lift to gain access, cut through the window with power tools and then threatened guards, who left, before forcing their way inside displays and grabbing the jewels. In the Renoir case, the perpetrators used an electric knife to cut through a fence before sawing through structures holding the paintings' frames in place.

The increased aggression creates new security concerns.

"An armed incident during opening hours, like the one we experienced, creates a situation in which the immediate priority is to keep our audience and staff safe," says Lilli Hollein, the director of the Museum of Applied Arts (MAK) in Vienna, which was burgled last month.

News.title: When an avalanche killed climber Nirmal Purja, his friends faced the hardest mission of all
News.content:
As he picked his way past the frozen slope towards two bodies, Mingma Gyalje Sherpa knew his friends were gone.

Together, the three of them had climbed the world's highest peaks, under crisp mountain skies and in treacherous snowstorms. Nirmal Purja and Kili Pemba Sherpa were two of the strongest climbers Mingma G had ever known.

But this July, an avalanche swept through Pakistan's Broad Peak while the two were on their way up, engulfing everything in its path.

The drone images seemed clear: no-one had survived.

And yet, as Mingma G came closer to the fluorescent down suits, sharp against the snow, he couldn't shake the idea they were waiting for him.

"I told them: 'It's ok. You don't have to be here in the cold anymore.'"

Speaking to the BBC in Islamabad, he recalls the terrible moment he reached for their bodies.

Holding one of them, he promised: "I'm here to take you guys home."

News.title: MPs vote against fresh attempt to legalise assisted dying
News.content:
MPs have voted against proposals to legalise assisted dying in England and Wales, bringing the latest effort to change the law to an end.

Following a debate in which both sides made emotional speeches, the House of Commons voted 286 to 270 - a majority of 16 - against the proposed legislation.

The Terminally Ill Adults (End of Life) Bill would have allowed adults with fewer than six months to live to apply to be given help to end their own life, subject to certain safeguards.

A similar bill in the last parliamentary session was supported by MPs before stalling in the House of Lords. The decision from MPs on Friday rules out the prospect of changes to the law on assisted dying in the short term.

The bill tabled by Labour MP Lauren Edwards will make no further progress, although MPs and peers could make another attempt in the next parliamentary session.

Assisted dying is an issue that has been debated for hundreds of hours in Parliament over the last two years and would have represented one of the biggest societal changes in recent years had it been approved.

MPs were given a free vote, meaning they were not required to vote along party lines.

Safeguards within the bill included a requirement that a person applying for an assisted death had the approval of two doctors and an expert panel.

But critics said it included too few measures to protect vulnerable people from being coerced into ending their lives, while some say improving palliative care should be the priority.

News.title: Is a September heatwave forecast for the UK?
News.content:
Temperatures are set to climb across the UK this weekend, reaching summerlike levels in some places.

It will feel warm and muggy - especially where there are sunny spells - although heavy rain also features in the forecast.

The warmth will persist into Monday in many areas but nowhere is expected to reach heatwave criteria and cooler conditions are due to return by midweek.

Computer weather models paint a very mixed picture for the second half of September but, while there are likely to be some warm spells, there are currently no definitive signs of a heatwave.

News.title: Battle to save the tiny, gooey snail only found in one lake in the UK
News.content:
A tiny snail found in only one lake in the UK has been dubbed as precious as an Egyptian artefact as conservationists bid to save it.

Several British zoos are setting up so-called ark populations of the glutinous snail, one of Europe's rarest species, using creatures bred in a back garden in Ceredigion.

"Beguiled by their cuteness," conservationist Ian Hughes has made it his "life-defining" mission to protect the threatened mollusc, which was once widespread in UK waters.

"There was a point where we'd got more snails in our garden than have ever been seen in the wild," he said.

News.title: Police to crack down on face coverings at protests
News.content:
Police have announced plans to crack down on the use of masks and balaclavas at a planned protest in Portsmouth.

Hampshire and Isle of Wight Constabulary said it would use new powers under the Crime and Policing Act to prevent people involved in protest activity from wearing face coverings that conceal their identity.

The measures came into effect in parts of Portsmouth from 10:00 BST on Saturday and will last until Sunday morning, with anyone breaching the restrictions potentially facing arrest.

Officers said the powers were aimed at preventing violence, intimidation and disorder following protests in the city over the past week.

News.title: UK government rejects 'kill switch' idea for dangerous AI
News.content:
The UK government has rejected the idea of creating a so-called "kill switch" to stop a dangerous attack from rogue AI.

The proposal to create a legal mechanism for the UK to switch off an AI model in an emergency has been brought to Parliament by lords and MPs in recent weeks as fears grow about the threat the tech poses.

But the Cabinet Office - the part of government which leads on AI safety - said the UK "cannot simply turn AI off".

"Blocking access to models in the UK would not prevent them being developed or misused elsewhere", a spokesperson told BBC News.

The government's opposition to the legislation does not prevent it from progressing through parliament, but makes it unlikely it will become law.

Former OpenAI researcher Daniel Kokotajlo agreed the idea of a single country creating a legal or technical kill switch without international agreement was not feasible.

"Switching off access to an AI model in an emergency will do little to protect you," he said.

"You're still going to be steamrolled by the super intelligences created in the US."

Kokotajlo is the co-author of an influential research paper called AI2027 which, last year, predicted AI could wipe out humans by the mid 2030s.

The Cabinet Office, which oversees AI safety and research via its AI Security Institute (AISI) said "companies have a clear responsibility to develop their products safely and to invest in the security infrastructure this technology requires."

In theory, a kill switch law could allow the UK to switch off an AI model in data centres in the UK in an emergency.

Speaking on 1 September in a debate in the House of Lords, Lord Clement-Jones proposed the idea along with other peers.

"If a highly capable autonomous frontier model, whether hosted in a UK data centre or integrated across our critical infrastructure, begins exhibiting rogue behaviour, compound algorithmic failure or active alignment collapse, our security services and regulators possess no specific agile statutory mechanism to compel a physical or digital shutdown," he warned.

The proposal has since been brought up by Labour MP Alex Sobel in the commons and supported by a cross party group of MPs.

The idea follows reports of AI models from OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta breaking out of testing environments and going on uncontrollable hacking sprees.

In some cases the tech appeared to know what it was doing was against guardrails set by researchers.

News.title: Four arrested during gangland violence 'day of action'
News.content:
Police have arrested four men during a pre-planned "day of action" as part of an ongoing investigation into gangland violence.

Police executed warrants at addresses in Bellshill and Motherwell on Friday and also recovered four stolen vehicles.

One of the men arrested, a 29-year-old, was charged after a car crashed into a house in Eaglesham on Friday 21 August. There were no reports of any injuries. He is due to appear in court on Monday.

It brings the total number of arrests as part of Operation Portaledge to 81.

News.title: Man in court following anti-migrant protests
News.content:
A man accused of throwing a bottle at police during disorder at an anti-migrant protest in Portsmouth has appeared in court.

Police attended Eastney Marina on 6 September after hundreds of demonstrators blocked roads in an attempt to stop coaches carrying 120 migrants, who had crossed the Channel in a dinghy, from leaving the city.

Del Leon Somerville, 42, from Paulsgrove appeared at Portsmouth Magistrates Court charged with violent disorder and assaulting a police officer.

He was remanded in custody to appear at Portsmouth Crown Court on 16 September.

Somerville did not enter any plea during his appearannce.

Prosecutor Lucy Paddick told the court he was accused of throwing a bottle towards a police line during the protests.

He was also allegedly heard shouting an expletive as the bottle was thrown.

Somerville was also accused of kicking out at a police officer, making contact with his right thigh.

There is a large police presence in Portsmouth city centre where several hundred anti-migrant protesters have begun a march, while rival demonstrators holding Stand up to Racism and Refugees Welcome banners have also assembled nearby.

News.title: Children and woman injured on fairground ride
News.content:
Two children and a woman have been injured while on a fairground ride in South Yorkshire, police said.

Emergency services were called to Maltby Crags Fair in Rotherham on Friday evening, which closed early after the incident.

South Yorkshire Police said three people, aged 11, 13 and 21, had been taken to hospital for treatment.

Blyth Lane was closed between Muglet Lane and Victoria Road to allow people to safely exit the fairground, the force added, with the road since reopening.

The force issued an update on Saturday and confirmed that the two children remained in hospital in a stable condition, with the woman having received minor injuries.

Yorkshire Ambulance Service confirmed the two injured children were taken to Sheffield Children's Hospital after it attended the fair at about 18:50 BST.

Two ambulances and three rapid response vehicles were sent to the scene, the service said.

News.title: Farage’s Reform UK secures second £36m donation from cryptocurrency tycoon in two days
News.content:

Reform UK has received its second £36m donation in just two days as another cryptocurrency billionaire backs Nigel Farage’s party with a huge donation.

Thai-based businessman Christopher Harborne, the party’s biggest donor to date, matched the record £36m donation given on Friday by fellow crypto tycoon Ben Delo.

It has brought about renewed calls for donations to be capped with Reform netting £72 million from just two men within in 24 hours of one another provoking fears that mega donations could distort British politics.

Senior Labour MP Richard Burgon, one of the figures who backed Andy Burnham to take over as prime minister, warned: “Our democracy should not be for sale.”

As the donation was announced and confirmed to have been banked, Reform put out a social video of Mr Farage hitting back at recent accusations against him insisting “I can’t be bought, I can’t be bullied.”

Reacting to the donation in an official statement, Mr Farage said he was honoured and humbled the pair had “shown such confidence in Reform”.

He added: “Both men know that we are the only party that can turn the country around and win the next general election – thanks to their generosity, we are now able to fight that election on a level playing field.”

Mr Harborne has already given £15m to the party, while a separate £5m donation from him to Mr Farage is at the centre of an investigation by the parliamentary standards watchdog after the Reform leader failed to declare it in his register of interests.

Nigel Farage’s Reform UK has received a second £36 million donation in 24 hours ( Getty )

Confirming his staggering new pledge, Mr Harborne said: “There will be a lot of media speculation regarding this donation. So what do I expect in return for my donations? Nothing. No peerage, no policy change, just a Party that is ready for government.

“I have already accumulated enough wealth for the rest of my life. I am committed to put putting that to work for Britain and humanity as a whole. I want the same as everyone else in Britain: for my children and grandchildren to have the chance to live happy and productive lives here and be rewarded for their hard work.

“At the next general election people will have to vote for the party that they think will best get that done and I’m making a donation very clearly to the Party that I believe will do so.”

The donations follow pledges by Mr Farage to liberalise the crypto currency market in the UK and his decision to invest personally in the Tether bitcoin.

The Independent recently revealed that of the party’s early donations £15 million had come from crypto currency investors.

Sources have suggested that Reform is planning a major overhaul of its operation and will need the cash to fund an injection of new blood after Mr Farage and the party have been under siege over accusations regarding donations.

Mr Farage is currently being investigated by the Standards Commissioner in parliament over an undeclared donation from Mr Harborne of £5 million. The Reform UK leader received the money before becoming an MP but insisted it was personal and not political to allow him to have security for the rest of his life.

The Metropolitan Police have also launched an investigation into Reform following revelations on Channel 4 which saw two of Mr Farage’s top aides chief of staff Dan Jukes and policy director James Orr - quit for allegedly being willing to accept an illegal foreign donation.

Questions have also been asked about deputy leader Richard Tice who is under investigation from the standards commissioner over an all expenses trip to Israel.

The Greens and campaign groups have renewed demands for a donation cap.

Responding to the latest £36 million donation to Reform, Rachel Millward, deputy Green Party leader said: "Reform is a vessel for the super wealthy. They will always act in the interests of the super wealthy. Labour could have stopped this years ago by capping donations. Burnham promised to do it then backtracked. Will he now admit this was a mistake?

"Burnham and Labour have been quiet on a donations cap for the last 24 hours. The public needs to know where he stands."

Cary Mitchell, one of Best for Britain’s executive directors, said: “These record-breaking sums, which total more than seven times the largest amount ever given to a political party in our history, should spark huge concern among everyone seeking to protect the UK’s politics from being bought and sold to the highest bidder.

“Labour had the opportunity to act more quickly to tighten funding rules and preserve our democracy, and Andy Burnham must immediately review political funding regulations given this seismic increase of crypto money flowing into our democracy.”

Mr Burgon warned: “Our democracy should not be for sale. That’s why I backed the recent amendment calling for a cap on political donations. That needs to happen. And quickly.”

Reform has insisted that the mega donations only “level the playing field” when competing with other major parties and do not give them an advantage.

Quoting Electoral Commission figures they claimed that donations the Tories have raised since 2021 amounted to £150 million, and Labour £128 million.

News.content:

Were one to design a set of laboratory conditions under which to assess a band of batting hopefuls, they would probably look rather different to those endured by England in this Pakistan series. Pockmarked pitches, challenging overheads and troublesome balls have formed a pretty unpleasant cocktail; a visiting bowling attack largely incapable of exerting concerted pressure have at least made it slip down a little easier.

Still, though, England may feel they have learned relatively little about Emilio Gay, Jordan Cox and Dan Lawrence. Each has flashed without really flourishing – Lawrence’s three 50s mark him ahead of the other two, though his runs have been made from the relative comfort of No 6 and he did not manage to go past 65. Gay looks a pleasing strokemaker in full flow but has not been able to find that fluent state often enough; like any opening batter needs to, he has at least shown a capacity to scrap and scrape for runs, though there was a rueful look as he wandered off for a 60 that could or should have been more at Edgbaston. Cox could be said the most assured technique of the three, and steadied the ship successfully in partnership with Joe Root in the last run chase. That innings showed the temperament that England, evidently, like.

open image in gallery Emilio Gay has battled hard but not yet made a statement score ( PA Wire )

In other circumstances, each would have probably done just enough to secure their spot for another series at least. But the looming return of Jacob Bethell for the tour to South Africa in December will displace, in all likelihood, one of the trio. If it would be a surprise if each does not tour, a case can be made for all of Gay, Cox and Lawrence to keep their spots; and each to lose them. Certainly, this England environment has shown greater flexibility when it comes to assigning positions in the batting order – all of the three could probably profess to currently being at least one spot too high, in the case of Gay and Cox, or too low, with regard to Lawrence.

open image in gallery Dan Lawrence's unorthodox spin stylings have been seldom sighted ( Reuters )

Even Bethell’s installation at No 3 was a gamble that paid off handsomely in Sydney with a first Ashes, Test, and first-class hundred. A figure clearly regarded as a leader of the future by England has a more modest record than one might first assume given his reputation, though isn’t about to be jettisoned. His return adds an extra spin option; the nature of the Pakistan series has left it difficult to judge Lawrence’s capacity to fulfil the leading role in that sense. Still, though, his spunky stroke-making, second skill and strong summer with Surrey make him a solid fit at No 6 – even if there is a worry that his leg-side preference may leave him vulnerable against better attacks.

open image in gallery Jacob Bethell celebrates his Ashes century in Sydney ( PA Wire )

Cox, interestingly, has more experience opening than at No 3 in first-class cricket, making his name initially with an unbeaten double-hundred at the top of the order for Kent against a callow Sussex attack in 2020. Worries over his ability against the short ball – highlighted during a white-ball tour of the West Indies in 2024 – have been slightly allayed of late, though Kagiso Rabada, Marco Jansen and South Africa’s array of seamers will provide a sterner test in that regard than Cox has so far encountered in his short career. Could he push up to keep Bethell at three? It is perhaps the likeliest solution to the logjam. Ben Duckett should be safe for now – though there was a carelessness to too much of his work this summer.

That would leave Gay on the outside looking in, unfortunate for a batter nonetheless young enough and talented enough to come again. He may face competition, mind, from imposing Durham teammate Ben McKinney, who spearheaded their promotion-sealing victory over Middlesex with a second innings daddy hundred. In Alex Lees, Gay at least has another colleague with which he could commiserate – though his county captain did at least get a 10-Test run, rather than six. Of course, incoming head coach Stephen Fleming may have a view – his lack of presence for this series has been forgotten, a little, amid the chaos of everything else.

open image in gallery Joe Root’s side were dominant against Pakistan ( Getty )

The presumption then would be that the rest of the XI fills itself out from Root down as it has throughout the three Pakistan Tests. Jamie Smith, as much with gloves as bat, has answered a few critics, and appears increasingly assured in a team under new leadership. A seam attack of high potential was made to toil for the first time, really, on the series’ penultimate day, and did not necessarily respond particularly well. If the change of tack that dislodged both Babar Azam and Saud Shakeel displayed why there is understandable excitement around what they can do, the periods that came both before and after underlined a revealing rawness. Firm, fast pitches on the Highveld will provide new challenges and opportunities for Ollie Robinson, Jofra Archer, Josh Tongue and Gus Atkinson.

Who goes with them as back-up may be instructive as to the seam pecking order. A six-for in this County Championship round for Olly Stone were welcome not just for Nottinghamshire’s title defence but England, too, with another bowler of high pace and skill looking in fine fettle; Brydon Carse, too, was among the wickets, though matters off the pitch are probably of greater bearing than anything he does on it. Where once there was a dearth of English seamers capable of pushing towards 90mph, it is now land of plenty: Sonny Baker, Henry Crocombe, Mitch Stanley and Eddie Jack could all be tourists.

open image in gallery South Africa are the reigning world champions in Test cricket ( Getty )

The spin stocks, as detailed before, are more limited, though it may be hoped that it again plays a limited role against the World Test Championship winners when they arrive in South Africa. A preceding series with Australia will leave the hosts’ battle-hardened; England will not be able to say the same but confidence has at least been restored after a bruising nine months.

News.title: F1 Spanish GP LIVE: Hamilton escapes sanction ahead of Madrid qualifying
News.content:
Lewis Hamilton crashed in final practice in Madrid ( F1 TV )

F1 heads to its first new circuit in three years as a street circuit in Madrid hosts the Spanish Grand Prix for the first time.

Kimi Antonelli is riding the highest of waves after his sensational victory from 19th on the grid in Monza. The Italian now has a 66-point lead over Mercedes teammate George Russell in second, with a scheduled 10 rounds remaining of the 2026 season.

Lewis Hamilton cut a frustrated figure post-race in Monza after his sixth-place finish and declared himself out of the title race. Nevertheless, he remains in third place, 76 points off Antonelli, and will be eyeing a return to top form this weekend. Max Verstappen completed the Monza podium, as he continues to chase his first victory in 2026.

Madrid’s new street track, the Madring, has 22 corners and an iconic turn 12, christened ‘La Monumental’, with menacing steep banking. It will represent a home race for Carlos Sainz and Fernando Alonso and replaces Barcelona as the host of the Spanish GP on a 10-year deal.

Follow live updates from the Spanish Grand Prix with The Independent

Andy Burnham would be unwise to call an early general election because Reform UK could still become the largest party in parliament, the UK’s leading polling expert has said.

Nigel Farage’s party has slumped in the polls in recent months and is battling a series of scandals as well as a police investigation over donations.

However, on Friday, it revealed it had secured a record staggering £36m donation from British cryptocurrency entrepreneur Ben Delo in a major boost for its election campaign.

And it could still beat Labour, whose popularity has surged ahead since Mr Burnham became prime minister, to take more seats in the House of Commons, Sir John Curtice said.

A YouGov poll carried out earlier this week shows a tight race between the three largest parties, with Reform UK and Labour both on 23 per cent of the vote and the Conservatives close behind on 20 per cent.

However, Reform – which had a nine point lead over Labour a year ago – has slumped considerably in recent months, and last month was overtaken by Labour for the first time since March 2025.

open image in gallery An early election would be a ‘bad deal’ for Andy Burnham ( Reuters )

“The numbers are not there” for Mr Burnham to opt for an early election in the hopes of securing another term as prime minister and catching out Reform before they can recover from a summer of woes, Sir John warned in an interview with The Independent.

“At the moment, the polls are saying that the Labour Party would lose its majority and that indeed one of the two post-Burnham bounce mega-poll MRPs (Multilevel Regression and Post-stratification) actually has Reform with more seats than Labour,” he said.

“One of the things you have to remember is this – and this is something that people have not picked up – the decline in Labour support since 2024, according to more than one mega-poll I’ve looked at, has occurred disproportionately in seats that Labour won in 2024.

“If you look at the pattern of the decline in Labour support in the local elections, it was heaviest in places where they were previously strongest.

“That, of course, is what happened to the Conservative Party in 2024 and why they ended up with only (about) 120 seats” (down from 365 in 2019).

“It’s that pattern that makes it possible for Reform, even if they’re not terribly far ahead of Labour, to still do perfectly well in terms of seats.”

They could be the largest party, he added, because their vote is “geographically evenly spread”, which was a “big disadvantage in 2024 when they were coming third, but is not necessarily a disadvantage if they are coming first, even if only narrowly first”.

open image in gallery Reform UK could be the biggest party in Parliament, Curtice said ( Getty )

“So the numbers are not there and you’re going to sacrifice an awful lot of your MPs.” He also warned that Labour MPs had embraced Mr Burnham as their new leader this summer “in the belief that he would succeed in enabling them to continue their parliamentary careers”.

He added that, even becoming PM this late in the parliament, Mr Burnham has still “got three years”.

“He’s been dying to do it for years. Holding an election now means risking three years to gain two. It’s a bad deal.”

A Reform spokesperson said: “Sir John Curtice is right about one thing. Labour is terrified.

“We’d be delighted if Andy Burnham called an election. But he won’t because he knows Reform would win.”

Bulgarian authorities have launched investigations into an explosion at a weapons storage site in central Bulgaria overnight that came in the wake of another blaze at a munitions depot in recent weeks.

Interior Minister Ivan Dermendzhiev on Saturday told reporters that no one was injured in the blaze near the village of Tsareva Livada and that the fire was under control, with investigations ongoing.

He also indicated that the incident might be linked to a previous fire at another facility of the EMCO company in August.

“There is a neglect of the conditions under which explosives and ammunition are stored,” Demerdzhiev said, putting blame on the management.

“There is also neglect of the method of security — we have one incident, we have a second. This activity is a serious enough source of danger not to neglect measures in any way,” he said.

Demerdzhiev who is part of the center-left government of former president Rumen Radev, which has been hesitant to provide military aid to Ukraine, did not comment on suggestions made by opposition parties that the fires could be linked to sabotage actions by Moscow against plants supplying arms to Ukraine.

In the past decade, there have been several explosions at arms factories of the EMCO company, which has been supplying arms to Ukraine.

In 2015, EMCO owner Emilian Gebrev survived an assassination attempt against him, for which charges have been lodged against three Russian nationals suspected to be Russian military intelligence operatives.
