Oasis star Noel Gallagher remarked that The Smiths musician Johnny Marr has "always been a bit gung-ho" with his instruments as the pair browsed Marr's collection currently on display in London.

Marr, 62, is auctioning off a large portion of the guitars that featured across his award-winning career. Having risen to fame in the 1980s with rock band The Smiths, he subsequently joined The The, formed his own group, and built a successful solo career.

The sale forms part of “Marr’s Guitars: The Johnny Marr Collection”, set to take place at Christie’s in London on September 17. The event includes 111 lots with valuations reaching up to £150,000.

In a video released by Christie’s on Saturday, Gallagher joined the fellow musician to look over the items going under the hammer while sharing memories attached to the instruments.

The two Manchester-born artists inspected a 1982 black Rickenbacker 330 Semi-Hollow Electric Guitar, which Marr originally used to compose hit singles “This Charming Man” and “What Difference Does It Make”.

"You’ve always been a bit gung-ho with your guitars," Gallagher remarked, recalling how he borrowed the instrument for the sleeve of Oasis's 1994 debut single Supersonic.

Gallagher added: "I remember the day when Oasis was recording Definitely Maybe for the first time and you sent down some guitars, because we had one guitar each!

"Someone took it out and just put it on the floor so it would look like we were a working band. It’s on the cover of Supersonic.

open image in gallery A selection of guitars on display during the preview at Christie's in central London ( PA )

"I remember looking at it on the floor going, ‘that can not be The Smiths’ guitar, there’s no way he’s sent that down here to a load of geezers from Longsight!’

"I was like ‘you better take that back, mate!’ – what if someone stands on it!"

Expected to bring up to £80,000, the instrument will go under the hammer alongside a red Gibson ES-355TDSV electric guitar estimated between £100,000 and £150,000.

That guitar was originally purchased for Marr by Sire Records founder Seymour Stein to persuade The Smiths to sign to his label. Inspecting it, Marr noted: "So many people associate me over the years with the (Rickenbacker)."

Marr suggested that most people connect Gallagher with a red Gibson, to which Gallagher answered: "I got mine because of seeing you on Top of the Pops! Those, to me, are the best guitars ever made."

open image in gallery The sale presents approximately 80 guitars, alongside amps and equipment that have been integral to Marr's extraordinarily wide-ranging career ( PA )

Additional lots include a 1971 D-28 acoustic guitar, estimated at up to £50,000, and Marr’s composite solid-body Fender Stratocaster electric guitar, expected to fetch between £40,000 and £60,000.

Roughly 80 guitars will be auctioned, with Marr donating 100 per cent of the hammer price from 31 lots to benefit The Guide Dogs for the Blind Association and The National Autistic Society.

The sale also features amplifiers, gold and silver records from Marr’s long career, a collection of harmonicas, alongside posters and memorabilia from The Smiths.

A U.S. tourist claims she was attacked by a shark while vacationing in the Caribbean, and blames a sailing instructor at her resort for the “permanent nerve damage” and “massive scarring” that resulted, according to a federal lawsuit reviewed by The Independent.

After the animal bit down on Yvonne Martin’s upper thigh, the Columbia, Maryland, resident broke free and returned to the beach at Club Med Turkoise, the all-inclusive property in the Turks and Caicos Islands where she was staying, her complaint states.

Once there, another guest, not Club Med personnel, attended to Martin’s bleeding leg, the complaint goes on. It says the resort’s nurse took her credit card information but “was unable to provide adequate assistance,” after which an ambulance summoned by staffers took another hour to arrive.

Martin’s hospital stay was cut short due to issues with Club Med’s liability coverage, even though she was “in trauma” and required additional care, the complaint contends. She was transported back to Club Med and, the complaint continues, “instructed… to remain in her room while insurance issues were addressed.”

“When a shark bite occurs, there is only a window of 6 to 8 hours to be treated and stitched due to dangers of infection,” the complaint states.

open image in gallery FILE PHOTO: A Maryland woman is suing Club Med in the Caribbean after an alleged shark attack put her in the hospital ( Hans Lucas/AFP via Getty Images )

However, it alleges, “Club Med and the hospital which treated Ms. Martin missed that window.” Martin, who was traveling alone, was confined to her room for the next two days, untreated, leading to a “worsening infection that required emergency medical care in Miami, Florida.”

As a result, Martin was forced to undergo “invasive surgery, extensive physical therapy, and lengthy hospitalization,” according to the complaint.

It says she has since endured, among other things, “mental anguish, humiliation… permanent nerve damage, massive scarring, and [loss of] enjoyment of life.”

Attorney Jim Tate, who is representing Martin, said his client “had quite an ordeal.”

“She was at the Turks and Caicos Club Med alone for her holiday and after her injury was totally at the mercy of Club Med,” Tate told The Independent. “It seems that rather than make sure that Ms. Martin received proper care, Club Med concentrated on finding insurance.”

Tate described Martin as “an attractive senior,” and said that the shark bite has “permanently marred her swimsuit appearance.”

A Club Med spokesperson did not respond to a request for comment.

open image in gallery Club Med guest Yvonne Martin says in her lawsuit that she was told by a sailing instructor to swim 75 feet back to shore, during which time she claims she was bitten by a shark ( Getty Images )

On October 15, 2024, Martin was enjoying a stay at Club Med Turkoise, overlooking the crystal-blue waters of Grace Bay on Providenciales, the northwesternmost island in the Turks and Caicos archipelago, according to her complaint, which was filed September 9 in Maryland federal court.

“Unlike family-oriented properties, Club Med Turkoise is an adults-only haven catering to singles, couples and groups of friends ages 18 and up,” the resort’s website tells prospective guests. “This exclusivity creates a social, carefree vibe — perfect for those seeking sophistication paired with fun.”

Martin had signed up for a sailing lesson, which the complaint says was “organized and operated by Club Med resort personnel.” When she got down to the beach, Martin signed in with the sailing staff at their designated spot next to Sharkey’s, an open-air grill and beach bar for Club Med guests, according to the complaint.

It says Martin was assigned to her own Hobie Cat, a small catamaran, which she sailed alone, without incident, under the supervision of a Club Med instructor. But bad weather was approaching, and the instructor told Martin to head back in, the complaint states.

“Under normal protocol, guests returning from a sailing session are assisted back to shore by the Club Med sailing team, who retrieve the boats at the end of the sessions, take control of the vessels upon their return and [sail them up onto] the beach,” it explains. “At no time are guests required to leave the boat prior to reaching the shore.”

This time, because of the impending weather conditions, the routine was a bit different, according to the complaint.

“Ms. Martin was approximately 75 feet from the shore when a member of the Club Med sailing team shouted instructions at her from another boat ordering her to jump off the boat into open water rather than guiding the vessel and Ms. Martin safely back to shore in the customary manner,” the complaint says. “... Club Med resort employees took no safety precautions to ensure that the 75 feet of water which Ms. Martin was required to swim through was safe and free from dangerous sea predators, especially sharks.”

open image in gallery Shark attacks in the Turks and Caicos archipelago are rare, but they do happen. Club Med guest Yvonne Martin is suing the resort chain over a shark bite she says she got during an October 2024 stay ( AFP via Getty Images )

Shortly after diving in, Martin was attacked, the complaint alleges. Yet, it argues, there were no “urgent” weather conditions that day that required Martin to disembark so far from land.

“Ms. Martin did not assume the risk of a shark bite because she was aboard a boat and did not intend to enter open water,” the complaint states. “It was only after being ordered to jump off the Hobie Cat… by Club Med resort employees that she entered the open water.”

Shark attacks in the Turks and Caicos are extremely rare, researchers say. However, they do happen.

Last year, a 55-year-old Canadian tourist had both of her hands bitten off when she tried to take a selfie with a 6-foot bull shark off Providenciales, according to local authorities. The woman’s husband jumped into the hip-deep water and wrestled the shark off of her – reportedly preventing it from attacking a second time – while his wife managed to get herself to dry land, where she collapsed before being rushed to the hospital.

In 2023, a 22-year-old Connecticut woman snorkeling in Grace Bay had her foot bitten off by a Caribbean reef shark. A boat captain retrieved the woman’s foot, but doctors in Miami were unable to reattach it, according to reports.

A year later, professional kiteboarder Lucas Arsenault lost his right leg to a tiger shark that attacked him about a mile off the northern coast of Providenciales, while he snorkeled with friends and family. He later said he could hear his own bones shattering as the shark bit down, and conceded that he “shouldn’t have survived that.”

Martin is now seeking damages to be determined by a jury, of no less than $500,000, plus lawyers’ fees and court costs.

Manchester United supporters’ group have revealed how they will protest during Sunday’s Manchester derby.

The Red Army said there will be no flag display ahead of the game as part of a protest which follows the club’s investigation into ticket touting.

United revealed they had banned 685 season tickets following a contentious probe which had been condemned by many, with protests already planned for Sunday afternoon.

The Red Army said they will make their own views known by removing their regular flag display in the Stretford End and replacing it with a single banner above the players’ tunnel. It will read: “The way you treat us is a disgrace.”

In a statement, the group said: “This isn’t a ‘TRA’ message, it’s a message on behalf of every genuine fan group, match-going supporter, supporters’ club and fan representative who has either contacted us directly or been negatively impacted by the recent behaviour of the club.

“It’s an honest, heartfelt cry for recognition from the maligned, vilified, and misrepresented beating heart of our football club – the generational match-going supporters.

“Neither is this solely a ‘Manchester United’ problem, this is a league-wide crisis that should be addressed at every club, regardless of rivalries and history. Without drastic changes, there will be no rivalries in the future vision for football shared by the decision makers.”

open image in gallery Michael Carrick’s reign began with a derby victory over Manchester City (Martin Rickett/PA) ( PA Wire )

In the statement, the Red Army called for match-going supporters to be prioritised in the club’s fan engagement process.

On Thursday, United released an update on their investigation into touting, revealing that 685 accounts have been subject to a ban while 464 supporters received a reduced sanction or final warning.

The club said the investigation had identified 1,617 accounts that required further review due to “unusual activity”. Of those stripped of season tickets, 113 failed to respond to requests for further information, 73 did not appeal and 499 received bans upheld by an independent appeals panel.

A club statement read: “Bans were issued where there was significant misuse of the ticketing system for financial gain.

“This included the operation of organised ticketing networks, which were controlling, selling and distributing tickets from hundreds of accounts.”

The 1958 supporters’ group responded by calling for fans to “stand united” against the “season ticket ban fiasco” in a protest ahead of the derby, saying a “line has been crossed”.

Fans have been asked to gather outside the Bishop Blaize pub near Old Trafford at 3pm.

News.title: Root relief as England survive scare to clean sweep Pakistan
News.content:
When Joe Root came to the crease in the first over of the day, his England side were teetering horribly, the problems of the third evening bleeding into the fourth morning. But a welcome, if streaky, unbeaten half-century ensured they wrapped up a 3-0 win in his first series back in charge.

The scorecard will record this as a routine England eight-wicket victory and, for the most part, it was. Thanks to a stand of 130 between Root and the superb Jordan Cox, England chased their target so quickly that the few thousand who came down to Edgbaston were refunded 50 per cent of their ticket because only 24.2 overs were required.

But in the final session of day three and the opening minutes of day four, there was a genuine tension in the air, the sort that comes with tailenders thrashing sixes and a low target. The protagonist was Razaullah, a 20-year-old who spent the first two Tests of this series in Mardan, in the mountains of the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa region near Pakistan’s border with Afghanistan. But having been summoned as part of an overhaul of the squad, he rattled England, first with pace and then clean ball-striking, and made a match that had seemed un-losable very shaky indeed. When Cox hit the winning runs, a scrambled single into the offside, Root’s relief was palpable. It is England’s first series win since 2024.

Razaullah’s partner in a stand of 121 that took Pakistan from two behind to an awkward target of 130 was Mohammad Abbas. On the fourth morning, he ensured England’s start was nightmarish. Abbas, Razaullah’s wisened batting partner on the third evening, was back in his comfort zone: clutching a new Dukes ball under slate-grey skies. He started around the wicket to Ben Duckett, and was immediately on the money. The ball was angled in, demanding that it was played, then nipped slightly away, taking the edge. Duckett’s trudge off was glacial, with his curious Test summer over. He has scored England’s only century of the season, but failed to make fifty otherwise. In this series, he has averaged just eight.

Abbas stayed around the wicket for Emilio Gay, who was pinned plumb in front, fourth ball, the last of the opening over. Not for the first time in his short career, Gay swished his bat over the stumps in frustration, but still reviewed, to no avail. Abbas had given Pakistan the sort of start Ollie Robinson has made commonplace for the England this summer. England were two for two, and a thin crowd was on edge.

News.title: Hamilton smashes into barriers and argues with Ferrari team at ‘car killer’ track
News.content:
The incident immediately brought out red flags at the Madring, F1’s newest circuit, which has garnered headlines this week for being “mental” and “crazy”.

Hamilton locked up at Turn 22, going straight on at the right-hander and shunting into the barriers. After engaging reverse, Hamilton attempted to return the car to the pits, much to his race engineer Carlo Santi’s consternation.

“We have the wing under the wheels,” Santi told him. “Stop in the safest place possible.”

Hamilton replied: “If I can make it back I will. If I can’t, I’ll do it safely.”

Santi continued: “We have a puncture in the front right, stop the car.”

Hamilton again ignored the request, saying: “I can see that.”

Santi tried a third time: “Stop the car in the safest point you can find. It’s the race director asking.”

Hamilton insisted one final time: “I can make it back safely!”

But Santi would not let him. “It’s a formal request,” he said.

News.title: Razaullah’s incredible hitting scrambles England’s minds
News.content:
England will look to complete the series whitewash as they hold a commanding position coming into day three of the third and final Test against Pakistan at Edgbaston in what could be the final day of the English Test summer.

England finished up their first innings on 453 on day two, with a mammoth 320-run lead over Pakistan. Five England batsmen passed the fifty mark; Emilio Gay, Harry Brook, Dan Lawrence, Jamie Smith and Ollie Robinson, but none went on to convert those half centuries into hundreds. It means that Ben Duckett’s century against New Zealand at Trent Bridge back in June will be the only England Test hundred of the summer, the first time that has happened in a six-Test summer. England managed 21 half centuries over the course of the summer, so it works out as 4.76% conversion rate.

Having seen England pile on the runs, Pakistan then lost a wicket with the first ball of their second innings, with Saim Ayub making a pair to sum up a miserable return to their Test side for the opener having been jettisoned in as part of wholesale changes for the visitors. Abdullah Shafique followed three balls later, with Robinson taking both wickets as his fine summer continued. Robinson now has 28 wickets across four Tests this summer at a staggering average of 7.75. Joe Root made history yesterday, taking his 220th catch, the most by an outfielder in Test history. Rain though prevented England the opportunity of potentially wrapping up a two-day finish in a Test in this country for the first time since 2000.

Pakistan will resume on 52/2, still 268 runs behind England, with Azan Awais resuming on 29 not out and will be joined by Shan Masood, who is on 21. Pakistan are yet to reach 200 or bat more than 51 overs in this series so the series whitewash may not be a million miles away. Will we see any rare Pakistan resistance in this series or will England’s seamers dominate again? Play on day three from Edgbaston is set to get under at 11am and it could be the final day of not just the series but the English Test summer.

News.title: Interest rates predicted to rise four times by July
News.content:
Thanks for joining me. Britain’s economy grew unexpectedly in July, handing Chancellor John Healey some breathing space ahead of the Budget.

The UK’s gross domestic product (GDP) expanded by 0.4pc during the month, according to the Office for National Statistics (ONS). Analysts had expected the UK economy to flatline.

Officials said pubs and clubs, advertisers and alcohol makers reported an increase in turnover linked to the World Cup, while many firms also said the second hottest July on record had a positive impact.

The data showed Britain’s economy may be benefitting from the massive investments in AI, with activity in telecoms expanding by 1.1pc in July, computer programming up 3.5pc and information services up 1.1pc.

The data will lend support to the “optimistic story” that John Healey tried to tell about the economy in a major speech this week.

Growth also accelerated from 0.3pc in June after Andy Burnham took over as Prime Minister in July.

It slightly eases pressure on the Chancellor after the cost of government borrowing costs rose to levels not seen in decades after a jump in the price of oil reignited a bond market sell-off.

The Treasury’s 10-year interest rate rose above 5.3pc on Thursday, a level not seen since 2007. It threatens to wipe around £10bn from Mr Healey’s fiscal headroom before his first Budget next month, according to economists at the Item Club. Here is what you need to know.

5 things to start your day

1) Badenoch must scrap triple lock, says senior Tory MP | Politician urges Conservatives to ‘slaughter some sacred cows’ to stabilise the public finances

2) | Michael O’Leary demands sacking of ‘incompetent’ air traffic control chief | Ryanair boss urges Transport Secretary to dismiss Martin Rolfe after IT meltdown grounds passengers

3) | Guardian staff threaten walkout over pay as paper hails record revenues | Journalists’ union will ballot members over strike in protest against company’s offer

4) | Hotel bosses criticise Burnham’s fresh assault on hospitality | Prime Minister gives mayors power for unlimited levy on stays in blow for pubs and families

5) | Iceland to become first British supermarket to open in Falklands | New shop will begin trading before Christmas despite rising tensions with Argentina over islands

What happened overnight

Oil prices remained at their highest level since May as tensions flared in the Middle East.

Brent crude was above $105 a barrel after after Iran-backed Houthis seized control of Yemen’s keyport of Mocha, threatening Saudi oil exports in the Red Sea.

Asian shares declined, tracking Wall Street losses. Japan’s Nikkei 225 dropped 2.8pc to 63,442.30, while South Korea’s Kospi lost 2.3pc to 6,872.39.

Hong Kong’s Hang Seng dipped 0.8pc to 24,753.54. The Shanghai Composite index was down 1.8pc to 3,862.73.

Australia’s S&P/ASX 200 fell 1.2pc to 8,712.20.

Taiwan’s Taiex lost 1.7pc, while India’s Sensex declined 1pc.

On Thursday, Wall Street’s benchmark S&P 500 dropped 0.6pc in its fourth straight loss. The Dow Jones Industrial Average lost 0.6pc, and the technology-heavy Nasdaq composite fell 0.7pc.

News.title: Mainoo looks primed for battle with Man City’s new-look midfield
News.content:
This was Manchester United’s first foray back into the Champions League for 1,003 days, but even with hazy memories of the competition, they know full well they are unlikely to have it this easy again in Europe this season.

After an unconvincing beginning to their Premier League campaign and with Manchester City the visitors to Old Trafford on Sunday, Michael Carrick will have been grateful for a gentle start to life back among Europe’s elite.

Little-known Sabah of Azerbaijan have quite the story to tell, but the closest they got to making this an awkward evening for United came in the first half when, already trailing 1-0, Joy-Lance Mickels miscued an inviting header from close range. Otherwise, it was one-way traffic.

United’s biggest threat on the night was complacency, but there was none of that. This was a professional, unfussy display with a few nice flourishes. Kobbie Mainoo impressed again in central midfield and Carrick was able to substitute a number of his best players early with the derby in mind, as well as resting Luke Shaw entirely.

Goals from Matheus Cunha, Bruno Fernandes and Benjamin Sesko in the first half killed the game as a contest before Lisandro Martínez scored a fourth with just over 20 minutes remaining.

News.title: ‘All I see are dead bodies’: The survivors of Syria’s chemical massacres
News.content:
“Unfortunately, I am still alive,” says Mohammed Suliaiman Abo Alkair, his green eyes heavy and distant.

The 38-year-old steps from his living room onto the roof and gestures towards a cluster of trees – a lone patch of green in a sea of grey rubble. It was there, at two in the morning 13 years ago that the whistle of a rocket ended not in an explosion but a thud.

For a moment, there was relief; the feeling of being spared. But then came a cloud of the nerve agent sarin.

Almost everyone around Mohammed died. His family and one small boy in a neighbouring house were the only ones to survive.

That August night, as Damascus slept, forces loyal to the Syrian President Bashar al-Assad launched eight sarin-filled rockets at the opposition-held districts of Zamalka, Ein Tarma and Jobar. The US government estimated that 1,429 people were killed, including 426 children. Other estimates put the number at 1729.

For more than a decade, nobody was held to account. Mr Assad denied the attack, shielded those responsible and later used sarin again – at Khan Sheikhoun in 2017, and in at least ten further attacks documented by the Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons.

Only after Mr Assad fled Syria in December 2024 did the prospect of justice emerge. Investigators for Syria’s new government have since uncovered previously undeclared chemical-munitions caches, and the authorities have detained 18 suspects. None has yet been tried or punished.

But as attention turns at last to justice, the survivors remain invisible, absent from the reckoning. For now at least they remain largely invisible.

News.title: What an AI Armageddon might actually look like
News.content:
Jacob Coxon has left AI developer Anthropic with a public reckoning. For three years, the 27-year-old Brit trained models at OpenAI and Anthropic.

Both AI startups acted irresponsibly, Coxon wrote on X on Wednesday. “The people building AI earnestly believe that it could kill us all by the end of the decade,” Jacob Coxon warned.

The response from his manager arrived just hours later. Evan Hubinger, Head of Alignment Research at Anthropic, also confirmed the warning: “We are, in fact, earnestly convinced that AI could kill all humans! I think the probability of that happening within the next decade is greater than ten percent.”

Anthropic, he added, does not yet have a solution to this problem.

When the head of safety at a multibillion-dollar technology company casually predicts humanity’s downfall at the hands of his own product, the debate leaves the realm of academic thought experiments.

The warning comes from the engineers writing the code. Both developers point to an industry dynamic in which competitive pressures outweigh safety concerns.

But what exactly are AI developers afraid of? What is the hypothetical scenario in which artificial intelligence brings about Armageddon?

Sports.title: Premier League star flipped £60k Land Rover on way to training just DAYS after club was warned over reckless driving
Sports.content:
HORROR SMASH Premier League star flipped £60k Land Rover on way to training just DAYS after club was warned over reckless driving

HULL City were warned about reckless driving on a road outside the Premier League club’s training ground days before a player flipped his £60,000 Land Rover, it is claimed.

£10.5million summer signing Sorba Thomas, 27, remarkably escaped the scene “completely unscathed” following the horror crash yesterday morning.



Local councillor Phil Redshaw, who visited the scene on Millhouse Woods Lane, said there have been “a few near misses” of late on the residential road – a stone’s throw from the club’s Cottingham training ground.

He told The Mirror: “I wrote to the Hull City club secretary on Sunday asking them to remind players to be careful driving down the road because of the residents’ concerns.



“I wanted them to remind their staff to drive with extra care, because they get new players in every season.“

Cllr Redshaw said gardens back directly onto the pavement where “lorries have no option but to go” in order to get past.

Shocking pictures show the overturned Land Rover Defender, complete with a personalised number plate, in the middle of the road.

Fans feared the worst for the Welsh international winger when the images emerged.

Witnesses described seeing the former Stoke City player’s car skidding on its roof after a reportedly high-speed crash.

However, Hull was quick to confirm the deadline day signing had somehow suffered no injuries in the incident, just hours before the team face Chelsea at Stamford Bridge today.



The Tigers said in a statement: “Hull City is relieved to confirm that Sorba Thomas is unharmed following a road traffic accident near to the club’s Cottingham training ground.

“The club is aware of images of Sorba’s car circulating on social media and can reassure supporters that he has sustained no injuries and emerged from his vehicle completely unscathed.”

Hull boss Sergej Jakirovic must decide whether Thomas will travel with the squad to London.

The Tigers, still yet to concede, put their unbeaten record on the line against the free-scoring Blues.

While a Humberside Police spokesman told The Sun: “Officers and emergency services are currently in attendance following reports of a road traffic collision on Millhouse Woods Lane, Cottingham.



“The road remains closed and motorists are advised to avoid the area to allow emergency services to operate effectively.”

Ex-West Ham trainee Thomas, capped 27 times by Wales, only secured his shot at the Prem this month.

He made his name in non-league at Boreham Wood after being released by the Hammers before Huddersfield gave him a chance in the EFL.

Following loan stints at Blackburn and French side Nantes, he moved to Stoke City in 2025 and shone in the Championship last term, ultimately earning a move to Hull.

He made his Premier League debut off the bench in last week’s goalless draw with Aston Villa.



The Sun has contacted Hull City for further comment.

Sports.title: When will Villa Park’s North Stand be re-opened?
Sports.content:
ASTON VILLA’S North Stand at Villa Park is undergoing a major refurbishment at the moment.

The iconic stadium will look a lot different when the construction works finish next year.



The old North Stand was first opened in 1977, replacing the Witton End terrace.

SunSport has all of the information on the construction works at Villa Park.



When will Villa Park’s North Stand be re-opened?

The stand will be closed for the entirety of the 2026/27 season, but the club have said that the construction will be completed in time for the beginning of the 2027/28 campaign.

In an announcement in April, Aston Villa revealed they had accelerated plans for the stand to be completed by this time, which also involved “significant cost savings.”



Unfortunately for Villa fans, the work was not able to be completed in the off-season due to the mammoth task at hand.

Season ticket holders in the North Stand have been given the option of moving somewhere else in Villa Park for this season, with priority access to switch back to the new section of the ground next summer.

Aston Villa’s President of Business Operations, Francesco Calvo, said: “Temporarily reducing Villa Park’s capacity is not a decision we take lightly.

“However, it is the right decision and one that we have made with our supporters and the long-term future of the Club at the heart of our thinking.



“By completing the redevelopment in one season, we reduce disruption, improve the Villa Park experience more quickly and ensure we are investing responsibly while remaining compliant with financial regulations.”

Sports.title: Derby vs Birmingham suspended as Henrik Meister goes down with nobody near him and medics rush on
Sports.content:
STAR WORRY Derby vs Birmingham suspended as Henrik Meister goes down with nobody near him and medics rush on

DERBY striker Henrik Meister was stretchered off after going down off the ball during today’s lunchtime clash with Birmingham.

Meister, a recent loan signing from Pisa, was treated for around seven minutes after falling to the turf early in the second half.



Meister had been involved in a clash of heads moments earlier during the early exchanges of the second half.

There was silence around Pride Park as the 22-year-old Dane was attended to by medical staff before being carried off down the tunnel.



Meister was making his first home start for John Eustace’s side after being handed his debut in a 3-0 Championship defeat at West Ham last weekend.

He was given a standing ovation by both sets of fans.

The score was level at 1-1 at the time of Meister’s withdrawal.

Bobby Clark had fired the Rams in front on 40 minutes.

But Blues levelled via Carlos Vicente barely two minutes later.

Birmingham boss Chris Davies turned to Paik Seung-ho on the hour mark, replacing Jhon Solis.



And it proved to be an inspired decision, with Paik giving his side the lead just four minutes later.

Birmingham went into the weekend looking to climb up towards the play-off places, while Derby were hoping to avoid falling into the bottom three.

Sports.title: European finalists demand stadium reopened ‘immediately’ and threaten legal action after it was shut amid safety fears
Sports.content:
RAYO VALLECANO have demanded that their stadium be reopened immediately having been BANNED from playing there in July.

And the LaLiga side and last season’s Conference League finalists have even threatened to take legal action if they do not get their wish.



Rayo’s Vallecas ground was shut just weeks before the new season over safety concerns.

An audit commissioned by local government chiefs found a risk of Legionnaires’ disease – a lung condition caused by bacteria in water – from the stadium.



It also pointed to fire hazards from debris at the ground in addition to electrical issues.

As such, the Madrid-based club have been forced to play their first two home matches of the season at Butarque, the home of Leganes.



Following safety work done on Vallecas, Rayo are demanding that they be allowed to return to their traditional home.

In a club statement, the Spanish side claim that an audit guaranteeing the safety and hygiene of the ground was received by the Regional Ministry of Culture, Tourism, and Sport yesterday.

Rayo chiefs believe that they should be allowed to play Tuesday’s scheduled home fixture against Espanyol at Vallecas, rather than Butarque.

In an apparent dig at how quickly they were banned from their ground in July, Rayo’s statement added: “In these communications, the Regional Minister stated that procedures must be respected, procedures that the Club is unaware of beyond having read and confirmed the conclusion of the independent report prepared by CEIDAL.

Sports.title: Southampton hitman Cyle Larin reveals high-tech home gym and recovery den behind red-hot goalscoring form
Sports.content:
CYLE LARIN takes working from home to an absolute extreme.

While most people sit at the kitchen table with a mug of tea, the Southampton hitman has decked out his house with a high-tech man cave built purely for elite performance.



Larin’s ultimate home den features a state-of-the-art gym setup, heavy weights, recovery pumps and even his own personal massage table.

And the Canadian striker‘s private retreat is paying massive dividends after firing him to a red-hot goalscoring run — landing him the SkyBet Championship player of the month award for August ahead of today’s clash with Bristol City.



Larin, 31, insists the brutal physical grind of the English second tier means extra homework off the pitch is non-negotiable.

He told SunSport: “I use it every day. With so many games, you just need to be physically ready for each match.

“It doesn’t mean doing heavy weightlifting every day. It could be mobility, strength, stretching, or recovery things.

“I have recovery bands, weights, recovery pumps — almost anything a proper gym would have. We even have a recovery massage table in there too.

“Over the years, playing at different clubs with different players, I’ve learned how important that is. The Championship is one of the most physically demanding leagues in the world.”

The striker will keep his newly acquired gong proudly on display in his private setup as a daily reminder of what he can achieve at St Mary’s.

“The first person I told was my wife — she was so thrilled for me.

“I was really happy to receive it because it’s the first one ever, which makes it a bit more special.

Larin credits Saints boss Tonda Eckert as a primary catalyst behind his blistering form and his decision to commit his long-term future to the South Coast after spending the second half of last season on loan from Mallorca.

That bond proved vital during a chaotic summer.

Saints were expelled from the Championship play-off final after being caught spying on Middlesbrough — before being hit with a four-point penalty this season for further spying breaches at Ipswich and Oxford.

Sports.title: Lisandro Martinez brushes off record against Erling Haaland as he hails Man Utd team-mate as ‘the future’
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER UNITED defender Lisandro Martinez has downplayed his record against City striker Erling Haaland ahead of the derby.

Since Haaland plundered a hat-trick on his and Martinez’s derby debuts in October 2022, he has not scored in five derbies when the Argentine has played.



United great Nicky Butt predicted that the 6ft 5in Haaland would “pick Martinez up and run with him” and “treat him like a toddler” before the Old Trafford derby in January.

Butt’s old team-mate and fellow podcaster Paul Scholes laughed that Haaland would “throw him in the net” after scoring.



United won 2-0 and Martinez afterwards dared Butt and Scholes to air their criticism of him at his home.

Haaland has hit five goals in his last three games and United have conceded six in their first three Premier League fixtures.

Martinez admitted their leaky form is “annoying” but was reluctant to overstate his record against Haaland.

Martinez said: “That is the past. It’s gone and now we have to – I have to – be ready for this game because it’s going to be so different from the last one.

“For sure when you win, your confidence is going up. But now we have to be calm, we have to be humble and enjoy [the Sabah win].

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“And then we have to think about the derby that is really important for us.



“Against Everton, we played to take the clean sheet and then we conceded the goals and that’s what annoys us.

“It’s really bad, for sure, because we want to be there and if we want to compete, we have to keep the clean sheet because it’s very important.”

City beat Porto in their Champions League opener on Tuesday night whereas United had to wait until Thursday to see off Sabah.

Although coach Michael Carrick afforded Luke Shaw, Harry Maguire, Diogo Dalot and Marcus Rashford complete rests, City have 48 hours’ extra recovery time.

But Martinez is just grateful to have midweek matches again after a season devoid of European football.



He added: “This is what we want, playing every three days, playing in all the competitions.

“This is what we have wanted for a long time and now we are ready. We have to recover now and this is the standard that we want as a team.”

Martinez also hailed Leny Yoro as “the future” of United after his first start of the campaign against Sabah.



Yoro joined United in a £58.91million deal in July 2024 but the 20-year-old is still behind Maguire in the right-sided centre-back pecking order.

Sports.title: Hamilton crashes as Antonelli tops final practice in Madrid
Sports.content:
Championship leader Kimi Antonelli was fastest in final practice at the Spanish Grand Prix as Lewis Hamilton crashed and lost valuable track time ahead of qualifying in Madrid.

Just 20 minutes into the session, Hamilton was on course to set a very quick lap until he outbraked himself at the last corner and hit the barriers head-on, albeit at a relatively slow speed.

He reversed out of the barriers but the front wing had dislodged itself and got stuck under the front right tyre, so Ferrari urged Hamilton to stop the car.

But the seven-time world champion wanted to limp back to the pit lane so he did not lose crucial running for qualifying later on at 3pm (build-up from 2.15pm), live on Sky Sports F1, before eventually coming to a halt in the middle sector.

Sky Sports F1's Anthony Davidson feels Hamilton was wrong to drive for such a long time with a damaged car.

"Any young driver that is watching this right now, you don't do that. You just don't do that. That's what you could have tried to do [get back to the pits] but that rule is there for a reason," he said.

"If it [the front wing] went under the car completely and jacked your front wheels up and there were marshals on the track... you've got to think of all these scenarios."

Image: Lewis Hamilton tried to limp around with a damaged car until he eventually stopped in the middle sector (PA)

The crash caused a 45-minute red flag as the marshals repaired the barriers, with the clock being stopped with 15 minutes remaining so the drivers could get more laps around the new Madring.

Antonelli, who leads the Drivers' Championship by 66 points over Mercedes team-mate George Russell, emerged on top with a blistering 1:32.797 to beat Ferrari's Charles Leclerc by 0.166s.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ollie Bearman took a huge hit right at the end of final practice at the Spanish Grand Prix

McLaren showed promise with Oscar Piastri in third and Lando Norris in fourth - the latter missed almost all of second practice on Friday.

Red Bull's Max Verstappen was fifth and Russell only sixth but it looks like pole position could be anyone's given the drivers are getting faster with every lap and the track is evolving.

Haas' Oliver Bearman proved how difficult the Madring is with a big crash in the high-speed Turn 11, leaving his team with a race to get his car fixed for qualifying.

Sports.title: Root steers England to series sweep of Pakistan after early scare
Sports.content:
England clinched a first home series whitewash of Pakistan despite an early scare by chasing down 130 on day four of the third Test at Edgbaston.

The thought of England losing the Test match would have been unthinkable when Ollie Robinson reduced the visitors to 0-2 on the second evening - Pakistan still trailing by 320 at the time - but it looked a genuine possibility when the hosts themselves lost two in their first over to start the fourth morning.

Ben Duckett (0) signed off a miserable series by nicking off first ball to Mohammad Abbas (2-27), who added Emilio Gay (0) lbw to finish a stunning opener.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player England's start to day four could not have gone worse after Mohammad Abbas removed Ben Duckett and Emilio Gay in the first over

But any fears of England succumbing to a calamitous defeat were soon dispelled by their skipper as Joe Root (62no) struck a fine fifty, sharing an unbroken 128-run partnership with Jordan Cox (59no), who notched his third half-century late on, to secure victory in 24.2 overs.

Score summary - England vs Pakistan, third Test, Edgbaston Pakistan 133 all out in 33.5 overs in first innings (put in to bat): Saud Shakeel (43), Mohammad Abbas (21); Josh Tongue (4-42), Ollie Robinson (3-15), Jofra Archer (3-25) England 453 all out in 89 overs in first innings: Harry Brook (75), Jamie Smith (69), Dan Lawrence (65), Emilio Gay (60), Ollie Robinson (50); Razaullah (4-148) Pakistan 449 all out in 96.4 overs in second innings: Shan Masood (95), Razaullah (81 off 63 balls), Babar Azam (76), Azan Awais (59); Gus Atkinson (3-109) England 130-2 in 24.2 overs in second innings (win by eight wickets): Joe Root (62no), Jordan Cox (59no); Mohammad Abbas (2-27)

Pakistan, meanwhile, will be left wondering would could have been, had Mohammad Ali not overstepped when bowling Root for 23 - dragging onto his stumps off a no-ball - with England just 35-2 at the time.

Will England stick with Cox for South Africa?

Cox's knock will have aided his hopes of retaining a spot in England's starting XI when the Test team are next in action for the three-match tour of South Africa, starting on December 17.

Image: England's Jordan Cox bats

Jacob Bethell - injured for the Pakistan series - is expected to return to the side, but could he or Cox open the batting instead of Gay?

And were Gay to retain his place at the top of the order, Cox could yet fill in at wicketkeeper instead of Jamie Smith, who didn't keep during Pakistan's second innings due to an injured finger - though he has three months for that to sufficiently heal.

Pakistan were briefly hopeful of successfully defending a total of 130 or less in a Test match for the first time since 1993, when New Zealand were bowled out for 93, chasing 127, at Hamilton.

The last such instance of 130 or less being defended in England was when England set Australia 124 in the 1997 Ashes at The Oval and bowled them out for 104.

Pakistan unearth gem in Razaullah after series of struggles

In what has otherwise been a dismal series for Pakistan, they at least leave having shown some fight in this final Test by taking things into a fourth day and setting a target that briefly troubled England.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player 21-year-old debutant Razaullah picked up the wicket of Joe Root with just his fourth ball in Test cricket!

Also, in 21-year-old Razaullah, they have certainly unearthed a raw gem. The debutant knocked over England's all-time leading run-scorer Root in the first innings with just his fourth ball in Test cricket, on his way to a four-wicket haul, while his exploits with the bat on the third evening will live long in the memory.

When Pakistan's eighth second-innings wicket fell, they still trailed by two runs - England looking set to clinch their series sweep inside three days - before Razaullah proceeded to smash 81 off only 63 balls, clearing the ropes a staggering nine times to equal Tim Southee's record for a debutant.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Razaullah smashed NINE sixes to equal Tim Southee’s record for the most by a player on Test debut during a remarkable innings against England at Edgbaston

Ultimately though, England are well deserving of the 3-0 series scoreline to herald Root's return as Test captain following Ben Stokes' international retirement earlier in the summer.

Butch: A lot of good things about England

Sky Sports Cricket's Mark Butcher:

"They were made to sweat for it at times, which is a good thing.

"It gave England pause for thought at times when it comes to differing conditions in Test matches - particularly with regards to South Africa and the ball not moving laterally as much.

"Perhaps a slight concern about the lack of centuries by the batters, but there was a lot of good things about England this Test match series.

"They weren't given much of a challenge for most of it, which is why yesterday was such a pleasing day as far as the summer is concerned."

Urooj: Major problems for Pakistan cricket

Sky Sports Cricket's Urooj Mumtaz:

"There are problems with Pakistan cricket, major problems. They lost this series, drew in the West Indies, lost to Bangladesh at home, where their record isn't particularly good.

"They have now lost 11 out of 12 away from home and 15 out of the last 20 Test matches. Those are telling figures, as were the size of England's wins.

"Pakistan maybe had just one good day of cricket in the Test series. There are ingredients to work with but a lot needs to be done right for longer periods of time if there is to be a brighter Pakistan future."

Sports.title: Enceladus takes on Christmas Day and Pienne Bonnard in 250th St Leger
Sports.content:
Enceladus takes on Ballydoyle duo Christmas Day and Pierre Bonnard in the latest renewal of the St Leger.

3.35 Doncaster - Enceladus faces Christmas Day and Pierre Bonnard in St Leger

The 250th renewal of the Group 1 Betfred St Leger looks a cracker, with Aidan and Joseph O'Brien set to dominate a field of 11.

Joseph O'Brien took this race with Galileo Chrome in 2020 and looks to have a super chance with Enceladus.

The son of Sea The Stars has progressed with each start, including when winning the King George V at the Royal meeting. He warmed up for a crack at this with a ready success in the Gordon Stakes and may go off the market leader under Billy Loughnane.

Nine-time winner Aidan O'Brien saddles four runners with Derby hero Christmas Day a big player under Ronan Whelan. Any rain would be a positive given his Epsom triumph in wet conditions, and he will be 5lbs better off with stablemate Pierre Bonnard - who finished ahead of him at York.

Great Voltigeur runner-up Pierre Bonnard should be suited by this extra distance after defeat at the hands of Arc hopeful Maltese Cross, while Amelia Earhart is a quirky but talented filly. She looked like showing signs of revival when a runner-up in Group 3 company at Cork, but this is a huge step up from that assignment.

Of the others, Andrew Balding pair Galiyan and Hatteen rate each-way alternatives, with Saffie Osborne picking up the ride on Joseph O'Brien's second string, Highwayman.

1.45 Doncaster - 2000 Guineas favourite Desert Castle bids to go 2-2

The 2000 Guineas favourite Desert Castle is the headline act in a quality edition of the Group 2 Betfred Champagne Stakes.

The Charlie Appleby-trained Frankel colt burst onto the scene with a runaway success at Newmarket last month and he will be all the rage to follow up under Billy Loughnane - who will be eyeing more winners to fend off Oisín Murphy at the summit of the jockeys' championship.

Gentle Hurricane scored on debut before improving to claim second in the Acomb Stakes and granted further progress he can put it up to the favourite. Jason Watson replaces Oisin Murphy in the plate here, with the champion otherwise engaged at Leopardstown.

William Muir has spoken glowingly about Breacher and having landed a Salisbury maiden on his first start, he ran a solid third in Group 3 company. That form entitles him to hit the frame here.

Ballydoyle raider Sergei Diaghilev looks the pick of the remainder, with Rosberg and Silver Dominion also in situ.

2.55 Doncaster - Red-hot favourite More Thunder drops in trip

More Thunder drops back to seven furlongs in a strong-looking Group 2 Betfred Park Stakes at 2.55pm.

The William Haggas-trained five-year-old has been running with credit at the top table all season and this dip back in class and distance should see him hard to beat under Tom Marquand.

Never So Brave landed a first Group 1 victory last season but has failed to fire this season, while the same applies to last year's Middle Park victor Wise Approach.

Image: Never So Brave (centre) takes on More Thunder

Ralph Beckett's 2025 Sussex Stakes winner Qirat ran another fine race in defeat when chasing home Zavateri at Goodwood and cannot be ruled out, while Flora Of Bermuda and Volterra complete the shortlist.

Also on Town Moor...

Berkshire Regal locks horns with Hmas Perth in the opening 1.10pm British Stallion Studs EBF Maiden Stakes, worth £25,770 to the winner. Ed Dunlop won this race last year and will be eyeing further success in it, with Beloved Country his representative.

A typically competitive Betfred Portland (2.20pm) sees Getreadytorumble and Twilight Calls towards the top of the market. The team surrounding the latter have already tasted success at this year's Festival, with Speed Of Sound soaring to success in Thursday's opener.

Bullet Point tops a field of 17 assembled for a strong renewal of the Pertemps Network Handicap, although Moonfall is also likely to attract support for the popular George Boughey and Billy Loughnane combination.

Elsewhere...

The day begins with top-quality action from Australia. Sir Delius (formerly Delius) takes on Sheza Alibi in a classy looking Grade 1 Crown Makybe Diva Stakes.

Back on home soil, Solar Edge and Kylian do battle in Lingfield's feature - the Free Race Replays On attheraces.com Handicap at 4pm.

Woodbine plays host to top-class action in the evening, headlined by Notable Speech taking on Archivist and company in the feature Woodbine Mile at 10.20pm. Just 35 minutes later, Diamond Rain, Sea The Fire and Jancis all hold good chances in the E. P. Taylor Stakes.

Sports.title: 'Let's do this for the USA' - Shelton sets up Zverev showdown in US Open final
Sports.content:
Ben Shelton ‌defeated compatriot Frances Tiafoe in ‌an electric US Open semi-final on Friday to ​secure a title showdown with Alexander Zverev.

On a poignant evening that began with commemorations marking the 25th anniversary of ​the September 11 attacks, Shelton ‌came from a set down to beat Tiafoe 4-6 6-3 6-3 7-5 and move closer ​to ending a 23-year ‌American wait for a men's singles Grand Slam ​champion.

No home male player has won a Grand Slam singles title since Andy Roddick triumphed in Flushing Meadows in 2003. Shelton will now have a chance to claim his maiden Grand Slam crown.

He is the first Black American to reach the US Open Final since Arthur Ashe in 1972



Men's Final: Head-To-Head Zverev Shelton 5 Overall 0 3 On Hard Courts 0 1 In Finals 0 10 Sets Won 1

Earlier, Zverev booked his place in the final with a 6-3 7-6 (9-7) 7-6 (8-6) victory against Karen Khachanov to move a step closer to a ‌second Grand Slam title.

Shelton said: "First, 'Foe' is like a big brother to me. This is where we want to be, at the tail end of this tournament.

"I know what my goal is, what my job is. I'm going for it here. Let's do this for the USA!

"One more thing. It's a difficult day to be out here playing. My thoughts and prayers go to all the families who were impacted by 9/11."

Tiafoe ⁠powered ahead 5-4 ⁠when Shelton produced a double fault, before raising the ‌roof with a hold to bag the first set.

Tiafoe ‌continued to target his opponent's backhand in the second set but serving at 2-1, Shelton thought he had clocked the fastest serve in Grand Slam history with a 158 mph bullet. However, Hawk-Eye and the USTA later confirmed through review that it only hit 144 mph.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ben Shelton thought he hit a 158mph serve at the US Open semi-finals, but in fact it was an impressive 144mph according to Hawk-Eye

With new balls at 3-3, Shelton started with a 125 mph serve - Tiafoe got his racket up almost in self-defence and ended up getting knocked backwards to the court - and followed it with serves clocked at 144, 139 and 140, as he dialled up the intensity to draw ⁠level.

He then broke in the ​fifth game of the third ​set to take a commanding ​lead in the match.

With his booming ⁠left-handed serve and his defence proving impenetrable in the high-octane fourth set, ⁠eighth seed Shelton heaped ​the pressure on late to wrap up an emotional win.

The 23-year-old finished with 47 winners, including 20 aces, to book his place in the title match.

The victory sent him to his second title decider at Flushing Meadows, after finishing runner-up in 2020 to Dominic ​Thiem.

"After the second round at 3am, me and my team were in the dressing room actually laughing at how bad I was playing. ​That sense of humour helped me," Zverev said ⁠on court.

From 'pointless' start to the final

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch the moment Zverev goes around the net with a stunning winner over Khachanov

The German had played all his previous matches during the night sessions, existing in a perpetual loop of darkness and midnight finishes.

The 29-year-old has capitalised on the absence of Jannik Sinner and defeats for Carlos Alcaraz and Novak Djokovic, as well as a kind draw, to reach a third consecutive Grand Slam final.

"I really started off the tournament, and I ​was like, 'Well, this is pointless because I'm not going to do anything here,' and here I am sitting and preparing for a Sunday final," Zverev ​told reporters.

A solitary break was all Zverev needed to pinch a tight first set from his opponent and when he broke again at start of the second, a routine afternoon looked on the cards.

However, a double fault allowed Khachanov back on serve and instead Zverev became embroiled in a tie-break, at one point trailing 5-3 and only winning it after a lung-busting 35-shot rally.

The third set went the same way and Khachanov had set points at 6-4, but two wayward forehands and a Zverev ace gave him match point, which he took at the first attempt.

"I think it's going to be a fantastic ​feeling playing, you know, a final in a sold-out Arthur Ashe ​and not in an empty one," he said. "For me, a loud and energetic crowd is always great, as long as ‌they're fair."

Navratilova: There are no asterisks in Zverev's successes

Image: Zverev is 'cooking' according to Martina Navratilova

Sky Sports Tennis' Martina Navratilova:

"What a year Zverev has had at the majors. It's been outstanding stuff.

"Okay, Sinner lost early at the French Open and Alcaraz didn't play, but there are no asterisks; he still had to get through even as a favourite.

"And that has given the confidence to play better tennis after that. I think he played better at Wimbledon than he did at Roland Garros, and now he started off badly here by his own admission, but he hasn't lost a set the last four matches.

"He's cooking now."

Sports.title: Febrile Manchester derby awaits amid growing rift between United fans and club
Sports.content:
Manchester United’s nine victories from 10 Premier League games at Old Trafford in 2026 cast their stadium as a fortress Manchester City aim to ransack on Sunday, to join Leeds in departing with three points during this calendar year.

Michael Carrick has overseen the division’s highest home points-per-game return in that span: 2.7, ahead of Arsenal’s 2.27 (from 12 matches) and Manchester City’s 2.25 (11); and his side have scored the most goals: 26, to City’s 23, and the champions’ 20.

When Enzo Maresca’s side motor across town, the 199th edition of a local squabble that draws a riveted global audience will be as febrile as ever – on and off the pitch.

A United fan group, the 1958, has called for a “peaceful protest” before kick-off, starting at a pub near the stadium, against what it believes is disproportionate action in the club’s drive to eradicate ticket touting. United said on Friday that 685 accounts had been subject to a ban and 464 supporters had received a reduced sanction or final warning.

Then, when the whistle blows, United will attempt to end City’s perfect start of four victories in all competitions, improve a disappointing return of four points from three league games and repeat the opening result of Carrick’s second interim tenure, achieved in January four days after his appointment: a 2-0 downing of Pep Guardiola’s visitors in which Bryan Mbeumo and Patrick Dorgu were on target.

A 2-1 defeat by Leeds on 13 April is the sole blemish on United’s league record at Old Trafford since. The sequence shows how impressive Carrick’s stewardship has been and last month’s 5-2 hammering of Ipswich came in his first home game as the permanent manager.

View image in fullscreen Bruno Fernandes has been integral to Manchester United’s recent success at Old Trafford. Photograph: Allstar Picture Library Ltd/Richard Sellers/Apl/Sportsphoto

Scan the results of his 10 away league games and you find four wins (at Arsenal, Everton, Chelsea and Brighton), four draws (West Ham, Bournemouth, Sunderland and Everton) and two defeats (Newcastle and Hull): 16 points from 30, compared with 27 from 30 when United play in front of their crowd.

A major factor behind the home record is easy to identify: Bruno Fernandes. In the 10 Old Trafford games the 31-year-old has provided 10 assists and scored five times. Without the captain Carrick’s team would surely struggle, as his hat-trick against Ipswich underlined.

Mbeumo and Matheus Cunha have been key support acts, scoring four goals each (Cunha also has two assists), and Benjamin Sesko has impressed with five goals at an average of one every 70.8 minutes.

United’s rearguard is the achilles heel: 13 goals conceded in the 10 home matches (Arsenal have allowed seven, City nine) is hardly parsimonious, so on Sunday the visitors will hope to prosper by hogging the ball, stymieing the opportunity for fast breaks that Mbeumo, Fernandes, Cunha and Sesko thrive on, and going at pace at the creaky defence.

City did not do this enough in Tuesday’s 2-0 Champions League victory at Porto, perhaps because Elliot Anderson was stood down, and perhaps, too, because Maresca’s nascent team are in the work-in-progress phase.

View image in fullscreen Elliot Anderson has settled quickly at Manchester City after his £116m move from Nottingham Forest. Photograph: Dave Thompson/AP

Anderson has looked a natural schemer since his £116m transfer from Nottingham Forest, running contests. In last Saturday’s 1-0 win over Coventry his display was Rodri-esque: a big call, but no exaggeration as the 23-year-old sprayed passes around, snuffed out danger, demanded to be found when under pressure and showed a spurt of speed to escape traffic.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

United have their own midfield lieutenant: Kobbie Mainoo, who has started nine of the 10 home league games under Carrick, scoring once and assisting once. The match he missed? The Leeds reverse, which is surely no coincidence because the 21-year-old’s ability to mould time and space is priceless in the hurly-burly of the 100mph Premier League – as his masterclass versus Ipswich reiterated.

Harry Maguire calls the lad from Stockport United “midfield monster” so in the showdown between Mainoo and Anderson we may witness the derby’s defining battle – and the future of England’s engine room.

A United victory would send those of the red persuasion home happy, bragging rights secured in the workplace and local hostelries. But an underlying discontent will remain: at the longstanding grievance regarding the Glazers’ ownership that has haemorrhaged resources and saddled the club with a near £1.3bn debt, and at the recent initiative designed to eliminate the black market resale of tickets.

It is a worthy act but the accusation from fans is of a draconian approach. In July United began contacting supporters who used six or more devices to access accounts linked to the club or to forward tickets, on the basis this suggested the potential buying of seats to resell. Those in question were asked why multiple accounts were accessed, to identify the differing devices used, and for photo ID to prove validity.

A joint statement by six fan groups complained “of longstanding supporters who have followed Manchester United for decades, often across multiple generations of the same family, being treated as suspects”.

The dispute continues. On Tuesday the 1958 said: “Supporters are now facing serious sanctions which can remove their right to attend matches. We believe nobody should face such action without being told clearly what they are accused of and being shown the evidence used to justify it. If there is clear, substantive evidence of serious wrongdoing or organised ticket touting, show it. No loyal supporter should be treated as guilty without being given a fair opportunity to understand and challenge the case against them.”

United said that in addition to the sanctions and warnings, they had identified 1,617 accounts that required further review owing to “unusual activity”.

So before the derby will be the latest protest against the latest issue that shows the fracture between proud institution and proud fanbase. Against this backdrop Carrick hopes to extend United’s proud home record – which viewed through the prism of the disconnect between club and supporters is particularly impressive.

Sports.title: All change for Maresca: the data behind Manchester City’s rapid player turnover
Sports.content:
Manchester City have experienced a level of player turnover unthinkable in the Pep Guardiola era. Where Arne Slot benefited in his first Liverpool season by retaining the squad Jürgen Klopp bequeathed, Enzo Maresca must oversee the evolution of City while winning every week. Relying on relatively new players has not cost them Premier League points yet, but there could be reasons for concern before their derby at Old Trafford on Sunday.

Most people assumed City would demolish Coventry. Fantasy Premier League players set a record last weekend for the number who used their one-off option of triple-captaining a player to multiply his points by three. More than 91% used this bonus on Erling Haaland, expecting goals galore. He scored, but that was the only goal of the game. The match was closer than anyone anticipated.

Coventry’s chances were valued at 1.37 xG by Opta, suggesting they deserved to score. The more notable statistic was the visitors having 12 shots. Visitors to the Etihad hit that benchmark 17 times in the Premier League in a decade of Guardiola and none of those that did were newly promoted.

It is inevitable that a team containing many new players are less solid. City’s starting XI against Coventry was full of familiar names; it’s just that several are known for their achievements elsewhere.

Rayan Cherki was the fifth-longest-serving player and he joined the club last summer. Only one of the five men in the key defensive positions of goalkeeper, centre-back or holding midfield was a City player when the 2025-26 season began. It would have been different had Enzo Fernández not needed to start in place of Nico O’Reilly, who was injured in the warm-up, but not by much.

Here is one way we can attempt to quantify turnover within a squad. With 11 men playing 90 minutes for 38 games, a club’s Premier League campaign consists of 37,620 player minutes. There are players who covered 13,998 minutes for City in 2025-26 who have not appeared for them in the league this season, and most of them will not because they have left. This means that 37.2% of the club’s minutes need replacing – this is their turnover rate.

Across Guardiola’s 10 seasons, this figure averaged 14.5% and was no higher than 7.5% four times. Almost everyone who contributed significant playing time in a given season would do so the following season. There was a seven-season period of supreme stability in the middle of Guardiola’s tenure, though the current squad evolution had begun in his final campaign.

Consider who has left since May. Bernardo Silva and Rodri were pivotal to City’s success and played hundreds of matches before leaving. Nico González lasted 18 months, Tijjani Reijnders even less. He came, he saw, he conquered Wolves but very few others and is now in the Saudi Pro League. Omar Marmoush and Sávio (with 50 league starts between them) have been shipped to Tottenham. City’s financial power largely protects them against the cost of transfer failures but their recent recruitment has been flawed in many areas.

In fairness, Marc Guéhi and Antoine Semenyo played only half of 2025-26 for City and quickly established themselves in the first‑choice XI. There is also Jérémy Doku, a key player from last season who has not featured in the league this term. His return from injury will lift the retention rate, though it will not bring City up to the Premier League average (31.9%).

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The only teams experiencing more turnover by this measure are Aston Villa, Tottenham, Newcastle and Brighton. They are also the only clubs who can match (or top) City for having five players who logged at least 1,500 league minutes last season but have not featured in 2026-27.

Those clubs, unlike City, are not expected to challenge for the league title or Champions League. Arsenal have kept a more settled squad, which should help them pursue those goals. The far more immediate hurdle for City is the derby with Manchester United, another of the clubs with above-average retention rate. They are fifth in the standings. Marcus Rashford doesn’t count because he spent last season on loan and did not feature in the Premier League.

Maresca may opt to use more of City’s established players for this testing fixture than he did against Coventry. Phil Foden has more goals only against Brighton than he has against United and O’Reilly is fit to return. It is one thing to rotate against a relative minnow, another to take chances in a derby.

Whatever the outcome at Old Trafford, the man charged with the impossible task of following Guardiola has to tackle the challenge with a squad that has undergone greater turnover than any his predecessor handled.

Sports.title: Football lends voice to message worth relaying: men should talk about their pain | Barney Ronay
Sports.content:
If you watched US television adverts during the World Cup for any length of time one thing just kept leaping out. I’ve mentioned this before here, but it still seems both jarring and significant. Every third or fourth rotation in that endless daytime scroll, in between the Chicken Megadeth Hyper-Box Family Meal Deal, either side of David Beckham expertly consuming a light beer, is an advert for antidepressants.

The format for these is always the same kind of thing: contented, wholesome people throwing frisbees, or strolling through a small-town antiques fair, while a warm, honeyed, reassuring voiceover talks about how horrifying their lives are, with the suggestion that only a lengthy course of Smileothorium can solve this.

In another world there would be a call to study this phenomenon, to consider why a nation of such dazzling abundance and opportunity should also feel glazed, worthless and deprived of hope. But this is not that world. More than 50 million Americans have depression. This is demand and supply in action, a battle for market share in a £6bn industry. The US often worries about itself in its post-industrial age. What are we now? What can we still make? Where is the new frontier? Well, human misery is looking pretty hot right now.

The reason for talking about this here is that English football is doing a good thing this week. Between 4-14 September the Premier League is sponsoring the Together Against Suicide campaign. Harry Kane and Prince William have spoken warmly in support. The league is posting words of solidarity on its X account, which is probably not the best way to cheer yourself up if we’re being honest.

This is simple, useful messaging. It applies to people of any age, sex or background. But it applies in particular to men, and to middle-aged men, who are more likely to die by suicide than any other age group. Middle-aged men are more likely to experience depression and anxiety in those years. They can be hard to reach because this often happens out of sight or, most heartbreaking of all, without any indication there was even a problem.

It might be a little blunt in its styling. But what football is doing here is unequivocally good. Nothing else has the same level of reach and cut-through. If one person in the line of that message is touched by it, this seems like a happy outcome.

I think I have locus standi to talk about this. Everyone does. It’s universal. But I’m also unarguably a middle-aged man. I have two sons who are also now men. I have middle-aged male friends, many of whom are, with all due respect, a bit loopy. And like so many other people I’ve been down that road some of the way.

Life in Covid really did it for me. Exhaustion, isolation, the inescapable fact of having to carry on existing. Do you really have to, though? This kind of thing can creep into your mind like a shadow, just another idle thought. Until at some point you realise there’s a shadow in the corner of the room, a ghost in the chair, and it’s talking to you.

The fact is, it’s hard to be a man at any age. Or at least, it’s hard in a way that is distinct from other forms of hardness. And yes this statement might fail to draw an overwhelming wave of sympathy, but this is part of the problem. Pain comes for everyone. There’s no hierarchy of suffering. And male pain, male alienation is often carried around like a dead weight for exactly this reason.

double quotation mark Being able to talk about this stuff is the direct opposite of weakness. There is always someone willing to do this with you

As you get older this can be related to a sense of obsolescence. Men want to do stuff. There’s a kind of programming to feel useful, to serve some kind of function. Frankly, most middle-aged men would be happier if someone just gave them a big piece of wood and told them to saw it in half, then at the end of the day told them they’ve done a really good job, they’re good boys and everyone’s proud of them. Tomorrow you can come back and put it together again.

Instead it can feel like every part of the world is independently conspiring to make you feel like crap. Diminishing work, vanished usefulness, isolation, the way life can exhaust you quietly, without any obvious trauma. Men are not good at processing this. The key method, the strategy we’ve worked out over the years is: don’t process it at all. Carry on. Keep running through the red zone. Lads, it’s not a long-term plan.

I have two pieces of aged wisdom on this front. First, the obvious one. Embrace the feeling and talk about it. Sounds like a cliche. Is actually true. Feeling bad isn’t some deeper, truer version of you. The good stuff also exists and is just as real. Both will pass, and pass again.

Small things do help. Muscular, loud, well‑meaning men on the internet are actually right. Don’t eat rubbish. Get outside. Speak to other people. Remember that the sun also rises, that feeling terrible is also evidence of the ability to feel good. Prince William is right: being able to talk about this stuff is the direct opposite of weakness. There is always someone willing to do this with you, who will like and admire you even more as a result.

The second thing is: you do also have to fight. Those outmoded forms of masculinity – being stoic, resisting your own feelings – tend to get a bad rap. But everyone needs a bit of this. The problem is men are often not taught anything else to go with it.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Sport in Focus Our picture editors select their favourite sporting images from the past week, from the spectacular to the powerful, and with a little bit of fun thrown in Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Life is brutal. It will come for you. It is heroic to fight this, even more so when you’re suffering. Old English poetry is full of epic tales shot through with melancholy warriors weeping at the sadness of the empty hall. In Roman culture the ability to embrace melancholy and fear – as well as scything off the limbs of your enemies – was seen as a sign of great and crowning masculinity. Scipio burnt Carthage to the ground, then sank into a massive depression, at which point he was seen as even more masculine, even more thrillingly in touch with his depths.

View image in fullscreen Prince William makes a speech at Everton’s Hill Dickinson Stadium on World Suicide Prevention Day. Photograph: Shirlaine Forrest/PA

Letting it out is strong. Would you like to be a Viking? Or a Roman hero with a sword? Well, those guys spent half their lives in a state of profound inner doubt, telling people all about it, then feeling so much more able to ride off on a horse and do something ostensibly useful.

There is something worth saying about sport in the middle of this. I was at Arsenal last weekend and before kick-off a bubbly and cheerful voice announced: “Suicide is NOT inevitable!” as though what we’re talking about here is having dandruff or not drinking enough water. The messaging is good. The messaging is great. The messaging is also, let’s be honest, an attempt to soothe the effects of the world in which big sport thrives and makes its fortunes. Is this a nice place?

It isn’t hard to work out why American TV is so full of adverts for antidepressants. Take a look at the stuff in between. Terrible, degrading food. Consumer goods you don’t need but must be made to crave. Pills to get you off that addiction to opioids we’ve already given you. Endless excitable messaging from corporations that secretly hate you.

Big Sport does not exist outside of this world. It is part of the same system. Oh, now you care about sad middle-aged men? The same ones who can’t afford to go any more, who feel alienated from what was once a bit of a lark and a chance to get together, whose brains must be subjected to the curated rage of the online idiot-scape?

The note of regret here is that sport still has so much power to be warm, to act as a source of contact. Witness for example the rush of love a few years back when Ben Stokes was able to talk about being depressed while simultaneously operating at his peak as England captain. It felt like a message no one had ever really sent in the same way, that you can feel like this and still be OK, or even heroically functional; that feeling all those things is really just a part of feeling.

Sports.title: West Ham cut loose to hit Wrexham for six and go top of Championship
Sports.content:
West Ham secured their fourth league win in a row as they returned to the top of the Championship with a thumping 6-0 win over Wrexham at the London Stadium. It was a marvellous display of attacking football from Nuno Espírito Santo’s side, who swept to victory with room to spare and six different scorers.

Jarrod Bowen got the ball rolling after 28 minutes, Joël Piroe made it two before the break, then Konstantinos Mavropanos, Taty Castellanos, Mohamadou Kanté and Manor Solomon all scored in the second half as the Welsh side were dealt a hiding. The performance was further evidence the Hammers are finding their feet in the second tier after failing to win any of their first three games following Premier League relegation.

They should have led inside seven minutes, Castellanos sending a free header from Solomon’s cross over from six yards. Bowen then got clear in the box from a quick throw, but his shot was turned against the crossbar by a reflex save from Anthony Patterson. From the corner that resulted, Mavropanos headed a foot wide at the far post.

Piroe was guilty of an awful miss midway through the half, leaning back and blasting high into the Wrexham fans behind Patterson’s goal. Bowen showed him how it was done a minute later. Morato’s cross from the right was timed perfectly into the six-yard box, where the home side’s captain was arriving ahead of Jacques Ekomié to guide it into the far corner.

Mavropanos cleared off the line from George Dobson with Mads Hermansen beaten, which proved to be the closest Wrexham would come to a goal. Castellanos stayed onside and strode on to a through pass before unselfishly squaring the ball for Piroe to make it 2-0 before the break.

Patterson prevented Solomon from putting the game beyond Wrexham in the first two minutes of the second half, racing from his goal to smother the forward’s low shot. It would be a momentary reprieve and under a minute later it was 3-0. From Bowen’s corner, Mavropanos was left free inside the six-yard box to head home.

Bowen flashed a shot inches wide after cutting inside as the besieged visitors teetered on the edge of an all-out collapse in east London. West Ham’s fourth came from a Wrexham corner. A poor ball into the box was collected by Kyle Walker-Peters, who dashed away on the counter, exchanging passes before teeing up Castellanos to slot the ball into the corner.
