Kanté came off the bench and made it 5-0, a lovely rising finish after being sent clear by Solomon, then the Israel international completed the rout with a deflected shot via a post.

Sports.title: Premier League news: Iraola values Wirtz’s work ethic; Moyes backs ‘senior citizen’ Grealish
Sports.content:
1. Wirtz’s worth ‘not all about statistics’ Andoni Iraola has insisted Florian Wirtz should be judged by his influence on Liverpool rather than statistics and believes the player’s impact will increase as his rapport with a new-look attack develops. Wirtz impressed in Liverpool’s defeat of Atlético Madrid on Wednesday, having also produced some of his best performances last season in the Champions League. But he has also come in for criticism this season for the amount of times he has conceded possession. The £116m Germany international has one assist and no goals in the Premier League so far. “Flo played very well against Atlético Madrid and I also think he has been unlucky,” said Iraola. “I remember the ‘goal’ he scored against Nottingham Forest; they gave it live and then VAR disallowed it. He could have had very good assists but we haven’t finished them. That is why you cannot just play because of the numbers. “Whether a striker scores a lot of goals or he doesn’t, you have to look at the performances. Does he help us to play well? Yes. Well, someone will score the goals and someone will give the assists. I am not too focused on numbers. Nowadays everything is about numbers, everyone tells players you have to assist, you have to score goals. For me, you have to help us play well. Someone will score the goals and I don’t care if it is the midfielders like it was the other day. Someone will score the goals if we are doing well collectively. “There is an argument to make that the wingers have changed more than anywhere else,” Iraola said. “Now we have new weapons we can use with Bradley and Victor. With Florian, he is key for us. I am not worried because he will quickly learn where Victor prefers the ball or where Bradley prefers the ball. And, also, Bradley in just his second game you could see they already had a good association. I am not very worried.” Andy Hunter

2. Grealish ‘can be a wingers’ role model’ David Moyes has told Jack Grealish he wants him to become a role model at Everton for fellow wingers Tyrique George and Tyler Dibling. Grealish made an immediate impact from the bench against Manchester United last Sunday in his first outing since rejoining Everton on loan from Manchester City. Despite a lack of minutes in pre-season, as he recovered from the fractured foot that curtailed his first campaign with Everton, the 31-year-old could start for Moyes’s side at Tottenham on Saturday. The Everton manager wants Grealish to take on more responsibility this season. “Jack knows when he comes here there is an opportunity for him to play and to show what he can do,” Moyes said. “But I also want him to be a senior professional and a role model. We’ve got Tyrique and Tyler and if ever you are looking at somebody for how to play as a wide player, Jack Grealish would certainly be one of them. “I think both of them could learn an awful lot from Jack and I want him to become that senior citizen among them, somebody who teaches them. We’ve got a mature Jack Grealish now as well in terms of understanding the game and being a team player – not that he is an individual but he plays with an individual style.” Moyes believes there is greater expectation on Grealish given it is his second season at the club and there is a need to fill the creative gap created by Iliman Ndiaye’s departure. “If there is one person who would be able to carry that it would be Jack, just because of the way he is,” he added. View image in fullscreen Jack Grealish made an immediate impact from the bench against Manchester United last Sunday in his first outing since rejoining Everton on loan. Photograph: Adam Vaughan/EPA “He’s had six and a half months out. He’s had no pre-season games, he came on for 15 minutes in the Community Shield, so he’s had no real football and Jack is someone who thrives on the football. He gets himself fit through the games more so than the training. We need to be careful and see how he goes but he’s looking good.” Andy Hunter

3. João Pedro ‘as good as Haaland’, says Alonso Xabi Alonso has claimed João Pedro is at Erling Haaland’s level and similar in style to Karim Benzema. The Chelsea striker has reacted to missing out on Brazil’s World Cup squad by making an excellent start to the season and was named the Premier League’s player of the month on Friday. João Pedro has scored twice in his first three league appearances and has formed an exciting attacking trio with Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers. Chelsea have scored 16 goals in all competitions and Alonso did not hold back when asked if the 24-year-old is as good as Haaland. “I would say yes,” Chelsea’s manager said. “If you count how many top strikers we have in the Premier League, I’m sure that João is there. Haaland for sure is there. So I would rate him that way.” The range of João Pedro’s game has added to his threat. Alonso played with Benzema at Real Madrid and sees similarities between the pair. “In many things he reminds me of Benzema,” he said. “He is good in the box, he is good out of the box, he is good coming to his left side, he is good with the head, he is very complete, he is intelligent. Still young, still things to develop, but many, many absolutely outstanding qualities.” Chelsea host Hull on Saturday afternoon and will be looking for a strong home performances after fighting back from 2-0 down to beat Leeds 6-3 in the Carabao Cup on Wednesday. View image in fullscreen João Pedro has scored twice in his first three league appearances for Chelsea. Photograph: Paul Childs/Action Images/Reuters Palmer was key to the comeback and revealed that Alonso, who had rotated heavily, ripped into his players at half-time against Leeds. “I was angry with myself that I didn’t help the players to play better or have a better feeling,” Alonso said. “There is a moment that you try to explain what is not working well, try to make preparations and then there is a moment that you need to kick their arse a little bit, in a nice way. It worked – not for me but the players who came on with a better quality and better everything in the second half.” Chelsea will again be without Moisés Caicedo. The midfielder is yet to start this season and Alonso does not want to risk him. Jacob Steinberg

Sports.title: Ballon d’Or shortlist shows up Premier League’s attacking failings – but tide could be turning
Sports.content:
Premier League representation is low when it comes to the 16 attacking players on this year’s Ballon d’Or shortlist. Manchester United’s Bruno Fernandes and Manchester City’s Erling Haaland are there but Cole Palmer, one of the nominees in 2025, is out after an injury-hit year and English football’s shift towards physicality and set pieces last season is summed up by none of the forwards from the best team in the country making the cut.

The trio giving Arsenal a presence – Gabriel Maghalhães, Declan Rice and William Saliba – are all defensive minded. Arsenal won the league but their forwards are not regarded as elite. Injuries played a part, denying Martin Ødegaard, Kai Havertz and Bukayo Saka fluency, but Mikel Arteta’s side were not loved by neutrals. There was respect rather than admiration for their defensive rigour. There was an argument that a lack of ambition after going 1-0 up stopped Arsenal from beating Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League final.

It was a close-run thing, but a second consecutive European title for PSG was a victory for attacking football over the Premier League’s attrition. Luis Enrique’s side keep beating English opponents, and there was a similar vibe at the World Cup. Games flowed more in North America, in part because of officials clamping down on the “meat wall” at set pieces.

As for England, Thomas Tuchel’s plan to tap into the Premier League’s physicality failed. England retreated in their semi-final defeat by Argentina. It is also significant that not until Anthony Gordon’s goal against Argentina did an England attacker who played in the Premier League last season score at the World Cup.

“Spanish football demands a different level of tactical and technical intelligence,” Gordon has said since leaving Newcastle for Barcelona. “In England, sometimes intensity can cover up mistakes. You can miscontrol the ball and still recover by winning the next physical battle.”

The English top flight’s appeal partly rests on those bruising qualities but the grind went too far last season. How many classic games can you remember? Some of the top sides having disappointing campaigns did not help but across the board there was grumbling about an over-reliance on set pieces and goalkeepers being squashed during elaborate corner routines. Anthony Barry, Tuchel’s assistant, noted that the game had become congealed in the middle. There was an emphasis on long throws and timewasting. The league was harder to watch.

View image in fullscreen Anthony Gordon has said Spanish football demands a ‘different level of tactical and technical intelligence’. Photograph: Newhouse Media/MB Media/Getty Images

Now comes the shift. One of the themes during the first three weeks of the campaign has been the pace quickening. Lawmakers have reacted. The five-second countdown and threat of a restart reversal at goalkicks and throw-ins have forced teams to think twice about timewasting. The 10-second time limit on players leaving the pitch at substitutions has helped and a trial with tactical timeouts mean an outfield player will have to go off for at least a minute after the restart of play if their side’s goalkeeper has gone down injured.

Early days, of course, but the football has been enjoyable and the numbers are encouraging. There have been four matches in which both teams have had 14 shots this season, compared with only one at the same stage last year. According to Opta, the average ball-in-play time has increased from 55min 23sec during the 2025-26 campaign to 57min 14sec. Delay times are down from 29.2sec to 26.7sec. Excluding penalties, the percentage of goals from set pieces has dipped from 27.5% to 23.5%.

There are more fast breaks per game (2.27 compared with 1.94), more shots per game via fast breaks (1.9 compared with 1.75) and more goals from fast breaks per game (0.43 from 0.23). Chelsea, more transitional under Xabi Alonso, are flowing and have been involved in some wild games. Liverpool have replaced Arne Slot with the counterpressing Andoni Iraola. Newcastle have been rapid under Matthias Jaissle, who has played to the strengths of Harvey Barnes and Anthony Elanga. Roberto De Zerbi seems an outlier at Tottenham, who need to speed up. Manchester City may soon want more incision from Enzo Maresca. The Italian favours a methodical style but even Pep Guardiola was moving away from obsessive control last season. There is a sense that some managers are closer in style to Jürgen Klopp than Guardiola at the moment. Alonso’s style has seemed very similar to Klopp so far. His willingness to let talent breathe is also quite like Carlo Ancelotti; Palmer has spoken about being allowed more freedom to roam under Alonso.

Perhaps there will be a correction as teams wise up to each other, Europe kicks in and injuries bite. Perhaps it will amuse you to hear that Arsenal remain top for delaying at a corner (with an average of 43.2sec). Then again, last Sunday delivered the season’s first clash between potential title rivals – Arsenal taking on Chelsea at the Emirates Stadium – and the action was breathless. Chelsea did not hold back and it was interesting that Arsenal welcomed the end-to-end openness.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Havertz was full of imagination up front and Ødegaard, Arsenal’s creative hub, dominated. It is a fascinating development. Defence was Arsenal’s greatest asset last season; Rice was more influential than Ødegaard in midfield. Now the Norwegian looks rejuvenated. Fitness helps but so does greater freedom. Chelsea did not shut the game down, so Ødegaard ran it. The best player in the best team was not a defender. At those levels Ødegaard looks as good as Fernandes.

View image in fullscreen Florian Wirtz has struggled to adapt to the pace of the Premier League. Photograph: Allstar Picture Library Ltd/Richard Sellers/Apl/Sportsphoto

This matters. Florian Wirtz, a star in Alonso’s champion Bayer Leverkusen side, has come to England and found the pace difficult at Liverpool. The Premier League needs top talent to feel it can shine. The three Bayern Munich forwards on the Ballon d’Or shortlist – Harry Kane, Luis Díaz and Michael Olise – moved from English teams. PSG’s Ousmane Dembélé and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia are fresh for the business end of the Champions League in part because they aren’t being pushed to the limit by teams such as Brentford and Bournemouth on the weekend. Jude Bellingham, England’s jewel, has never played in the Premier League. Vinícius Júnior toyed with moving to Arsenal but stayed with Kylian Mbappé at Real Madrid.

The Premier League is the strongest and most competitive in Europe. Yet there has been a talent drain. It is easy to imagine the best forwards feel they will have more fun creating and scoring against less intense Bundesliga defences and have the freshness to compete for the Champions League, international tournaments and for individual prizes.

Look at how the four semi-finalists at the World Cup were well represented by Premier League defenders and defensive midfielders but not by wingers and strikers. Where are the stars? Those who have left have mostly not been replaced, which is why the Premier League could do with Bradley Barcola shining at Liverpool after his arrival from PSG.

Barcola succeeding could convince others to follow. If the France winger is worn down, though, it could have the opposite effect. The Premier League has to be careful. The new measures to tackle timewasting could be a gamechanger. There were only four added minutes at the end of each half when Arsenal beat Chelsea. It felt refreshing.

Sports.title: Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall: ‘I’ve seen all of the meltdowns and it annoyed me’
Sports.content:
Transfer deadline day may be “exciting for everyone”, as Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall puts it, but his experience of that transfer deadline day at Everton hauled him through the same gamut of emotions as every Evertonian. Excitement turned to bewilderment before the conclusion of the window left the midfielder exasperated, but for entirely different reasons to a fanbase left questioning the club’s direction under The Friedkin Group.

How, now, is the mood in the squad? It is the obvious place to start after a deadline day that left David Moyes with fewer players than he had at the beginning, one striker and no cover for either full-back position. It also featured the US international striker Folarin Balogun walking out on a £40m transfer minutes after submitting a deal sheet. “Really good to be honest,” Dewsbury-Hall insists. “Definitely not the same mood as what I’ve seen on the outside. There’s a good mentality this year of: ‘We’ll show everyone.’” Everton’s performances so far this season support that view.

“I’ve seen all of the reactions, all of the meltdowns, and in all honestly it annoyed me a bit,” Dewsbury-Hall says in forthright and insightful fashion. “I get where people are coming from; everyone wants to sign everyone and have the perfect squad. But there are still 19 lads in this building who are going to hopefully take this club to good things this year. That was getting disregarded.

“I saw people saying: ‘We’ll be lucky to stay up this year.’ What message is that sending to the lads who are already here? I’m not blaming anyone. We get it. It didn’t work. But let’s all be positive – right, it’s done, bang, let’s go – and that’s what we’ve been trying to say in the dressing room. Of course we would have wanted to sign a couple more, but we’re happy with what we’ve got and it’s given us more impetus now to move on.”

Moyes has expressed concern over the signals Everton’s transfer business could send to the dressing room at a time when he is trying to push the team on. So has it had a detrimental impact? “Not really, no,” Dewsbury-Hall insists. “I know we’ve got a smaller squad but we’ve got some really good players. Our starting XI is top, a European starting XI.

View image in fullscreen Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall says he needed his move to Everton to avoid his career stagnating. Photograph: Tony McArdle/Everton FC/Getty Images

“I get it, you need a whole squad, but we’ve got 17, 18 players at a really, really good level. I don’t think a couple of years ago it was at that level. Actually I know it wasn’t. Things can be out of your hands in football and that’s what happened for us. But we quickly realised: ‘Hang on a minute, look around the dressing room – top player, top player, top player.’ If we’re doing the right things we can still be successful.”

Dewsbury-Hall will be crucial to those prospects. The midfielder has flourished since his £28m arrival from Chelsea last summer, his game-time and growing influence vindicating the decision to leave Stamford Bridge behind. “I’m in the prime years of my career,” he says. “I couldn’t afford to spend more years stagnating.” The 28-year-old’s influence extends behind the scenes. This summer, following Séamus Coleman’s departure, he was nominated for a new leadership group that was established to compensate for the loss of the long-serving Everton captain.

“Because Séamus has left such a big hole we need a group of experienced lads to crack on together and keep the standards high and to drive things,” Dewsbury-Hall explains. “It’s just the more experienced lads – [Jordan] Pickford, Tarky [James Tarkowski, the new club captain], Jimmy [James] Garner, myself. The ones that have been playing in the Premier League for years or feel like they are settled at the club.

View image in fullscreen Kiernan Dewsbury Hall lets fly in Everton’s impressive 2-2 draw with Manchester United. Photograph: Tony McArdle/Everton FC/Getty Images

“It’s nice [to be voted in after just one season] but it’s definitely an impact I wanted to have. I’m really pleased that the lads look at me as someone that can be important for the dressing room.”

That sense of responsibility is evident in Dewsbury-Hall’s mentoring of fellow midfielder Harrison Armstrong, the 19-year-old who almost joined Nottingham Forest before deadline day only for the furious response of Evertonians at Bournemouth to prompt a U-turn from the club’s owners. “They definitely made their feelings known and obviously it worked,” says Dewsbury-Hall. “Big credit to them for that, they were amazing that day. And I know for a fact it made Harrison feel very good and it helped him. He is a very confident lad and well respected in the dressing room for such a young age.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“If there is anything I can help him with then I will. Shooting’s definitely one because his shooting is sometimes not the best, and I’ve told him that many times. But he’s got pretty much everything else. He always likes to say he’s got a better strike than me so I just tell him to look at the [Crystal] Palace goal [that Dewsbury-Hall scored on the opening day] or the Wolves goal last season. We have good banter.”

The Nottingham-born midfielder is clear in his targets for this season: European qualification, which he contends can be achieved despite the smaller squad, a strong cup run, improvement in his all-round game and a first England call-up. His rising performance levels have not gone unnoticed by Thomas Tuchel, who names his squad next Friday.

Dewsbury-Hall says: “I know I’m the closest I have ever been now. You get a message two weeks before the squad is announced. I got one for the long list for the World Cup and I’ve had one for these next games. It’s nice. It means you are doing OK. It’s a long, long message. It tells you that it’s a legal requirement for us [the Football Association] to tell you in advance that you are in contention and to be available for these dates. It’s a good feeling because you think: ‘OK, I am close,’ but you know you have to keep pushing it to the last minute. It’s up to me. It’s got to be me that forces his hand to choose me. It’s not going to be given to me.”

Nor will anything be given to Everton, but Dewsbury-Hall and company will push on regardless.

Sports.title: Evangelos Marinakis appoints manager considered by Tottenham and Bournemouth
Sports.content:
Tottenham and Bournemouth both came close to appointing new Olympiacos head coach Imanol Alguacil, talkSPORT understands.

Alguacil took charge of the Greek giants earlier this week, as he was chosen by Nottingham Forest owner Evangelos Marinakis to succeed Jose Luis Mendilibar following his brief tenure.



5 Imanol Alguacil takes charge of Olympiacos having built a strong reputation in Spain

In a manner which has become familiar, Marinakis axed Mendilibar just seven matches into the new season.

The departing manager became the 25th coach dismissed by the Greek businessman, who also owns Forest and Rio Ave, in 16 years.

Hours later, his successor was revealed to be Alguacil, who carved out a strong reputation during his seven years in charge of Real Sociedad.



The 55-year-old led the Basque outfit between 2018 and 2025, during which time he won the Copa del Rey in 2020 – the club’s first trophy in 34 years.

Having taken on Sociedad as a mid-table LaLiga outfit, Alguacil went on to European qualification in five consecutive seasons - reaching the last 16 of the Champions League and Europa League.



Premier League interest

With Alguacil building an impressive CV in Spain, talkSPORT can reveal this led to him being considered by Premier League clubs.

After the Spaniard left Sociedad at the end of the 2025/26, Tottenham explored the possibility of hiring him before ultimately settling on Thomas Frank.



This proved an ill-fated appointment, with Frank lasting just eight months in charge while Spurs went on to narrowly avoid relegation.

And more recently, talkSPORT understands Bournemouth identified Alguacil as a candidate for their head coach vacancy this summer.

With the tactician spending seven months at Saudi Pro League side before departing in February, the Cherries shortlisted him among their managerial options after Andoni Iraola's departure.

5 Evangelos Marinakis bought Olympiacos in 2010 Credit: Getty



5 Spurs and Bournemouth kept tabs on Alguacil after he left Real Sociedad and had a brief spell in charge of Al Shabab

Marco Rose instead took charge at the Vitality Stadium, and is searching for his first win after setting an unwanted Premier League record in his first three games.

Alguacil is also understood to have been high up on Liverpool's list of options, with his work at Sociedad ranking him highly in their data, before Iraola ultimately took the role.

And while the Spanish coach missed out on a Premier League role, he is said to have been sold on the project at new club Olympiacos.



Discussions centred on their sporting project - with Marinakis' goal to compete strongly in Europe and the opportunity for Alguacil to build something rather than simply taking the next available job.

Rated by Mourinho and Enrique

As well as being considered for major vacancies, Alguacil's rising stock has seen him earn praise from some of football's leading managers.

Alguacil’s record of 153 wins and 95 losses in 330 matches at Sociedad led to the legendary Jose Mourinho admitting he struggled to find a weakness in his team after facing him as Roma manager.

5 Alguacil's only managerial silverware so far is the 2020 Copa del Rey with Real Sociedad



5 Real Madrid boss Mourinho was full of praise for Alguacil when the pair faced off in 2023 Credit: Getty

Speaking in 2023, the ex-Manchester United and Chelsea boss said: “It’s difficult to find weaknesses in Real Sociedad.

"Imanol is a very good coach; he has a very well-prepared team.

“In addition to the quality they have, they are also capable of changing systems from one match to another or even during the same game.”

Mourinho isn't his only admirer, with PSG's back-to-back Champions League-winning boss Luis Enrique also claiming Sociedad played the most impressive best in LaLiga under Alguacil.



After facing Alguacil's Sociedad, Enrique said: “What a great team, what a way to compete!

“They are wonderful. I’ll tell you something: Real Sociedad is the Spanish team that plays the best football, without any doubt. Imanol Alguacil deserves congratulations.”

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta is not crazy for sabotaging Arsenal’s pre-season – it’s completely right
Sports.content:
Dean Saunders has defended Mikel Arteta after the Arsenal boss revealed he deliberately disrupted his side's match preparations during pre-season.

The Gunners were affected by air traffic control issues as they travelled to Italy to face Napoli in their Champions League opener.



4 Arteta's Arsenal are looking to win the Champions League this season after losing in the final last term Credit: Getty

Delays flying out of London Luton Airport on Tuesday meant that Arteta's side arrived in Italy around three hours behind schedule.

Arsenal managed to put this behind them on the pitch, as they earned a deserved 1-0 win at the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona.

And Arteta later said his team had been unaffected by the disruption because of his methods used in pre-season.



In his press conference ahead of the Gunners' trip to Sunderland, he said: "I love those challenges and I try to create them in pre-season. So when they happen, we have already experienced them and we are ready.

"So, get to the stadium very late, change the routine and suddenly the players have to do something else.



"It can happen, you can miss the flight, the train can be delayed, there is so much traffic, and I don't want the players and the staff panicking so when that happens, adapt to it.

"When that happens, adapt to it. We have two or three hours on the plane - can we use it? Play together, spend some time together, sleep.



"But don't complain or use it as an excuse because it's not helpful at all."

Arteta's methods defended

Reacting to the news on talkSPORT, ex-Liverpool and Wales striker Saunders defended Arteta's outside-the-box methods, pointing to his own experiences as a manager.

"Having managed myself, I can understand where he's coming from," Saunders said.

4 Arteta opened up on his most recent outlandish method in a recent press conference



4 The Gunners seemed to benefit from their preparations, as Martin Odegaard's goal sealed victory over Napoli Credit: Getty

"Because basically as a manager... I'll put it in a nutshell. Your job is to sign good players, get them fit, give them a plan with and without the ball and keep the discipline. Those are the basics.

"So what you try and do as a coach is eliminate every single excuse a player can throw at you. Because they will. Players find an excuse for everything.

Saunders continued: “Fitness levels to start with, they've got to be fit. And the physio treatment. So we're all fit.



“Training intensity - because they'll start throwing that one in. Is the hotel nice? Yes. Is the food that we're serving you up nice? Yeah. Have I given you a plan all week? Yes.

“So everybody's ready. No excuses. Get over that white line. Do not come in this dressing room and give me excuses. That's the only thing you can do for players - put them on the pitch and say, 'Go on then, I've set everything up for you'.

"That's what he's trying to do. He's trying to get in their heads and say, 'No excuses lads'."

4 Arteta has overseen Arsenal's 100 per cent start to the season Credit: Getty



Arteta's past innovations

This isn't the first time Arteta has made the headlines with his unusual methods to get the best out of his Arsenal side.

In the 2022 All or Nothing Amazon documentary covering the club, the Gunners boss famously prepared his team for an away trip to Anfield by blasting Liverpool's 'You'll Never Walk Alone' anthem on loudspeakers during training.

For another game, Arteta used a lightbulb in a pre-match team talk - as he wanted his players to shine and emit energy to one another.

Then in 2024, he hired professional pickpockets to steal items from his players during a team dinner, which was used as a lesson to teach them to stay alert.



Arteta's outlandish methods appeared to have rubbed off on his players too when, in April, a fire was lit at the club’s London Colney training ground by the team in an attempt to rouse themselves for their Champions League clash with Sporting Lisbon.

Sunderland vs Arsenal LIVE commentary: Match kick-off time moved as Guimaraes prepares for hostile debut

Arsenal head to Sunderland on Saturday night aiming to continue their blistering start to the season.

The reigning Premier League champions have made a flawless start to the campaign with three consecutive victories to kickstart their title defence.

5 Mikel Arteta's side are already looking like the team to beat this season Credit: Getty

Arsenal got their season going with a convincing 3-0 win over Coventry before a hard-fought 1-0 victory at Aston Villa.

Last time out, the Gunners came from behind to see off Xabi Alonso’s Chelsea in their toughest test of the season so far.

Next up is a trip to the Stadium of Light where Mikel Arteta’s side could only manage a 2-2 draw last season.

Sunderland quickly bounced back from their opening day defeat at Ipswich by picking up four points in their last two matches.

A 1-0 win over Fulham preceded Saturday’s 1-1 draw at Brentford and boss Regis Le Bris will be plotting a huge upset in this weekend’s clash.

Arsenal travel north to take on Sunderland on Saturday, September 12.

Sunderland vs Arsenal team news

He understands the game - he’s five, 10 seconds ahead. He knows what’s happening, he doesn’t need to think about it - he just acts, and it makes the people around him better which is another massive quality.

5 Kai Havertz continues to play a key role for Mikel Arteta's side

"When you put it in a tactical world, you probably put the nine in the centre - but then what do you do when there’s a set-piece, a transition moment, a high press, what if the goalkeeper is right or left-footed?

"There are a lot of factors that are going to take that space and the initial position to a different dimension."

Sports.title: How to follow Liverpool vs Fulham: Arbeloa returns to Anfield aiming to succeed in test Gerrard failed twice
Sports.content:
How to follow Liverpool vs Fulham: Arbeloa returns to Anfield aiming to succeed in test Gerrard failed twice

Former Liverpool defender Alvaro Arbeloa returns to Anfield on Saturday as his Fulham side take on the Reds.

Arbeloa played 98 games for Liverpool from 2007 to 2009, featuring 66 times in the Premier League during that stint.



4 Arbeloa is returning to Anfield as a manager after spending two years there as a player Credit: Getty

He's now going to be back on Merseyside, hoping to come out on top against his old side and pick up a much-needed win.

Fulham have lost their first three games in the Premier League this season, with boss Arbeloa still waiting on three points.

That has the Cottagers sitting 19th in the table heading into this clash, so they will be desperate for a victory.



History, however, doesn't give Arbeloa much chance of glory on his return to Anfield.

Three previous Liverpool players have taken on the club as a manager in the Premier League, but none of them have won.



Paul Ince was in charge of Blackburn in 2008 when his side were beaten by the Reds, while Mauricio Pellegrino lost twice to his old club when managing Southampton in 2017/18.

And most recently, club icon Steven Gerrard lost both of his meetings with Liverpool with Aston Villa in the 2021/22 campaign.



Can Arbeloa put an end to that losing streak? He'll hope to do so, particularly to Fulham's dismal start to the season.

How to follow Liverpool vs Fulham

Liverpool host Fulham on Saturday, September 12.

Kick-off at Anfield is scheduled for 3pm - which means the game is not available to watch live on TV due to the 3pm blackout.

Liverpool vs Fulham: Team news

Reds boss Andoni Iraola provided reassurance over summer signing Bradley Barcola after the winger limped off in Wednesday's 2-1 win over Atletico Madrid.

Speaking in his pre-match press conference on Friday the Spaniard said: "We still need to train this afternoon but Barcola was just cramps.

"We have to evaluate but there's no injury he should be available if everything goes normal.

Iraola appeared less hopeful over the availability of Cody Gakpo who missed the Champions League opener in midweek with an abductor issue.



"Cody we will see," the Liverpool boss said. "We will try with him and let's see if he's ready or we have to wait until the next one.

Liverpool still have Hugo Ekitike, Joe Gomez, Conor Bradley, Federico Chiesa and Giovanni Leoni ruled out injured.

But Alexander Isak appears to be back to his best following his long injury layoff, scoring twice against Ipswich.

4 Bradley Barcola could be in contention despite his premature exit on Wednesday night Credit: Getty



4 Isak has been in fine form at the start of the new Premier League season Credit: AFP

He has already scored as many goals as he did last season, looking to now score in a third straight Premier League game for the first time since a streak between December 2024 and January 2025.

Victor Munoz could start on the right wing again, with the Spaniard preferred to Rio Ngumoha in the last two games.

As for Fulham, Tom Cairney is the only injured absentee.

Josh King is expected to continue in the No.10 position after scoring two goals in the first three games of the season.



But Sander Berge, Emile Smith Rowe and summer signing Hugo Larsson will hope to get a start at Anfield.

Sports.title: Celtic visited by police in Old Firm behaviour warning after fans banned from stadium
Sports.content:
Celtic visited by police in Old Firm behaviour warning after fans banned from stadium

Martin O’Neill revealed that his Celtic squad were given a behaviour warning from Police Scotland ahead of Sunday’s trip to Rangers.

The Hoops will make the short trip to Ibrox to face their city rivals in the Premier Sports Cup quarter-final.

4 Unsavoury scenes marred the Scottish Cup clash between the teams in March Credit: PA

4 Fans from both sides clashed on the pitch after Celtic scored Credit: Getty

Celtic head into the cauldron without the backing of their supporters after the SPFL opted to ban away fans from league and cup fixtures between the two clubs this season.

It comes after a ticket allocation dispute between the clubs that was sparked by fan disorder when the teams met in last season’s Scottish Cup quarter-final.

Celtic were victorious that day after a penalty shootout but the violent scenes that marred the win back in March will be felt during Sunday’s clash.

The Scottish Premiership champions were given a warning over their general behaviour by Police Scotland on Friday.

Celtic boss O’Neill revealed that his squad were briefed in an attempt to keep a lid on any possible outbursts during the match.

An opportune heads up

"We had the police come in today, just a little 15-minute meeting to remind us of our behaviour, which I think is a timely reminder," O'Neill revealed.

"I think it's just the overall picture. Gosh, it'd be nice to have something to celebrate. I think it's just general behaviour.

"They didn't mention this, but I'd assume one of the things would be what happens on the field of play, these things can be taken further.

"Punch-ups and excessive celebrations. I'd be delighted to be celebrating in the game, but in light of what's happened in recent fixtures, the conversations with police wouldn't have taken place."

Celtic have been triumphant in the last three Old Firm meetings since Rangers’ last win – a 3-1 win at Celtic Park in January.

4 O'Neill is relishing Sunday's trip to a raucous Ibrox Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

The Hoops find themselves five points ahead of their rivals in the Premiership with just six games played.

But Sunday’s clash without their travelling supporters will provide a huge test for O’Neill’s men.

Pressed on the prospect of playing at Ibrox without their fans, O’Neill said: "I think the games themselves almost take care of themselves in that sense.

"It'll be strange in many aspects not to have any away fans in our area. I always felt as if it would give you a crumb of comfort in some description.

"Nervously looking forward to it, excitedly looking forward to it.

"I suppose if you get in front in the game, that makes them anxious. Talking about getting in front and getting in front are two different things. The crowd will be right behind their team, which you would expect.

4 Celtic will not be able to call upon their travelling fans for Sunday's quarter-final Credit: Getty

"We just do our best. We know that we're up against a very fine side. We're up against a crowd that can make a difference. I'd be delighted to be celebrating something in the game."

Baptism of fire?

O'Neill could opt for England international Sam Johnstone in goal after his clean sheet in midweek.

The Celtic boss favoured Viljami Sinisalo at the start of the season but may persist with the former West Brom shot-stopper.

"I haven't made my mind up," O'Neill admitted. "I thought he (Johnstone) did very well. We had to get a look at what Sam could do. It's great to have the two of them.

"Vil has done exceptionally well for us. It was just an opportunity for us to see what Sam could do now; what he could do a couple of years ago was fantastic. What he can do now might have been a different picture."

Sports.title: Why there is no 12:30pm Premier League kick-off today with Arsenal clash moved

Why there is no 12:30pm Premier League kick-off today with Arsenal clash moved

For the first time this season, there will be no early kick-off in the Premier League today.

Fans have been treated to three brilliant 12:30pm matches so far this term, but they're going to have to wait for their football this weekend.

In the opening Saturday of the campaign, Hull City shocked Manchester United, with the newly-promoted side winning 2-0.

And goals galore followed, with Liverpool and Nottingham Forest drawing 2-2 before Newcastle and Bournemouth did the same last weekend.

However, there is no early game to look forward to this weekend, meaning fans have to patiently wait for the action...



Why is there no early kick-off this Saturday?

The Premier League have shuffled the schedule today due to the European football being played in midweek.

Sunderland vs Arsenal is taking place at 8pm, exclusively live on talkSPORT, after the match was confirmed to be rescheduled in July.



The match at the Stadium of Light was moved two months ago as the league pre-empted that the Gunners would be playing in the Champions League in the days prior.

Mikel Arteta's side beat Napoli 1-0 in Italy on Wednesday evening.

Sunderland vs Arsenal was also selected for TV coverage on TNT Sports, with the broadcaster only able to use the 12:30pm and 8pm slots.



Typically, if a game can't be played early on a Saturday due to a team playing in Europe on a Wednesday or Thursday, they will instead broadcast the fixture in their late slot.

In this case, Sunderland vs Arsenal was switched to the 8pm slot, which has left the early kick-off empty this weekend.

Sports.title: Wrexham issue ‘sincere apology’ after local councillor tells them to ‘get their act together’
Sports.content:
Wrexham issue ‘sincere apology’ after local councillor tells them to ‘get their act together’

Wrexham found themselves in a dispute with a local councillor after redeveloping their training base without full planning permission.

The Welsh side completed work on their Colliers Park facility in September before getting the green light from North Wales Council.



4 Wrexham have been on an incredible journey since Ryan Reynolds and Rob McElhenney's takeover in 2021 Credit: Getty

Club chiefs submitted an application for a new pavilion at the site in August, when the building was almost finished.

Wrexham later issued a public apology after their construction work was slammed by Gresford community council planning committee chair, Councillor Mike Morris.

The local council said that the club's rise - from non league to the Championship under Hollywood owners Ryan Reynolds and Rob McElhenney - is 'no excuse for not following the procedure properly'.



Wrexham slammed by local councillor

Councillor Morris hit out at Wrexham's lack of planning process, aiming some strong words at the second-tier outfit.

He said: “I do wish that people would get their act in order and not put in retrospective applications just because it suits you — which, at the end of the day, (is) what it came down to.



“You wanted to do it in the summer, and you know the fact you’ve had good results, and you know the football club is doing very well, we all applaud that, but it’s no excuse for not following the procedure properly.

“It’s no different to any other retrospective application.

“So it will be a matter for members to consider whether they are going to support it or not, and that will come out in the debate.”



Once reports are completed on the matter, local councillors will vote on Wrexham's project.

In response, the Red Dragons' chief strategy officer Aidan Miller offered a 'sincere' apology to the committee and local residents.

4 Wrexham could be faced with a long wait to get official permission for their new training facility Credit: Getty

Miller said: “The club sought to undertake the works during the summer off-season period, when activity at the site is significantly reduced, allowing construction activity and associated impacts to be managed effectively and within the site footprint.



“The club recognises that planning permission would ordinarily be secured before development commences, and we sincerely apologise to the committee and local residents.

“Notwithstanding this, throughout the development of the project, the club has sought to act responsibly by selecting an established sporting location, making use of existing infrastructure, and designed a proposal to minimise impacts on neighbouring occupiers and the wider community.

“The club has engaged fully and thoroughly with the planning process, including undertaking pre-application consultation, engaging with statutory consultees, and responding to matters raised in relation to parking, highways and phosphate mitigation.”

Wrexham's training ground redevelopment isn't the only construction work taking place at the club, with a new Kop stand at their Racecourse Stadium also in the works.



It is anticipated the new-look Kop would boost their total stadium capacity to 18,000.

4 Construction of a new Kop stand at Wrexham's Racecourse Ground is underway Credit: Getty

4 Phil Parkinson watched his Wrexham side ship six goals away to West Ham on Friday Credit: Getty

Wrexham dealt Hammer blow

With plenty going on behind the scenes, Wrexham suffered a setback on the pitch on Friday night as they were thumped 6-0 by West Ham.



The result leaves Phil Parkinson’s side 16th in the Championship with one win from seven games.

This was the club's heaviest defeat under the Reynolds and McElhenney ownership, leading talkSPORT's Scott Minto to question the future of manager Parkinson - in his sixth season in charge.

Minto said on air: "There's very, very ambitious owners.

"But you have to think about what he's done and he’s earned the right to right this wrong… but this is a really poor run.

"And there are question marks against him maybe with signings, certainly with substitutions, or lack of, tonight."

Sports.title: England v Pakistan SERIES RATINGS: Who was 'near-perfect from start to finish'? How did Joe Root fare on his return as captain? And which struggling star scored just 2/10?
Sports.content:
England v Pakistan SERIES RATINGS: Who was 'near-perfect from start to finish'? How did Joe Root fare on his return as captain? And which struggling star scored just 2/10?

England swept Pakistan with an eight-wicket victory in Birmingham to clinch a comfortable 3-0 series win on Saturday.

Daily Mail Sport's RICHARD GIBSON was at Edgbaston and runs the rule over England's players in his series ratings.

Ben Duckett: 2/10

The senior opener finished bottom of England’s batting averages for the three Tests, with a mark of 8.8. The question for the selectors will be whether this is a long-term problem - he also endured an underwhelming tour of Australia last winter - or an isolated blip.

Duckett finished bottom of England’s batting averages for the three Tests, with a mark of 8.8

Emilio Gay: 5/10

Endured a difficult second series as a Test cricketer, in matches where the balance of power lay with the ball, but showed some mettle by digging in for a half century in the first innings at Edgbaston, just as the debate about his shelf life was whipping up. 5

Jordan Cox: 7/10

Has displayed levels of versatility that ensure an England future: this series has not only shown him to be a competent replacement for Jacob Bethell at No 3, but also an able deputy with the wicketkeeping gloves, giving him an advantage in future squad selections over another fill-in gloveman Ollie Pope.

Joe Root: 6.5/10

A reputation for being one of the game’s great problem solvers needs to be lived up to, fast. Discounting a run out, each of the England captain’s last eight dismissals has been leg before wicket. Pakistan’s medium-paced seamers feasted on his weakness to balls nipping back into the stumps. Lacked clarity when Pakistan’s tail wagged this week.

Harry Brook: 7.5/10

Threw away the chance of a first hundred in 13 months with an ill-judged call for a single in Birmingham, but his overall demeanour bodes well. Brook is at his most valuable to the team when playing the situation in front of him and batting for the close on day one was a positive sign at the start of the post-Bazball era.

Brook is at his most valuable to the team when playing the situation in front of him

Dan Lawrence: 7/10

Determined to ensure a fourth life as an England player is more than a fleeting one, the response to his recall has been 50s in each of his three appearances and a decent cameo of his off spin in the third Test. Like Cox, he appears to have a plane ticket for South Africa sorted.

Jamie Smith: 6.5/10

Finished the summer strongly, countering a previous struggle dating back to the Ashes. Kept smoothly, whether up to the stumps or back, and made it three 50s in four Tests with eye-catching innings at Lord’s and Edgbaston, where he struck 69 despite nursing a dislocated finger.

Gus Atkinson: 5/10

Luckless for seven-eighths of the series, it was not until Pakistan’s final innings that he put some dropped catches and near misses behind him. He had 201 runs to his name, in fact, before he took his second wicket, courtesy of a splendid slip catch by Lawrence. He will bowl worse and take more.

Ollie Robinson: 9.5/10

Near perfect from start to finish, Robinson’s mastery with the new ball makes one wonder what he might have added to England’s Ashes bid last winter. No one has taken 20+ wickets in a series in this country at such a low average before (21 at 8.76) and he even added a 50 with the bat.

Robinson was 'near perfect from start to finish' according to Daily Mail Sport's Richard Gibson

Jofra Archer: 7.5/10

This is the first multi-match series in which the Sussex fast bowler has been an ever present during a seven-year Test career. A collection of 23 wickets also makes this his best ever summer. The sustained pace and hostility in the three outings against Pakistan were arguably his most impressive trait, but his failure to deal with Razaullah’s long handle added a late blip.

Josh Tongue: 8.5/10

His determination to dismiss batsmen with attacking plans means he can be expensive at times, but his success rate is what England will be most enthused about ahead of bigger challenges against South Africa away and Australia at home. His 19 victims mean he is averaging more than five a Test over a 15-match career.

PAKISTAN: Azan Awais 4, Imam-ul-Haq 2, Saim Ayub 1, Abdullah Shafique 3, Shan Masood 4, Babar Azam 4, Saud Shakeel 6.5, Salman Agha 3, Mohammad Rizwan 4, Ghazi Ghori 4, Ali Usman 6, Khurram Shahzad 3, Mohammad Ali 5.5, Mohammad Abbas 8, Mohammad Imran 3, Razaullah 7.

Sports.title: England survive scare as Joe Root guides hosts to series whitewash over Pakistan at Edgbaston
Sports.content:
England survive scare as Joe Root guides hosts to series whitewash over Pakistan at Edgbaston

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

England were given an almighty early morning scare before half centuries from captain Joe Root and Jordan Cox wrapped up a 3-0 whitewash of Pakistan at Edgbaston.

Mohammad Abbas, one of Pakistan’s tail-end heroes on Friday evening, struck twice in the opening over to breathe further life into the third Rothesay Test.

Had Mohammad Ali not sent down a 17th no-ball of the series, England would have been reduced to 35 for three - and Root dismissed.

Neither was the inside edge into his stumps on 23 the only close call for Root, who twice nicked in the vicinity of first slip before going on to reach 50 from 57 balls.

There had also been an over-ambitious review for leg before wicket by Shan Masood, deputising as captain with Babar Azam temporarily off the field, earlier in Ali’s over.

Intent on making the most of the cloud cover, Abbas rejected the original ball handed to him before the start of play and selected his own from fourth umpire Russell Warren’s box.

Half centuries from captain Joe Root (above) and Jordan Cox wrapped up a 3-0 whitewash of Pakistan at Edgbaston

It seemed to be of his liking, as Ben Duckett rounded off the most miserable of series with a first-ball departure, held low down by wicketkeeper Ghazi Ghori.

A dramatic start to the fourth morning then took another twist when Emilio Gay was pinned leg before by one that nipped back off the seam from around the wicket, taking a review with him.

England set off in pursuit of 130 in the knowledge that only once had Pakistan successfully defended so few runs in Test history, against New Zealand back in 1993 when, with Waqar Younis and Wasim Akram in their pomp, they won with 127 to play with.

Not since 1997 when Australia imploded for 104 had any team managed to seal a Test match win in this country when faced with 130 or fewer in the bank.

But any hope of Pakistan pulling off a spectacular heist went when Ali overstepped, leaving Cox to hit the winning run, pouncing on a misfield, after bringing up a third 50-plus score of the series.

Sports.title: Lewis Hamilton crashes in Spanish Grand Prix final practice - and IGNORES order from engineer - as row with Ferrari escalates
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton crashes in Spanish Grand Prix final practice - and IGNORES order from engineer - as row with Ferrari escalates

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Lewis Hamilton was involved in a frosty exchange with his engineer after crashing his Ferrari into the barriers during the final practice session of the Madrid Grand Prix on Saturday.

The 'car-killing' Madring claimed another victim when Hamilton - who was on course to set the fastest time of the session - veered off track and into the barriers ahead of qualifying.

The collision caused major damage to the front wing of the car, with seven-time world champion Hamilton told to leave the car and allow for a recovery vehicle to return it to the garage.

However, the 41-year-old defied orders from his engineer and reversed out of the barriers before making his way onto the track, seemingly eager to return the car himself.

He was repeatedly told to 'stop the car' but ploughed on with a tyre puncture, before eventually limping to a halt.

The British driver has been at the centre of tension behind the scenes at La Scuderia, with last weekend's Italian Grand Prix seeing an explosive clash with team-mate Charles Leclerc.

Hamilton was squeezed off the track by Leclerc, clearly the Monegasque's error, in the second half of the first chicane in early exchanges of positions last Sunday. 'Charles pushed me off,' the seven-time world champion complained at the time.

Lewis Hamilton crashed his Ferrari and defied team orders in Madrid on Saturday

Leclerc crashed out moments later at the Parabolica in an unrelated event, again his mistake, and it was a big bang. Hamilton went on to finish sixth – a combination of failure that amounted to a poor result for Ferrari on home turf.

In a message to team principal Fred Vasseur, the seven-time world champion said: ‘Here there are no rules. And that’s something that needs to change. When I was at Mercedes we had written rules of engagement. And we never had it too bad.

‘There was a moment with me and Nico a couple of times. But more often than not, it was good. Here there are no rules.

But speaking ahead of the new home of the Spanish Grand Prix, Hamilton revealed he held crunch talks with his team-mate: 'What is great is that there was no shying away from having a discussion. We sat face to face, just him (Charles) and me, and talked about it and we were both honest and open and then we quashed it and moved on.

'That shows maturity from him and it is healthy. It is a relationship we have built over time.

'Of course, there are going to be frustrations along the way. And there will be more times where we are close because we are approximate in pace and we both want to win as much as each other and do well for the team, but, yes, it is really positive.

'It has been really positive. I spoke to Fred (Vasseur, Ferrari's team principal) on Monday and we had clearing out discussions.

'Naturally we are going to have different opinions, but we come together to find a way forward and that is the positive of where we have got to over the past 15 months, when we can have really great communication internally and same with me and Charles.

'If you look at the history of the sport, this happened before, so it is no biggie.'

Hamilton was ordered to stop the car but refused, despite extensive damage to his front wing

Hamilton spoke after the race in Italy about needing rules of engagement. Have they been agreed?

'No,' he said. 'Right now I am trying to focus on having a better weekend. I am sure at some stage we will discuss how we can be better but we have not had a lot of time. You can't change things in two days.'

Hamilton's deficit to Mercedes' championship leader Kimi Antonelli stands at 76 points. It is a vertical fight for the Briton. Tough, but the target is not insurmountable.

Chasing a never-achieved eighth title, Hamilton said: 'Mathematically it is not impossible, but it is the biggest gap I have seen in a long, long time, and at this stage of the year, too (with 10 rounds remaining).

'Mercedes are the leaders, out ahead, and doing a fantastic job and we should just focus on doing our best each weekend.

'My job at Ferrari is a long-term process and not something that will change this weekend. There are a huge amount of moving parts, a lot of people, and a culture that has been there for a long time. Moving pieces are not so easy. It doesn't happen overnight. But we will get there.'

Sports.title: 'We have to stay humble': Lisandro Martinez fires warning to Man United team-mates after Champions League rout over FK Sabah - with Michael Carrick's side plotting another derby scalp over arch rivals City
Sports.content:
'We have to stay humble': Lisandro Martinez fires warning to Man United team-mates after Champions League rout over FK Sabah - with Michael Carrick's side plotting another derby scalp over arch rivals City

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Lisandro Martinez has called on Manchester United to remain 'calm and humble' heading into Sunday's derby against Manchester City – despite the 4-0 rout of FK Sabah in the Champions League.

Martinez added the cherry on top of a very good night for United when he bundled in a fourth goal in front of the Stretford End on Thursday against Azerbaijani minnows Sabah.

While Martinez accepts that confidence has shot up as a result of the team's exploits in Europe, hosting Manchester City at Old Trafford on Sunday afternoon is not a task anyone in United red can afford to take lightly.

'When you win, your confidence is going up, you know, but now we have to be calm, we have to be humble,' he said.

'Then tomorrow we have to think about the derby that is really important for us.'

Martinez is a World Cup winner and has bags of experience in a squad bursting with young players.

Lisandro Martinez (right) has warned Man United from getting complacent after a big 4-0 win

Martinez was on the scoresheet against FK Sabah - but he knows tougher tests are ahead

With that in mind, the Argentinian centre back felt compelled to play down talk that United now look capable of challenging for the very biggest prizes.

'It's too early to say that,' Martinez added.

'We just have to be ready every game, we have to be humble, have to enjoy, have to fight every game, and we know what we want, but I can't tell you [if we will challenge at the top this season].'

The win over Sabah was as celebrated by United staff for the goals scored but also for the clean sheet, the first of the season after conceding two goals in games against Hull City, Ipswich Town and Everton.

For Martinez, the issues at the back, which were exposed badly at Hull City and late on at Everton, 'annoy' United's stars.

'It will always be a responsibility for us [to keep clean sheets] but I think against Everton, I think we played to take the clean sheet and then we conceded the goals, that's what annoys us,' he said.

'It's really bad, for sure, because we want to be there, and if we want to compete, we have to keep the clean sheet because it's very important. Today we did it and we have to build on that.'

'Yeah, but that is the past. It's the past, you know, it's gone and now we have to, I have to be ready for this game because it's going to be so different than the last one.'

Sports.title: Chelsea target Lamine Camara breaks silence on dramatic collapse of £47m deadline-day move to Xabi Alonso's side
Sports.content:
Monaco's Lamine Camara has insisted that he has 'turned the page' after his £47.2million move to Chelsea dramatically collapsed minutes after the window closed on deadline day.

Chelsea thought they had secured the 22-year-old Senegal midfielder with less than two hours of deadline day remaining, having agreed a £47.2m deal. However, in an eventful twist, the Blues were left stunned and furious when Monaco then went back on their word.

Chelsea sources told Daily Mail Sport at the time that the two clubs had reached a full, written, club-to-club agreement for Camara to join.

Yet when Monaco renegotiated their transfer of Folarin Balogun to Everton, Chelsea were told that the six-year deal with the option of a one-year extension for Camara was being withdrawn. Insiders at Stamford Bridge described it as a deeply unprofessional way for another club to conduct business.

Camara appeared to be keen to draw a line under the situation ahead of Monaco's match against Strasbourg on Saturday.

He said: 'There was a possibility I could leave. It didn't go through at the last minute and that's part of football.

'I've turned the page and am focusing on the season.'

Monaco's Lamine Camara (right) has insisted that he has 'turned the page' after a £47.2million move to Chelsea dramatically collapsed minutes after the window closed on deadline day

The Blues had sanctioned the joint-record British transfer of Enzo Fernandez to Manchester City for £125m on deadline day, but did so without having their own replacement at the ready.

Chelsea spent their deadline day chasing Camara, seeing two bids worth £38.5m and £42.9m turned down earlier in the day before having a third accepted.

And Chelsea sources added they had the opportunity to stop Fernandez from joining City after they learned of the U-turn on Camara – but they had given their word to their Premier League counterparts and, unlike Monaco, they honoured it.

Monaco have won their first three Ligue 1 fixtures of the season and sit second to Rennes in the table, with a game in hand, heading into the weekend.

'I can help the team a lot,' the Senegal international Camara added.

'Football moves fast. Maybe other opportunities will come along. But for now, I'm staying focused on the season with Monaco.'

Sports.title: Under-fire Russell Martin hits out at 'personal' attacks following Leicester City's dire results - and opens up on 'difficult' period for loved ones amid widespread criticism: 'I don't know why I upset so many people'
Sports.content:
Under-fire Russell Martin hits out at 'personal' attacks following Leicester City's dire results - and opens up on 'difficult' period for loved ones amid widespread criticism: 'I don't know why I upset so many people'

Leicester City manager Russell Martin said that he feels criticism he has received has 'become really personal' as he opened up on a turbulent start to the season with the League One side.

Leicester were tipped by many to come straight back up to the Championship after suffering back-to-back relegations from the Premier League to League One.

Yet they sit 18th in the third division after their opening five games, with Martin's side notching just one win, two draws and two defeats to leave them at their lowest ever position in the 142-year history of the club.

The Foxes were thrashed 4-0 at home to Oxford United last weekend, leaving Martin's job under intense scrutiny as he faced chants of 'sacked in the morning' from both the travelling and home fans.

In the lead-up to Leicester's match against Stockport on Saturday, Martin - who is married to former glamour model Lucy Pinder - opened up on the criticism and the toll it's taken on his loved ones, saying: 'It has become really personal from some guys in the media and definitely from fans.

'It is what it is, and I have to deal with it. It doesn't affect me too much, genuinely, but it is really difficult for the people around me, who know me and understand me and know what I am.

Martin said: 'I don't know why I upset so many people. One of the players asked me this week why I am so criticised outside of here, because obviously they see stuff, and I can't answer it'

The Leicester boss said the onslaught has been difficult for his loved ones. He is married to former glamour model Lucy Pinder

'I don't know why I upset so many people. One of the players asked me this week why I am so criticised outside of here, because obviously they see stuff, and I can't answer it.'

Martin has been working to implement a possession-heavy style, which is already turning off many fans, while former Foxes forward Matt Piper described it as 'passing teams to death'.

The 40-year-old manager still appears to have the backing of his players, however. Captain Harry Souttar claimed after last weekend's Oxford defeat that it was 'solely' the responsibility of the players.

And 20-year-old defender Jayden Joseph said the squad believes in Martin's philosophy, urging patience from the club's fanbase. 'We need to give it that bit of time for it all to come together,' he said.

Martin said on Friday: 'Speak to the players and people I've worked with, and (then) people who have never seen it and have maybe watched a few clips of some bits, and it's a very different perception from reality.

'But I guess when you try to do something that is a bit different to some, then it's always there to be shot at.'

He also doubled down on his playing style, adding: 'I love what I do, I love my job and love always trying to develop people and players by playing in a way where I think they can bring the best version of themselves.

'Sometimes it takes time. It's not easy, but I will always choose to try to embark on something that I really believe in that focuses on trying to develop whilst winning. And maybe I'm in the wrong job for that.

The Foxes were thrashed 4-0 at home to Oxford United last weekend, leaving Martin's job under intense scrutiny as he faced chants of 'sacked in the morning' from both sets of fans

'There is enough feeling from me and the players I work with that it can be really brilliant at times.

'I always have to keep learning and I spent a long time out of the game after Rangers and spent a lot of time watching different football and trying to sharpen my tools.

'The most frustrating thing is that I've enjoyed the process here so much so far and it's not quite shown with the results, but I'm convinced it will. Otherwise, I wouldn't do it. So ultimately I'll keep doing what I'm doing and hopefully we will be really successful and I really believe we can be.'

Since guiding Southampton to the Premier League via the 2023-24 Championship play-offs, Martin has won only three of his last 28 league matches across two years with three different clubs (Southampton, Rangers and Leicester) for an 11 per cent win ratio.

His time at Scottish giants Rangers saw him win just one of his seven league matches, drawing five and losing the other. Across 17 games in all competitions there, he recorded just five victories.

Sports.title: Keely Hodgkinson hits back at critics as she makes feelings clear on 'high expectations'
Sports.content:
Keely Hodgkinson hits back at critics as she makes feelings clear on 'high expectations'

British track hero Keely Hodgkinson has spoken out over claims she's had an underwhelming season

View 3 Images Keely Hodgkinson has hit back at her critics (Image: 2026 Getty Images)

Keely Hodgkinson has hit back at critics who have suggested she's had a poor season on the track. The 2024 Olympic gold medallist eased into the World Athletics Ultimate Championship 800m final in Budapest, Hungary, on Friday night.

‌



The 24-year-old has endured her difficulties this year. In August, she skipped the final rounds of the Diamond League and the final in Brussels due to hamstring discomfort.

‌



Earlier this year, she stepped away from the 400m final at the UK Athletics Championships due to unexpected muscle tightness. Hodgkinson also suffered a fall during a training session that left her with bruised and cut knees prior to a July race in Eugene, Oregon.

‌



The track star suffered disappointment at the 2026 European Athletics Championships, too. Her rival, Swiss star Audrey Werro, ran a championship-record time of 1:54.81 forcing Hodgkinson to settle for silver.

Speaking after she claimed a place in Saturday night's 800m final, it was put to her that her season is not as disappointing as some are presuming.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Usain Bolt's true thoughts on Ultimate Championship prize money making sprinters richer READ MORE :

Amy Hunt looking to add more titles at inaugural World Athletics Ultimate Championship READ MORE :

"It's not been bad at all," she told Athletics Weekly. "You've got to have perspective. People were saying that two years ago... I know my standards are high and the expectations are very high, and that's okay.

"Sometimes, life doesn't go your way and I'm doing the best with what I've been dealt with but I'm actually really proud. I'm really happy to be here and look forward to tomorrow."

View 3 Images Keely Hodgkinson was happy with her performance in Budapest (Image: 2026 Getty Images)

‌



While slightly below Hodgkinson's lofty standards, her season has been far from all doom and gloom. In February, she improved on her own British 800m record, setting a time of 1:56.33 at the British Indoor Championships. She later eclipsed that time days later, running 1:54.87, in Lievin, France

In March, Hodgkinson won gold in the 800m at the 2026 World Athletics Indoor Championships, the second-fastest indoor time in history. She stormed into the final on Friday night, recording a time of 1:57.57, nearly one full second faster than second-place Addison Wiley.

However, Swiss runner Veronica Vancardo, suffered a brutal tumble during the race after being tripped by Italian star Eloisa Coiro.

‌



View 3 Images There was drama in the Women's 800 Metres Semi-Final first heat as Veronica Vancardo fell (Image: 2026 Getty Images)

Hodgkinson told BBC Sport afterwards: "This season we've had a fair share of people falling over, but she's still got all her teeth so she'll be ok. That's one of my worst nightmares, touchwood it hasn't happened to me so far. She should be okay. It's part of racing unfortunately."

On her performance, she added: "I'm happy with that, I'm glad to be back running. It was a lot of fun. I just wanted to get through and complete it. It's been a month since I last raced so it's nice to get that run out through the legs, hopefully go a bit better tomorrow."

Article continues below

Hodgkinson will have to beat eight competitors if she wants to win in Budapest. Driving her on will be her desire to beat Werro, with the 2026 European champion also set to run in tonight's final.

Sports.title: Man Utd in astonishment over JJ Gabriel after Michael Carrick makes feelings clear
Sports.content:
Man Utd in astonishment over JJ Gabriel after Michael Carrick makes feelings clear

JJ Gabriel has been making waves at Manchester United, with the teenage prodigy scoring a hat-trick in the UEFA Youth League

View 2 Images JJ Gabriel continues to impress at Manchester United and is on the fringes of the first team (Image: (Photo by Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images))

Manchester United are reportedly 'in total shock' at JJ Gabriel's quality the youngster continues his extraordinary rise towards Michael Carrick's first-team squad. The 15-year-old, who frequently trains alongside United's senior players, was handed a chance to showcase his abilities during pre-season.

‌



While the intention is to manage his progression carefully, the club recognise they possess a genuine talent. United are conscious they have 'a real gem on their hands.'

‌



In the build-up to United's Champions League victory over Sabah FK, their Under-19s were competing at the Leigh Training Centre for the UEFA Youth League encounter.

‌



Gabriel maintained his outstanding start to the campaign, netting a hat-trick as the young Red Devils cruised to a 5-0 triumph, and became the youngest United player in history to achieve the feat in the competition.

Bruno Fernandes disclosure about Man Utd training says it all about Marcus Rashford READ MORE :

Speaking on his YouTube channel, Fabrizio Romano said: "It's going to be important to see how Manchester United manage JJ in terms of involving him in the first team in official games.

"That's going to be an important topic because everyone at Manchester United, when they speak about JJ Gabriel, is in total shock at how good this boy is. So obviously, his pathway is going to be absolutely important in order to understand more about JJ."

‌



United have already made the call to elevate Gabriel to the U21s setup this season, and he remains on the periphery of the first-team squad. United supporters are keenly anticipating their first look at the youngster in a competitive fixture for the senior side.

Carrick has been a regular presence at United's youth matches, closely monitoring Gabriel's progression. Speaking last month after observing Gabriel, the Red Devils head coach said: "I really enjoyed the game. You could see the quality.

View 2 Images JJ Gabriel is already making a name for himself aged just 15 (Image: Manchester United/Manchester United via Getty Images)

‌



"JJ is one of the boys. He's obviously got a really big talent. He's trained with us quite a bit and is getting experience all the time. He's physically adapting to each step that he makes, and we're just continuing his development."

The United boss wasn't the only one singing the youngster's praises — U21s manager Adam Lawrence was full of admiration for Gabriel following the UEFA Youth League victory. He told the Manchester Evening News: "Well, I think the first thing in my job is not to ruin him.

"So when you have a talented player like JJ and the other lads of course, you obviously don't want to stifle their freedom and their creativity. And I think essentially what you try and do is to set the team up to allow the talent to function and to play free at the right moments.

‌



"Of course, it can't always be free and off the cuff in terms of some of the off-the-ball responsibilities that he's working on and some of the pressing things that he's thinking about.

"But again, in terms of how he plays properly and how he connects with other teammates at the top end of the pitch, he's just in a real good space. If you look at that game today, I think he's playing properly.

Article continues below

"I think he's trying to do the right things. It's enjoyable working with him and challenging as a coach because the best players challenge you. When you work with talented players you have to find a way to help them and allow them to flourish and keep improving. Of course, there are things that you can keep working on but he is of course in a real good place."

Sports.title: Big Stacks' real name, prison term and explicit videos
Sports.content:
Big Stacks' real name, prison term and explicit videos

Big Stacks will finally get the chance to go head-to-head with rival Jordan McCann as the pair are due to trade leather in Newcastle on Saturday night

View Image Big Stacks speaks ahead of his fight

The 'UK's Hardest Man' - more commonly known as Big Stacks will be looking to pick up his first win under the Misfits Boxing banner on Saturday night.

‌



Stacks will finally settle his rivalrly with Manchester rapper Jordan McCann. The pair clashed in a heated altercation in the build-up to a Misfits event earlier this year. The 'Hardest Man' had been arguing with Tyson Fury's brother shane, before McCann landed a punch that injured Stacks, resulting his fight with Armz Korleone to a body-shots-only contest.

‌



McCann was also competing on the card, and would go on to lose to Ibiza Final Boss in a one-sided affair. After months of trading barbs, both McCann and Stacks will finally trade leather in the ring. And so, here is everything you need to know about the 'UK's Hardest Man'...

‌



Who is Big Stacks and what is his real name?

Despite being known as Big Stack or the 'UK's Hardest Man,' his real name is Charlie Robert. The 33-year-old internet personality has made a name for himself as of late in the world of social media. Robert, 33, is best known for his work on Kick as a live streamer and has amassed millions of views on the platform.

His nickname stemmed from him messing around, proclaiming himself as the 'Hardest Man' in the UK, and while it was merely a joke, people and professional fighters took it seriously and began challenging him. Due to the attention he got, Stacks decided to run with it and stick with the label.

After building quite the brand as a internet personality, he transitioned his fame into influencer boxing, signing with Misfits. He made his debut in a comical 'bodyshots only' contest against Armz Korleone earlier this year, but would go on to lose via TKO in the fourth stanza.

‌

Big Stacks' criminal history

From a young age, Robert found himself getting into trouble as he was heavily involved in street gangs and carrying out robberies. Despite first getting locked up at the age of 12, Stacks revealed to All Out Fighting that he first started getting 'nicked' at the age of 10.

The 33-year-old grew up on a council estate surrounded by violence and into a life of crime early on. Throughout his life so far, he has been arrested around 60 times, serving separate sentences for various crimes.

‌



Discussing how he spent his teenage years, Stacks revealed to All Out Fighting: "Just in jail. I got involved in gangs. And I was just in and out of jail. It was normal for me. Because I used to love fighting, I was always getting done for assaults, GBH's. For me, in and out of jail was my second home."

In his early 20s, Robert was handed a 13-year prison sentence for a serious violent assault where he attacked a man with a baseball bat and broke his kneecaps. The incident originated from a dispute involving drug dealing and a suspected setup.

Recalling the incident, he said: "I was involved with gangs. I had some beef with some other drug dealer. He's pulled up on me with a baseball bat. He tried doing me with the bat, dropped the bat and drove off. We chased after him. I thought I had been set up by the geezer I done. So, in my mind, I think 'how the f*** did this other geezer knew who was there at the same time

"We called the geezer and were gonna meet for a deal. And I ended up battering him. Could have got it wrong. In my head, I did get it wrong, but at that night, I genuinely thought he set me up. I was intoxicated, just jumped out and battered a kid. Obviously, I regret it."

His history with adult site OnlyFans

Not long after his release from prison, Stacks opted to set up an OnlyFans page and create content. The 33-year-old has openly admitted he set up the account and used the platform as a quick way to make money following his long stint behind bars. Robert revealed he would film explicit content with women and publicly release it to his followers on the site.
