2 adults + 3 kids R420

HOUSEKEEPEING RULES

Hubbly can be rented on-site.

No firearms.

No illicit or Illegal drugs.

Snacks for kids are permitted.

Only plain gazebos and umbrellas are allowed: no branded ones.

Camp chairs and picnic blankets allowed.

All children from the age of 1 – 10 must register their parents’ details on tags and registration forms at the gate.

PayShap will be accessible through all vendors, and cardless payment

options will also be available.

World.title: Danny Jordaan re-elected as SAFA president
World.content:
MIDRAND – Following weeks of campaigning, the the SAFA presidency race has ended with the re-election of Danny Jordaan.

At the age of 75, Jordaan secured a fourth term and outdid his opponent, Sandile Zungu.

Zungu, the AmaZulu chairperson, went toe-to-toe with Jordaan, wanting to unseat him after three terms at the helm of South African football.

Jordaan received 157 votes while Zungu received 82.

His re-election comes amid reports of death threats, harassment and intimidation targeting delegates ahead of the vote.

Security was tightened at the congress venue in Midrand.

Members are also voting for the national executive committee and provincial leadership.

FIFA, CAF, COSAFA and SASCOC representatives are among those attending.

World.title: Steve Biko remembered 49 years on
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Today, 49 years ago, South Africa lost a man widely regarded as a son of the soil.

Steven Biko died from severe brain damage suffered from days of beatings at the hands of the apartheid police.

His legacy, however, lives on.

Those who remember him as a revolutionary leader are also reminded of his humble beginnings in the Eastern Cape.

Biko was born in Tarkastad, Eastern Cape, in 1946.

But it was in Qonce, formerly known as King Williams Town, where he touched the hearts and minds of many people through community upliftment programmes.

Lindiwe Tyamzashe-Ngcukana, a resident, said they still benefit from Biko’s efforts, years later.

"We have a clinic that has a doctor, and we stay nearby. For us it was very important. We even have a garden where locals are employed and many others received jobs at the clinic that Bantu Biko built."

Biko’s son Nkosinathi also reflected on his father.

“Time is everything in this process, for reasons we know, including age and so forth.

So, it has always mattered to us to have a process driven by rogue and the intent to account to this nation on the issue of the murder of Steve Biko.

“Just to measure time, this man (his brother Samora) was two years old when our father died.

He's the man on my mother's lap with the bottle and in tears with the picture that touched the world."

World.title: 1787 firearms removed from circulation
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - More than 1,000 firearms seized in Lesotho have been destroyed in a joint operation between SAPS, and the Kingdom's police.

The operation forms part of African Amnesty Month and the AU’s Silencing the Guns initiative.

Police said the cross-border cooperation will help tackle crimes including trafficking, stock theft and vehicle theft.

The latest destruction follows the disposal of nearly 12 thousand firearms by the SAPS two months ago.

Authorities say removing illegal weapons from circulation is key to preventing them from ending up back in the hands of criminals.

World.title: SA’s cybercrime laws put to the test amid capacity concerns
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - South Africa’s extradition of six Nigerian nationals to the US shows its cybercrime laws in action.

The Hawks and Interpol apprehended the group for alleged involvement in an online love scam where dozens of US women were defrauded of more than R100 million.

One expert warns that while the laws exist, a lack of human resources to address the issue remains a concern.

Jason Jordaan, a cybercrime investigator, said South Africa has exceptional legislation.

“In fact, I'd like to almost postulate that our legislation is probably superior to some of the legislation I see in countries like Europe and the United States as far as cybercrime goes. But I think the big difference is, like I said, it comes down to capacity. We struggle with capacity in this particular regard.

“Oftentimes, when we do build up capacity within the government sector, it gets poached to the private sector where salaries are significantly higher sometimes in this regard. And I think that costs us in the long run. But I don't think as a country we need to step back from a legislative point of view in terms of our ability to deal with this."

World.title: Parliament trespasser arrested
World.content:
CAPE TOWN - Cape Town police have opened a trespassing case against a 34-year-old man found in the Parliament yard.

The man jumped over the fence on Thursday night and fell asleep.

Authorities found him on Friday morning and apprehended him.

The suspect will appear in court on Monday on trespassing charges.

Parliament's building is currently undergoing repairs after a 2022 fire.

World.title: SAFA Congress underway
World.content:
MIDRAND - The wait is almost over!

The South African Football Association Elective Congress is set to be an interesting one.

Incumbent president, Danny Jordaan, will battle it out with AmaZulu chairperson Sandile Zungu.

Jordaan has been calling the shots at SAFA House since he was elected in 2013.

Since he succeeded Kirsten Nematandani and defeated Mandla Mazibuko, the 75-year-old has held the position for three terms.

However, he is up against a confident man in Zungu, who believes he has what it takes to unseat him.

Saturday's congress will see 265 members cast their votes, with 208 of those votes coming from 52 regions.

World.title: Four arrested for driver’s licence fraud
World.content:
THOHOYANDOU - Police in Limpopo have arrested four suspects involved in a cash-for-driver’s licence scheme.

The group had allegedly been operating at the Marble Hall Licence Testing Centre in Limpopo.

The syndicate is alleged to have fast-tracked bulk transactions involving between 20 and 30 learner licences at a time, bypassing lawful licensing procedures.

One suspect was found in possession of several learner’s licences.

Two cashiers, 63-year-old and 53-year-old women, were found with cash.

They face charges of fraud, corruption and contravention of the Cyber Act for tampering with the eNatis system.

World.title: Bafana Mahungela case puts self-representation in the spotlight
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - An accused person who chooses to represent themselves can not expect the court to play the role of their attorney.

These are the words of legal expert Ayanda Gwabeni, who explains how courts remain neutral in the matter .

Gwabeni's comments come after Bafana Mahungela was convicted for the murder of Kirsten Kluyts.

The pregnant teacher's body was discovered after a run at the George Lea Park in Sandton back in 2023.

In the Johannesburg High Court on Friday, Mahungela questioned whether his rights had been adequately protected during the trial.

He told the court how he chose to represent himself under the "care" of the court, but now questions that processes after he was found guilty of all charges.

The 23-year-old was found guilty of kidnapping, robbery with aggravating circumstances, murder, and attempted rape.

The post-mortem revealed that Kluyts died from blunt force trauma to the head and strangulation.

Kluyts was 14 weeks pregnant at the time of her murder.

Gwabeni said the courts roles are limited in such instances. He explained how the court cannot cross-examine witnesses for the accused and that their duty remains to guard against unfairness.

"The court is neutral in the matter. The only duty of the court is to guard against unfairness, it cannot go further than that," he said.

Gwabeni said all accused persons are given three options when it comes to representation in court.

"They are advised they can hire a private attorney of their choosing, use the state-provided services through Legal Aid or they can represent themselves."

He said that while it is not advisable for anyone to represent themselves in these kinds of matters, the court can not force anyone to take legal representation.

"The law is acquired over time. An attorney is expected to have skill an ordinary member of the public may not have. They also have the know-how that ordinary members of the public may not have.

"Accused persons cannot rely on the court to do the job of an attorney on their behalf."

Sentencing proceedings have been set for 27 October.

World.title: Matiang'i, Ndindi Nyoro team up in fresh push for opposition unity
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Jubilee Party Presidential candidate Fred Matiang'i and People’s Party of Kenya leader Ndindi Nyoro at an SDA Church service at Kangema Empowerment Centre Hall,Murang'a. [Boniface Gikandi, Standard]

Jubilee Party deputy leader Fred Matiang’i and People’s Party of Kenya (PPK) leader Ndindi Nyoro have stepped up calls for opposition leaders to unite ahead of the 2027 General Election, saying Kenyans want a team capable of addressing the country’s development challenges.

Matiang’i and Nyoro shared a platform in Kangema, Murang’a County, where they called for the opposition to set aside differences and work together to offer Kenyans an alternative political leadership.

The two spoke during a Seventh-day Adventist Church service at Kangema Empowerment Centre Hall, less than 200 metres from the homestead of the late John Michuki, whom they described as a respected statesman and mentor to many leaders.

Nyoro said opposition leaders needed to come together and focus on issues affecting Kenyans, rather than pursuing individual interests. He introduced Matiang’i as his personal friend and said the two leaders’ appearance together demonstrated the need for greater unity within the opposition.

He said Kenyans were looking for leaders who were not self-centred but committed to improving their living standards.

“My presence in Kangema with Dr Matiang’i is a testimony that opposition leaders will come together and focus on post August next year,” said Nyoro, adding that PPL leader Martha Karua and Peter Munya were part of the team.

Matiang’i, who served as Interior Cabinet Secretary, called on opposition leaders to unite and bring Kenyans together ahead of the next election.

He said he admired Michuki and had followed in his footsteps at the Ministry of Interior, adding that he had the capacity to help develop the country.

“Let's stop name-calling, and all the leaders in the united opposition in DCP, Linda Mwanchi, PPL, PPK should come together and chart the way forward,” said Matiang’i.

Former Murang’a Senator Kembi Gitura said the appearance of Matiang’i and Nyoro together demonstrated unity of purpose and a desire to bring Kenyans together.

“The presence of Matiang’i and Ndindi was big news nationally when they sat away from Nairobi chatting about the destiny of the nation,” said Kembi, a director of elections at Jubilee Party.

Nyamira Senator Okong’o Omogeni said Kenyans were being weighed down by the high cost of living and needed to focus on electing credible leaders.

Gitura also said he was proud to have inherited Kiharu’s political legacy from former Cabinet minister Gikonyo Kiano and former presidential candidate Kenneth Matiba, whom he said had contributed significantly to the country.

“Now Ndindi Nyoro is my MP and has ambitions similar to those of Matiba, eyeing

The meeting was attended by Omogeni, Borabu MP Patrick Osero, Kitutu Masaba MP Clive Gisairo and Murang’a Jubilee Party chairman Peter Kimari.

World.title: ODM vows not to interfere with Linda Mwananchi rally in Nairobi
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Linda Mwananchi leaders during a rally in Western Kenya. [Linda Mwananchi, X]

The Orange Democratic Movement (ODM) has said it will not disrupt the planned Linda Mwananchi rally scheduled for Sunday at Jacaranda Grounds.

In a statement on Friday, September 11, ODM Nairobi Chairman George Aladwa said the party had no business interfering with the rally, noting that Linda Mwananchi had a right to speak to Nairobi residents.

“I want to make it clear that nobody in ODM has any intention of disrupting or interfering with the Linda Mwananchi rally,” Aladwa stated.

He added: “We believe that political competition should be about ideas, policies and the ability to convince Kenyans, rather than confrontations between supporters of different political formations.”

Aladwa said ODM’s opponents had a right to tell Nairobi residents what they stood for and what they intended to offer Kenyans.

“The people are intelligent enough to listen to different political messages and make their own decisions,” Aladwa said.

At the same time, Aladwa said ODM was engaged in an extensive programme to market and strengthen the party across Nairobi as it prepared for activities to commemorate the anniversary of the death of its former party leader, the late Raila Amolo Odinga.

The chairman lauded Odinga for his contribution to Kenya’s democracy, the struggle for constitutional reforms and the political transformation of the country, saying his contribution could not be erased.

“His legacy remains an important part of ODM and Kenya’s political history. As we approach the 2027 General Election, our responsibility is to ensure that ODM remains strong, organised and firmly rooted across Nairobi,” the chairman stated.

“We will continue engaging residents in all constituencies and wards and explaining the party’s agenda to the people. I appeal to ODM supporters to remain calm and focused. Do not allow yourselves to be provoked into unnecessary political confrontations,” he added.

World.title: Ndindi Nyoro tells Ruto to keep off Tata Chemicals
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

PPK leader Ndindi Nyoro addresses a rally at Nambale market in Busia on August 30, 2026. [Benjamin Sakwa, Standard]

Kiharu MP Ndindi Nyoro has cautioned President William Ruto against meddling in the affairs of Tata Chemicals, Africa’s largest soda ash plant in Lake Magadi, Kajiado County.

Nyoro, who is the Peoples’ Party of Kenya leader, has accused President Ruto of an alleged plot to take control of Tata Chemicals through a shareholding scheme.

He said Ruto’s directive on Tata Chemicals closure raises concerns over the future of multinational firms and their operations in the country.

Speaking during a tour of Wote, Makueni County, on Thursday, Nyoro termed the Head of State’s move selfish, saying even if he had since softened his stance on the firm, it remains wanting for investors.

“His utterances were and remain wanting for external and internal investors. We don’t want investors to work in a bad political environment. Even if he seems to have made a U-turn on the matter, we are aware he has been pushing to be a shareholder in the company. We don’t want investors to be interfered with politically because we must create an environment where our people have access to job opportunities. It is almost reaching a catastrophic level in terms of lack of jobs for our people,” he said

The PPK leader warned that the country is in a bad economic state with a Sh13.5 trillion debt that is projected to grow further by next year.

“When Ruto exits next year the debt will be more than Sh15 trillion. The next president, who will be coming from the opposition, will have hard times in running this country. For every Sh100 that will be collected as tax from 2028, Sh91 will be used to repay government debts. We should not have time now to fight as opposition and also as Kenyans. We must hold hands and send the president back home because of his failures,” Nyoro said.

The MP urged opposition leaders to put aside their political differences and unite behind a single presidential candidate ahead of the 2027 General Election, saying that a united opposition would have a better chance of defeating President Ruto.

“If the opposition wants to defeat President Ruto, they must come together and present one presidential candidate. I am ready to talk to all the opposition principals,” Nyoro said.

Nyoro also outlined a raft of proposals he says could help revive Kenya’s economy and ease the financial burden on ordinary citizens.

Among his proposals is the use of the National Social Security Fund (NSSF) to strengthen the health sector. He argued that Kenyans should be able to access quality healthcare without being forced to bear the full cost of medical services.

Nyoro further proposed changes to the way education is financed, suggesting that bursaries currently administered through the National Government Constituencies Development Fund (NG-CDF) and county governments be channelled towards financing free primary and secondary education.

He said such an approach would create a more uniform education financing system and ensure that children from poor households are not disadvantaged because of their parents' inability to meet school-related expenses.

Nyoro's proposals come amid growing debate over the country's economic direction, the cost of living, access to healthcare and the financing of education.

World.title: Mama Tutam acquitted of Sh25m fraud, says Nigerian tycoon cost her marriage
World.content:
Nairobi Woman Representative aspirant Faith Mwikali Ndiwa, alias Faith Nguthu addresses journalists at the Milimani Law Courts in Nairobi on September 9, 2026. [David Gichuru, Standard]

A Nairobi Woman Representative aspirant has confessed the frustrations and embarrassment that befell her after befriending a wealthy Nigerian businessman who later accused her of defrauding him of Sh25 million.

Faith Mwikali Ndiwa, alias Faith Nguthu, popularly known as Mama Tutam, said she was kicked out of her marriage after the father of her three children discovered reports linking her to an alleged love affair with Nigerian investor Jude Olabayo Veracruz.

World.title: Sifuna hits back at Ruto over opposition agenda
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna promised to introduce austerity measures if the opposition takes power.

Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna has hit back at President William Ruto after the Head of State accused the united opposition of lacking a clear policy agenda ahead of the 2027 General Election.

Speaking in the Senate, Sifuna, who has been fronted as a potential presidential candidate in the coming elections, said the opposition’s immediate plan was to restore meritocracy in government and remove Ruto from power.

Sifuna also questioned government spending, citing claims that Sh12 billion had been spent on hospitality at State House at a time when the country was facing financial constraints.

“We are being told that Sh12 billion was spent on hospitality at State House, in a country where we are told we have no cash for capitation. So those of you who ask us for a plan, ours is to send you home,” Sifuna said.

The senator further promised to introduce austerity measures if the opposition takes power, arguing that government spending could be streamlined to free up resources for essential services.

“I believe in the first 100 days after we kick this government out, we should be able to cut out the fat that is being utilised at State House so that we can pay our teachers and fund our hospitals,” he said.

Sifuna’s remarks came a day after Ruto accused opposition leaders of using ethnic profiling and intimidation to influence voters in areas perceived to be opposition strongholds.

Speaking in Ngong and Ongata Rongai in Kajiado County, Ruto defended the broad-based UDA-ODM political arrangement, saying the pact was aimed at promoting national unity and ensuring equitable distribution of national resources.

“They are intimidating people along ethnic lines, telling them they must vote a certain way. Do not allow yourselves to be divided through tribalism and hatred. Their agenda is to spread tribalism and hatred,” Ruto said.

The exchange comes as political parties and leaders intensify preparations for the 2027 General Election, with the opposition seeking to consolidate its support base while the Kenya Kwanza administration defends its record and broad-based political arrangement.

World.title: Centum taps insider as Mworia exits after nearly two decades
World.content:
Centum Investment Company PLC acting Group Chief Executive Thomas Omondi-Achola. [Courtesy]

Centum Investment Company PLC has appointed Thomas Omondi-Achola as acting group chief executive, tapping an internal candidate to succeed long-serving CEO James Mworia, who is leaving to head Kenya’s newly established National Infrastructure Fund (NIF).

The transition, effective immediately, marks the end of an 18-year tenure during which Mworia transformed Centum from a small investment firm into East Africa’s largest diversified investment platform, the company said in a statement.

World.title: Ruto: Kenya to end raw mineral exports
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto during a thanksgiving service in South Horr, Samburu County on September 6, 2026. [PCS]

President William Ruto says Kenya will no longer allow its mineral wealth to leave the country in raw form, coming days after the controversial saga surrounding Tata Chemicals’ operations at Lake Magadi.

Ruto defended the government’s decision to suspend Tata Chemicals’ operations at Lake Magadi, Kajiado County, arguing that Kenya has not been receiving sufficient value from the natural resource and that more investors should be given an opportunity to develop the area.

“We want to give five, six or even 10 companies an opportunity to use the resources there to create jobs, value, create wealth and reduce poverty,” Ruto said.

The President made the remarks during a thanksgiving service in South Horr, Samburu County, on Sunday, where he announced a broader government policy aimed at shifting Kenya from exporting raw materials to processing them locally.

“Going into the future, our position as the government. Whether we are talking about Magadi Soda or oil or all our minerals, we have taken the decision that we will no longer export raw materials,” Ruto said.

“We are going to process all minerals available in Kenya.”

The declaration puts the long-running Lake Magadi dispute at the centre of a much wider economic strategy.

Tata Chemicals has been associated with soda ash production at the lake for more than a century. Its Kenyan operations trace their history to 1911, when the Magadi Soda Company began extracting trona from Lake Magadi.

Operations were suspended on July 28, 2026, following a directive from the Ministry of Mining, Blue Economy and Maritime Affairs over compliance and licensing issues.

Ruto has argued that the resource should generate greater benefits for Kenyans through expanded investment, job creation and local value addition.

He accused the existing model of allowing valuable resources to leave the country while Kenya receives less economic benefit than it could.

The President’s comments reflect a longstanding challenge facing Kenya’s extractive sector: how to turn mineral deposits into manufacturing opportunities rather than simply exporting commodities.

Under the proposed approach, minerals such as gold, limestone, iron ore, graphite, titanium and soda ash would be processed or refined in Kenya before being exported.

The government says this would create industrial jobs, strengthen local supply chains and increase the value of exports.

Ruto cited planned cooperation with Nigerian businessman Aliko Dangote as an example of the investment model the government wants to pursue.

He said talks were underway to establish an oil refinery and petrochemical complex in Lamu, alongside efforts to attract investors into mineral refining.

“It is imprudent for any government to export raw materials, create jobs and value in other countries while we have a big population of young people who need jobs,” Ruto said.

World.title: Sifuna condemns abduction of Standard Group Associate Editor
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Busia County Senator Okiya Omtata, Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna, Bumula MP Jack Wamboka during the burial service of Mary Gorreti Okiya at Kabula, in Bumula on September 5,2026. [Benjamin Sakwa, Standard]

Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna has declared that the fight to restore democracy, media freedom and the rule of law following the abduction of Standard Group Senior Editor will form the centrepiece of the Linda Mwananchi government vowing to defeat President William Ruto in the 2027 General Election.

Sifuna accused President Ruto’s administration of undermining constitutional freedoms and creating an atmosphere of fear, saying the country must be returned to what he described as “the rail of the six important values” enshrined in the Constitution.

Speaking in Bumula Constituency, Kakamega County during the burial of Mary Goreti, the sister of Busia Senator Okiya Omtatah, Sifuna strongly condemned the abduction and arrest of a Standard Group Associate Editor, Alex Kiprotich, arguing that journalists must be protected if Kenya is to remain a democratic country.

“It is impossible that you are driving on the road and you are taken away the way the way the Standard Group Journaliat and Editor Alex Kiprotich was taken. Kenyans want to live in a free country. We do not want to live in fear,” said Sifuna.

He questioned the circumstances surrounding the incident and accused the Government of failing to protect media freedom, adding that the Linda Mwananchi movement would seek to restore institutions and constitutional safeguards if elected to power, arguing that democracy could not survive where citizens, journalists and political opponents lived in fear.

"You cannot just arrest a senior journalist in the middle of the road with police carrying firearms, then you dump him some 500kilometres near the dam, a country cannot have democracy if media is not being respected and allowed to do it's work as per the constitution," said Sifuna.

He said the movement’s agenda was not merely about removing the current administration from power but it's main plan is rebuilding systems of governance around constitutionalism, democracy, individual freedoms and the rule of law.

“With less than 11 months remaining, we want to tell Kenyans that our entire plan is to return this country to the rails of the six important values contained in our Constitution, including democracy, freedom of citizens and the rule of law,” said Sifuna.

Sifuna also accused the Government of using threats against political opponents, saying leaders should not threaten citizens with arrest, expulsion or other forms of intimidation.

He challenged religious leaders to remind politicians that the power to determine the length of a person's life belongs to God.

Sifuna further linked the rule of law to economic growth, warning that investors would be reluctant to establish businesses in Kenya if government could arbitrarily order them to leave.

He said Kenya could not rely on government alone to create employment for millions of young people, arguing that the country needed both local and foreign investors.

“No investor can bring his project to a country where he can wake up one day and the President tells him, ‘Pack and go.’ It is impossible,” Sifuna said.

He argued that investor confidence was also affected by the possibility of commercial disputes being referred to foreign jurisdictions because investors lacked confidence in Kenya’s legal system.

Sifuna also criticised the government over the ongoing nurses and midwives strike, saying the rule of law required the State to honour agreements signed with workers.

World.title: Saudi oil pipeline shut down after attack triggers fires
World.content:
Saudi Arabia has shut down a key oil pipeline after it was attacked by drones from Iraq, as repercussions of the Iran war widen.

The development is more bad news for the Saudi government after the Iran-backed Houthis captured strategic points along the Red Sea, bringing them close to controlling the Bab al-Mandeb Strait, a critical energy route.

Saudi Arabia’s Ministry of Energy confirmed in a statement posted to its website Friday that the pipeline had been attacked and “was shut down as a precautionary measure.”

Two US officials familiar with the matter earlier said the pipeline system in Saudi Arabia was struck by projectiles on Thursday,

An early analysis found that pump stations, which are located next to the pipeline itself, were hit, one of the US officials said. A satellite image taken Friday appears to show extensive fire damage at one pumping station, and an image of a different pumping station, taken Thursday, showed a small fire sending up plumes of thick, black smoke.

It was not immediately clear who was responsible for the strikes or if sections of the pipeline itself were damaged.

US President Donald Trump said Iran was likely behind the attack on Saudi Arabia that shut down the pipeline, when asked about the incident by a reporter during a visit to Ireland.

“I think they are, probably they are,” Trump told journalists in Dublin.

Responding to a question about the fresh concerns in Saudi Arabia following the closure of the pipeline, and whether he could help move marine traffic through the Strait of Hormuz in light of the developments, Trump said everything will “work out fine.”

The Saudi Ministry of Foreign Affairs later released a statement condemning “the attack on the East-West Pipeline in the Riyadh and Madinah regions by several drones coming from Iraq, which resulted in injuries and some damage that is currently being addressed.”

The statement said they would not respond at this point to allow the Iraqi government space to react.

The strike and the Huthi advances signal that the kingdom’s oil resources — and its ability to export those resources — are facing increasing threats as the Iran War continues.

Satellite images appear to show extensive fire damage at a pumping station near Al Mesba’ah, Saudi Arabia. Airbus, Planet Labs

It was not immediately clear how long it would take to repair the damage to the pipeline system, sources said.

The Ministry of Energy statement said that the pipeline “was subjected to multiple attacks” on Thursday that “resulted in a number of injuries.” The statement added that teams were “taking the necessary measures to secure the pipeline and assess its safety.”

The Iraqi government put out a statement later Friday condemning the attacks, saying it had ordered an urgent investigation into those responsible and said it will not allow its territory or airspace to be used for attacks.

“The Iraqi government condemns the attacks that targeted the brotherly Kingdom of Saudi Arabia and affirms its rejection of any attack that undermines the Kingdom’s security and stability or harms the deep-rooted fraternal relations between the two countries,” the statement carried by state-run news agency INA said.

On Saturday, Iraqi security authorities said the country has closed a number of its borders as a precautionary measure following recent events.

Prices under pressure

This week oil prices surged past $100 a barrel amid sharp swings driven by events in the Middle East.

The Saudi Arabian oil giant Aramco did not respond to a request for comment. The State Department and the White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment. US Central Command declined to comment on the incident.

A satellite image shows a small fire burning at a pumping station near Al Dhekra, Saudi Arabia, on September 10, 2026. Planet Labs

Though the source of the attack was unclear, Iran-allied militia groups in Iraq have used drones in the past to attack Saudi Arabia, according to Behnam Ben Taleblu, Iran program senior director at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies (FDD), and may have done so again amid a broader Iranian strategy to use its proxies to push Arab nations to reject American forces in the region.

In late July, Saudi Defense Minister Khalid bin Salman met with US President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance in Washington, DC, to convey the Kingdom’s assessment on the ongoing US war with Iran – that Iran would seek to create leverage through escalation and would try to make use of its remaining proxies – militias in Iraq and the Houthis – to do so, sources told CNN.

Satellites detected nine large fires burning close to Saudi Arabia’s East-West pipeline on Thursday, though the locations of at least six of the fires appeared to correspond to flare pits, where oil and gas can be burned off in the event of an emergency.

The pipeline has become key to Saudi Arabia since the outbreak of the US-Iran war. The kingdom has rerouted about 5 million barrels of oil per day that would have been destined for awaiting oil tankers in the Persian Gulf, as Iran effectively shuttered the Strait of Hormuz. Instead, that oil has traveled through its East-West pipeline to its port of Yanbu on the Red Sea.

With Houthi fighters declaring they would target any Saudi ships attempting to pass through Bab al-Mandeb out of the Red Sea, that outlet for the kingdom’s oil could also be at risk.

Repairing pump stations could be less burdensome than repairing major damage to the pipeline itself, said US officials and experts.

The strike on the pipeline system also comes as Saudi Arabia reported to OPEC that its production of crude oil plunged last month, sinking to the lowest levels since 1990.

CNN’s Jennifer Hansler and Nadeen Ebrahim contributed to this report.

World.title: Ukraine is fighting Russia anywhere it can – even in the deserts of Africa
World.content:
The conditions are grueling. Temperatures regularly soar above 110 degrees Fahrenheit during the day, then drop sharply overnight. Water is scarce and the dust and sand get everywhere. But at least they are working above ground. This elite group of Ukrainian drone operators has spent years hunting Russians from dugouts in Ukraine. They are still doing the same – but in the desert in northern Mali.

Some 15 Ukrainian specialists have been deployed to the junta-led country in Africa’s Sahel region to assist local rebel forces who are fighting Russian troops – part of Kyiv’s mission to weaken its enemy wherever it operates. And Kyiv has also branched out to other theaters of conflict, capitalizing on its hard-won expertise in drone warfare to forge new anti-Russian partnerships.

Speaking to Ukrainian soldiers and officers involved in operations in Mali and Libya, CNN can reveal for the first time the extent of these operations on other continents. A Ukrainian Defense Intelligence source with knowledge of the operations told CNN that several Ukrainian specialists were also stationed in Sudan and that troops from Chad, Niger and Burkina Faso had previously traveled to Mali to receive drone training from Ukrainian soldiers there.

When Iran began striking US allies in the Middle East earlier this year, Ukraine sent teams of military experts to at least five countries in the Middle East. They spent several weeks teaching local forces how to take down the Iranian-made Shahed drones which Russia has been using to terrorize Ukraine for several years. One Ukrainian soldier who was deployed to the United Arab Emirates told CNN they were operating in combined teams with local troops driving alongside them and mirroring their every move.

In exchange for sharing its know-how, Kyiv received an array of security cooperation agreements and promises of ammunition.

In the Sahel, a vast semi-arid region to the south of the Sahara Desert, the situation is more complicated.

Thousands of Malian gather to celebrate the departure of French antiterrorist operation Barkhane, in Bamako, Mali, on February 19, 2022. Paul Lorgerie/For The Washington Post/Getty Images

Russia has been trying to assert itself as a power player in Africa, especially in the mineral-rich, coup-prone Sahel region. It has tried to fill the security void left by the withdrawal of French and other Western forces in recent years, propping up governments in exchange for cash and lucrative mining rights.

At first, the Kremlin outsourced these operations to the Wagner Group, a private military company owned by entrepreneurial warlord Yevgeny Prigozhin. After Prigozhin’s death following his attempted coup in 2023, Moscow merged what remained of Wagner with its regular military, creating the Africa Corps, which deploys in support of Moscow’s local allies.

‘Serious adaptation’

The Ukrainian group in Mali is embedded with a separatist group that calls itself the Azawad Liberation Front and is composed mostly of northern Tuareg rebels. They are not directly involved in the frontline fighting but provide the rebels with support, training and operational help, two Ukrainians deployed there told CNN.

“I coordinate their operations remotely. The signal from their drone comes to me over the internet, and I immediately tell them via radio what to do and where to fly,” one of the Ukrainian drone operators currently in Mali told CNN.

“They go out on missions, then return to me, and we go over every detail of their actions. I don’t go out to the front lines myself — that was a direct order from my superiors,” he said.

An undated photograph provided by the French Army shows three Russian mercenaries in northern Mali. French Army/AP

Russia has previously accused Ukraine of participating in massacres against civilians in Mali – an accusation Kyiv has denied. Separately, rights group Human Rights Watch released two reports over the summer accusing Russian troops in Mali of killing civilians, and another report that said that “all parties” directly engaged in the conflict unlawfully attacked civilians during a flare-up in violence in April. The report did not mention Ukraine.

Asked about the allegations last month, Russia’s Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov told reporters the Africa Corps “operates strictly within the bounds of legality” and “in response to official requests from the legitimate governments of African states.”

The Ukrainian Defense Intelligence source told CNN the point of the overseas deployments is to put pressure on Russia and undermine the notion that Moscow can be a reliable ally. “We are turning our experience in the field of (drones) into a foreign policy tool,” the source said.

But he said the mission is also beneficial to the Ukrainians because it gives them a chance to test their equipment and skills in a completely different environment – and to show partners their methods work everywhere.

“Dust and heat cause equipment to fail faster. Filters, cooling, electronics protection, batteries… everything works differently (and) requires serious adaptation,” he said, adding that even the way the war is fought is vastly different.

“In Ukraine, it’s high intensity, massive strikes, constant pressure. Here it’s more of a maneuverable war over large territories, ambushes, route control, working in small groups and depending on knowledge of the terrain.”

Soldiers from the National Front for the Liberation of Azawad (FLA) patrol the streets of Kidal in northern Mali, on May 8, 2026. AFP/Getty Images

Differences in discipline and training require adaptation on both sides, he said, adding: “We teach them tactics; they teach us to survive and fight.”

Russia is also using its operations in Africa to expand and adapt its military technology. Just this week, the state-owned weapons exporter, Rosoboronexport, presented new missiles and drones at the El Alamein International Airshow in Egypt, with the agency’s chief telling the Russian state news agency TASS these weapons are “proven” for combat in Africa and the Middle East.

Growing confidence

The Ukrainian contingents are small, but they are a sign of Ukraine’s growing confidence that its drone expertise has elevated its global status.

Héni Nsaibia, West Africa senior analyst at Armed Conflict Location & Event Data (ACLED), an independent conflict monitor, told CNN that Mali is one of the countries where Russia now plays a crucial role.

“They provide an essential lifeline to the regime,” he said, adding that Africa Corps forces have been “instrumental in preventing a more profound collapse, and possibly even the fall of the regime.”

“But (the Russians) also need this military regime in place in order to be able to stay in Mali,” Nsaibia added.

The first allegations that Ukraine was helping the Tuaregs came in 2024. In July that year, the rebels ambushed and killed dozens of Wagner fighters and Malian soldiers near the town of Tinzaouaten, on the border with Algeria.

An Azawad Liberation Front soldier walks near damaged infrastructure at the former Africa Corps barracks at Camp 2 in Kidal on May 11, 2026. AFP/Getty Images

Andriy Yusov, the spokesperson for Ukraine’s Defense Intelligence, said at the time that the rebels received “necessary information” to fight the Russians. And while Ukraine later denied any substantial cooperation with the rebels, Yusov’s comment prompted a backlash from the military juntas of Mali, Niger and Burkina Faso, who lodged an official complaint with the United Nations Security Council, accusing Ukraine of sponsoring terrorists.

CNN asked Defense Intelligence for comment for this article and was referred to earlier comments made by officials.

The drone operator told CNN that Ukrainians also assisted rebels in the takeover of the strategic northern Mali town of Kidal earlier this year. The Tuareg rebels and militants linked to al Qaeda launched simultaneous attacks against the Russian troops, forcing them to withdraw. The Russian Defense Ministry accused Kyiv of playing a role in the attack, saying in a statement that “Ukrainian and European mercenary instructors” trained the rebels before the assault.

Nsaibia said the Kidal takeover marked a key defeat for the Malian regime – and the Russian troops that have been propping it up.

“It was a major setback that they lost Kidal and had to negotiate a safe corridor to be able to withdraw,” he told CNN. However, Nsaibia said that the situation could have been much worse for the Malian regime, had it not been for the assistance of Russia’s Africa Corps.

‘Attacked by the same idiots’

The attack in Kidal highlighted the massive difference drones can make on the battlefield in Mali and elsewhere in the Sahel, where war still tends to be fought in more traditional ways, using infantry troops equipped with rudimentary weapons.

The Ukrainians in Mali told CNN the partnership with the Tuareg is one of convenience, not necessarily conviction.

“Culture and religion are different, but when you are being attacked by the same idiots, ideological differences fade into the background,” the Defense Intelligence source said.

Ukraine’s former spy chief, Kyrylo Budanov, pictured in 2025, this week praised its Defense Intelligence for protecting the country’s interests around the world, from “Russia to Africa, in a suit and in camouflage.” Andrew Kravchenko/Bloomberg/Getty Images

The drone operator told CNN that his personal opinions and feelings are irrelevant.

He described some of the rebels as “radicals” who are prone to spontaneously shoot in the air and act in “disruptive ways.”

“Sometimes it’s emotionally hard to ignore certain things. It just so happens that we’re on the same side of the barricades right now… if these guys go on to successfully beat the Russians, we’ll be more than happy to train them,” he told CNN.

He believes any operation that weakens the Russians can help Ukraine move the needle towards victory at home. “It puts pressure on them. This whole story has both psychological and real results,” he told CNN.

A Russian ‘shadow’ fleet, and an escaped Ukrainian naval drone

Earlier this year, a group of Greek fishermen spotted a mysterious black vessel floating near the country’s western island of Lefkada.

It turned out to be a Ukrainian naval drone carrying explosives. Greece issued a formal diplomatic protest to Ukraine and Kyiv officially apologized for the incident, but it blamed Russia for creating the situation by attacking Ukraine and using a “shadow” fleet of oil tankers. These allow Russia to sell its oil in defiance of international sanctions, helping to finance the war.

The drone had escaped from Ukrainian operators deployed to northwestern Libya, where they have been stationed since the end of 2025, the Ukrainian defense intelligence source told CNN.

Servicemen of Ukraine’s Security Service stand guard near the latest versions of its “sea baby” naval drone, in an undisclosed location in on Ukraine October 17, 2025. Vlad Smilianets/Reuters

Their presence there was first reported by French public broadcaster RFI in the spring, and while never officially confirmed by the Ukrainian government, it is now an open secret. One Ukrainian naval drone operator deployed in Libya told CNN his unit was using the international military base in Misrata as a launchpad to attack Russia’s shadow fleet in exchange for training local forces.

Like the aerial drone operator in Mali, he was recruited earlier this year by Ukraine’s Defense Intelligence straight from his previous post in Ukraine.

Ukraine – a longstanding contributor to UN-peacekeeping missions in northern and central Africa before Russia’s full-scale invasion – has made no secret of its desire to become a different kind of player on the continent.

Kyrylo Budanov, Ukraine’s former spy chief who is now the head of Zelensky’s presidential office, said in 2023 that Ukraine’s goal was to “keep killing Russians anywhere on the face of this world until the complete victory of Ukraine.”

It’s a sentiment shared by all the Ukrainian troops who spoke with CNN.

On Monday, Budanov once again pointed to Ukraine’s growing global footprint, posting a statement on social media celebrating its Defense Intelligence for protecting the country’s interests around the world, from “Russia to Africa, in a suit and in camouflage.”

World.title: What it’s like to use the iPhone Duo, Apple’s biggest change to the iPhone in its history
World.content:
Cupertino, CA — The iPhone is getting the biggest change in its nearly 20-year history: a screen that can bend in half.

Apple on Wednesday announced the iPhone Duo, the company’s first foldable smartphone, signaling a major revamp of itsmost important product. Based on my limited time using the phone, it’s clear that Apple is thinking about how a foldable phone could enable people to use their phone differently – like as a bedside clock for example.

The phone has a screen on the outside and opens up to reveal a larger display inside, with cameras on the back, front and inside. It starts at $1,999 and launches on October 23.

Apple is hardly blazing a new path with the Duo. Phone makers like Samsung, Huawei and Motorola have been selling foldable phones for years, though such devices only account for a sliver of global smartphone sales. Apple’s entry into the market is expected to thrust foldable phones into the spotlight, potentially giving them mainstream appeal beyond their early-adopter audience.

Apple CEO John Ternus said at a company event that the iPhone Duo “will redefine the experience of using a foldable phone.”

Whether the iPhone Duo lives up to that claim will depend on if consumers want to spend nearly $2,000 on a phone primarily because it can fold in half.

Many of its most marketed features make the phone seamless to use, based on my limited time using the device. But it’s unclear whether these features will convince people to give up their non-folding phones.

Apple’s entry into the market is expected to thrust foldable phones into the spotlight. Lisa Eadicicco/CNN

A new type of screen for the iPhone

The new device is about the size and shape of a passport, and Apple claims it’s the thinnest iPhone ever when the phone is unfolded. The front screen is 5.4 inches, while the inside display is 7.6 inches.

The inner screen is about the size of an iPad Mini . The screen also has a matte texture that reduces glare and doesn’t seem to easily smudge. Most importantly, the crease is barely visible and you can’t feel it when running your finger across the display.

That’s critical because early foldable phones from Samsung and other companies had very noticeable creases, which made them unappealing to some consumers. However, Samsung and other Android device makers have since changed that, and the latest Galaxy Z Fold 8 has also evolved to become exceptionally thin.

Software that shifts with the phone

The iPhone Duo’s software is an important part of Apple’s strategy. The company emphasized how the software will adjust its position depending on how the phone is being used. When the phone is partially folded, for example, it will automatically slide app content to either side of the screen.

With the iPhone Duo, you can use both cameras at the same time during FaceTime calls, and the outer display can be used to preview shots. Lisa Eadicicco/CNN

This was particularly noticeable when watching a video on the inner screen. As I opened the phone, a Netflix show kept playing while it expanded to fit the larger screen without skipping a beat. Similarly, apps parted in the middle to fit either side of the screen when I slightly folded the phone so that it was shaped like an open book.

You can also use both cameras at the same time during FaceTime calls, and the outer display can be used to preview shots. Apps work in split-screen mode, so you can use multiple apps on the bigger screen at once. Samsung and Google have launched similar features for their foldable phones.

Key to Apple’s future

Apple has faced pressure to launch a new hit product after recent efforts like the Apple Vision Pro headset and last year’s iPhone Air failed to resonate with consumers.

The iPhone is Apple’s most profitable product, generating more than half its revenue. But the device has mostly remained the same over the past two decades, aside from gaining larger screens, better cameras and more advanced processors.

The Duo’s nuances – including the way the software makes adjustments when the display folds in different positions – could be critical for its success. That approach once worked for the iPad and Apple Watch: Apple developed specific software and operating systems to prevent them from feeling like enlarged or shrunken-down versions of the iPhone.

An attendee uses the iPhone Duo in Cupertino, California. Jeff Chiu/AP

For example, the iPhone Duo has a feature called Standby that essentially turns its cover screen into a bedside clock or a photo frame when the phone is locked and propped up like a tent.

Apple already offers this feature on non-folding iPhones, but those devices must be plugged in and propped up on their side. But this mode is much easier to use on a foldable phone that can stand on its own, potentially allowing users to use the iPhone Duo while it’s resting on their desk.

This convenience factor comes into play as the company faces pressure to develop new AI devices. Ternus, Apple’s new CEO, outlined why he believes the iPhone is the ultimate personal computer for artificial intelligence on Wednesday.

It’s clear that Apple hopes an iPhone that can be used in new ways, especially with AI, could help stave off those pressures.

World.title: Trump says Iran likely responsible for attack on vital Saudi oil pipeline
World.content:
US President Donald Trump said Iran was “probably” behind the attack on a vital oil pipeline in Saudi Arabia which led to the pipeline’s closure.

The East-West Pipeline was attacked by several drones coming from Iraq on Thursday, the Saudi foreign ministry said Friday, resulting in injuries and some damage. The energy ministry that the pipeline had been attacked and was shut down as a precautionary measure.

Trump pointed the finger at Iran as most likely being behind the attack when asked about the incident by a reporter during a visit to Ireland on Saturday.

“I think they are, probably they are,” Trump told journalists in Dublin.

He added that he had held a call with Saudi Crown ​Prince Mohammed bin Salman, whom he referred to ​as ‌a “good friend.”

A source told CNN that the Saudi Crown Prince had spoken twice with Trump on Thursday and urged him to strike the Houthis as the Iran-backed group advances towards the Red Sea, but Trump declined.

Responding to a question about the fresh concerns in Saudi Arabia following the closure of the pipeline, and whether he could help move marine traffic through the Strait of Hormuz in light of the developments, Trump said everything will “work out fine.”

The development marked more bad news for the Saudi government after the Iran-backed Houthis captured strategic points along the Red Sea, bringing them close to controlling the Bab al-Mandeb Strait, a critical energy route.

The strike and recent Houthi advances along the Red Sea signal that the kingdom’s oil resources — and its ability to export those resources — are facing increasing threats as the Iran war continues.

Saudi Arabia’s East-West Pipeline has become vital for the country to maintain oil exports since the outbreak of the US-Iran war.

The kingdom has rerouted about 5 million barrels of oil per day that would have been destined for awaiting oil tankers in the Persian Gulf, as Iran effectively shuttered the Strait of Hormuz. Instead, that oil has traveled through the pipeline to Saudi Arabia’s port of Yanbu on the Red Sea.

This is a breaking news story and will be updated with additional information.

World.title: Egyptian TV host Amr Adib warns of oil price surge
World.content:
Egyptian TV host Amr Adib warned of the repercussions that a sharp rise in oil prices—with the price per barrel exceeding US$104—could have on fuel prices in Egypt.

He questioned how the government would handle such high levels, given that it had previously based its calculations on a price of $75 per barrel.

Speaking on his MBC Masr show “Al-Hekaya” (The Story) on Friday evening, Adib noted that oil surpassing $104 per barrel represents a significant development for energy markets, particularly as diesel prices in the US have surged to six dollars per gallon.

“Oil is over $104 a barrel, and diesel has jumped to six dollars a gallon in the US; this is a crucial matter we need to focus on. The world is truly at a historic turning point—I am not trying to scare you,” he stressed.

Adib questioned how this rise would impact fuel prices in Egypt, asking, “There is an issue with oil prices—what will happen, and what should we do? The government had factored in a price of $75 per barrel; so, what do we do now?”

He noted that the rise in global crude oil prices introduces new variables regarding fuel pricing in Egypt, explaining that sustained high prices could have repercussions for the domestic market.

Crisis at the Red Sea

Adib linked the oil crisis to developments in the Red Sea, explaining that the Huthi group’s control over the Bab al-Mandab Strait is impacting the movement of ships passing through the Suez Canal—an additional factor in Egypt’s economic landscape.

In his assessment, Adib views the Huthis as acting to support Iran amidst the war, noting that ongoing regional tensions make it increasingly difficult to predict the trajectory of oil prices in the near term.

Adib emphasized that no one knows when this current situation will end, pointing out that its repercussions extend beyond Egypt to countries worldwide, given the interconnectedness of energy markets with trade flows and maritime corridor stability.

He further stressed that oil prices surpassing the $104 mark necessitates close monitoring of the potential impact on fuel prices in Egypt—particularly given the gap between the current global price and the $75 level that the government had factored into its calculations.

World.title: Everything you need to know about fees and processing times for Egyptian passports
World.content:
Information on fees and processing times for expedited Egyptian passports in 2026 have become a top search topic, driven by desires for citizens to quickly complete travel formalities and obtain their passports—particularly given that costs and delivery times vary based on the specific service level chosen.

The General Administration of Passports, Immigration, and Nationality offers several processing options—including standard, expedited, and immediate services—with costs and delivery times varying according to the citizen’s choice.

2026 Expedited Passport Fees

The fee for an expedited passport in 2026 is approximately LE 1,850 – offering a short turnaround time – while the “immediate” service allows for same-day issuance, subject to applicable regulations and procedures.

How to Obtain an Expedited Passport for the First Time

Citizens can obtain an expedited passport by visiting the passport office serving their area of ​​residence, obtaining the “Passport Form 29,” and filling in the required information.

After completing the form, the citizen submits the necessary documents to the relevant official for review and verification of compliance with procedures.

They then pay the prescribed fees and receive a payment receipt, with the passport to be collected at the scheduled time based on the chosen service type.

The collection timeframe varies depending on the service tier; expedited and immediate services allow for passport receipt within a shorter period compared to the standard service.

Required Documents for Obtaining a Passport (2026)

The documents required to obtain an Egyptian passport in 2026 include the following:

Valid National ID card for individuals aged 16 and older.

Birth certificate for those under the age of 16 who have not yet been issued a National ID card.

Original, stamped educational qualification certificate, if the qualification is not already recorded on the National ID card.

Recent color passport-sized photographs (4×6 cm) with a white background.

For students: Certificate of enrollment indicating the student’s current educational level.

For males: Military service status certificate, along with two copies.

For females: Marriage certificate and two copies to verify the husband’s name for inclusion in the passport.

For children: The father’s original National ID card and two copies.

Processing Time for Egyptian Passports (2026)

The processing time for an Egyptian passport in 2026 varies depending on the service selected by the citizen, as follows:

Expedited Service: The passport is received within 48 hours.

Immediate Service: The passport is issued on the same day.

Standard Service: The processing time ranges from seven to a maximum of 15 days.

Locations for Obtaining Passport

Citizens can obtain a passport from the Ministry of Interior’s Passport, Immigration, and Nationality offices by visiting the office serving the residential area listed on their national ID card.

Residents of various governorates and regions may also visit the Passport and Immigration Authority headquarters at Abbasiya Square during official working hours to submit the required documents to the relevant official and complete the passport issuance procedures.

Edited translation from Al-Masry Al-Youm

World.title: Planning Minister: Egyptian economy shows exceptional resilience amid regional, global challenges
World.content:
Minister of Planning and Economic Development Ahmed Rostom said the Egyptian economy has demonstrated exceptional resilience in the face of regional and international challenges, noting that the growth rate rose to 5.1 percent in fiscal year 2025/2026, up from 4.4 percent in the previous fiscal year and exceeding forecasts by major international institutions.

Rostom made the remarks during a high-level ministerial session held as part of the fourth edition of the Egyptian Entrepreneurship Sector Summit (2026 SDR Summit), organized by Entlaq under the theme “Data × Innovation: Reimagining Egypt’s Entrepreneurship Landscape.”

He stressed that “the real strength of this performance lies not merely in the overall figure, but in the quality and sources of this growth,” explaining that the industrial, trade, and information and communications technology (ICT) sectors collectively contributed around 48 percent of total growth.

Rostom highlighted the strong performance of non-oil manufacturing industries, saying it reflected the success of government efforts to strengthen the country’s productive base.

He noted that Egypt’s growth is being driven by a diverse range of sectors, including industry and service sectors such as ICT, stressing the need to maintain efforts to curb inflation and create more job opportunities.

He said the annual inflation rate declined to 12.7 percent in August 2026, compared with 13 percent in August 2025.

Rostom also highlighted the quality of Egypt’s data, saying it has received recognition from international institutions.

He noted that Egypt had benefited from the economic shocks it faced in previous years and dealt with them effectively, adding that international institutions have confidence in government figures and data issued in accordance with international standards.

He pointed in particular to the recently announced growth figures for the fourth quarter of the previous fiscal year and for the fiscal year as a whole.

The minister said the government aims to raise the share of private investment from 59 percent to 64 percent by 2030, with investment expected to come from a diverse range of sectors, including ICT and logistics, particularly in the Suez Canal Economic Zone.

He also highlighted the government’s efforts to settle outstanding dues owed to foreign companies, saying these measures had helped restore investment by those companies and contributed to positive growth in the petroleum sector.

Rostom said Egypt needs to develop new financing instruments capable of assuming greater risks and providing greater opportunities for expansion.

In this regard, he said the government is working to restructure the National Investment Bank and restore its development role in partnership with the private sector through its subsidiaries, including NI Capital and Ayady, as well as through cooperation with the World Bank on a financing guarantee mechanism for infrastructure projects.

Regarding the entrepreneurship ecosystem, Rostom said the government views startups and innovators as key drivers of digital transformation and future job creation.

He added that the Ministerial Group for Entrepreneurship is currently working to establish a flexible and enabling regulatory and institutional environment aimed at expanding private-sector partnerships, strengthening the venture capital ecosystem and providing financing mechanisms suited to the needs of startups.

Rostom concluded by stressing that the government’s objectives extend beyond achieving high growth rates to implementing a comprehensive economic transformation program focused on competitiveness and expanding private investment in five key sectors: industry, agriculture and food processing, tourism, ICT, and energy security.

He said the program seeks to translate macroeconomic stability into sustainable growth that boosts exports and improves living standards across all governorates.

World.title: Civil Aviation Minister, IFC review developments in Hurghada airport tender
World.content:
Civil Aviation Minister Sameh al-Hefny met on Friday, September 11, 2026, with International Finance Corporation (IFC) Regional Director for North Africa and the Horn of Africa Ary Naim, IFC Egypt Country Manager Saad Sabra and IFC Infrastructure Projects Specialist Mohamed Mehni on the sidelines of the EIAS 2026 International Airshow and Space Exhibition in El Alamein city, northwestern Egypt, to review the latest developments in the tendering procedures for the management, operation and development of Hurghada International Airport under a public-private partnership (PPP) scheme.

The minister said the project comes as part of the Egyptian state’s directives to continue developing the civil aviation sector, enhance services provided to passengers and improve the overall travel experience.

al-Hefny praised the IFC’s role in providing technical and advisory support for the project, highlighting its international experience in preparing and implementing public-private partnership projects.

For his part, Naim affirmed the IFC’s commitment to continuing cooperation with the Ministry of Civil Aviation and supporting the project during its upcoming stages, contributing to the completion of the tendering procedures in accordance with international standards.

World.title: Former Maryland Quizzer Donates to Team, Pledges Help After Poor Living Conditions Exposed
World.content:
MONROVIA — A former Maryland County quizzer and coach, Freddie Goe, has donated US$35 to the county’s quizzing team following reports about the difficult conditions under which the players are staying during the ongoing National Quizzing Tournament.

By Peter P. Toe, Jr., [email protected]

Goe visited the team on Friday and also pledged to support their feeding and help improve their sleeping arrangements after reports that some players were sleeping on the bare floor due to limited mattresses.

The team is currently staying at a local school building in Day Break Mouth Open Community, where technical staff said the players have been facing challenges with accommodation, food and transportation.

The assistance from Goe follows earlier support from Maryland County Youth President Melvin Weah, who also provided assistance to the team.

The Maryland Students Union (MaSU) leadership also reported receiving US$10 and LRD$8,000 in support, including US$10 and LRD$7,000 from the Maryland Youth Association (MYA) and US$10 and LRD$1,000 from Marylanders based in Monrovia.

The MaSU leadership said the funds were being used to help cover transportation and feeding, while additional support is needed to secure suitable accommodation and provide some compensation for the players.

Speaking after the donation, Goe confirmed the support and appealed to other Marylanders to assist the team.

“As a former Quizzer and Quizzing Coach, I had to give back considering the challenges the team is faced with. We also seek the help of other meaningful Marylanders to contribute to the team for a success,” Goe said.»

Goe, a Senior Operations Engineer at the Liberia Electricity Corporation, previously quizzed for Central Site High School from 2013 to 2016 and later coached the school’s quizzing team from 2017 to 2022.

Meanwhile, Maryland has already recorded a win in the tournament, defeating Bong County 130–100, a 30-point margin. Team captain Leo Dickson was named Man of the Match after the victory.

Despite the win, members of the team continue to appeal for assistance with food, transportation and suitable accommodation as they prepare for their remaining matches.

World.title: Sleeping on the Bare Floor: Maryland Quizzing Team Battles Hardship for National Glory
World.content:
MONROVIA — Despite defeating Bong County 130 points to 100, a 30-point margin, in their first encounter at the ongoing National Quizzing Tournament, Maryland’s quizzing team is battling difficult living conditions, with some players sleeping on the bare floor due to a shortage of mattresses.

By Peter Poklo Toe-Jr

A photo shows members of the Maryland team sleeping on the floor, currently staying on a local school campus in Barnesville’s Day Break Mouth Open Community, where team officials say players are sleeping in open classrooms, highlighting the difficult conditions they are facing while representing the county in the national competition.

Despite the difficult conditions off the competition floor, Maryland delivered a strong performance against Bong County, securing a 130–100 victory.

Team Captain Leo Dickson was also named Man of the Match following Maryland’s victory.

In a video podcast Thursday after the game, Maryland Students Union (MaSU) President Eastman K. Toe appealed for urgent support for the team.

“It was on yesterday that we received the sum of L$8,000 plus US$10, which was L$7,000 from MYA President Melvin T. Weah and L$1,000 plus US$10 from Marylanders based in Monrovia,” Toe said.

He added: “Finance to cover transport and feedings. For the sake of security, we need unique accommodation and finance to help give little compensation to the players for encouragement.”

Toe said the team continues to face challenges with transportation, food and accommodation.

He said the team had planned to reach out to Maryland lawmakers for assistance but realized that many of the county’s lawmakers were not present in Monrovia.

Despite the challenges, Captain Leo Dickson said the players remain grateful for their achievement and determined to continue representing Maryland.

“We are grateful that we got this achievement. Through the challenges, we remained focused, and this is why we have come this far. But we deeply need our people to come through for us,” Dickson said.

The team’s Assistant Coach also acknowledged the difficulties facing the players but said their focus remains on succeeding for Maryland.

“We have been through the struggle. We have been through a lot of challenges since we arrived here. But we have Maryland as our focus to succeed,” the Assistant Coach said.

“But as players, this is not easy for us,” the Assistant coach added.

Technical staff member Samuel H. Griffiths Jr. said the team is particularly struggling with mobility and food.

Griffiths said the team’s sleeping arrangements are unsuitable because members are staying in open classrooms.

He said the team has largely survived on support from MaSU leadership and assistance from the Ministry of Youth Affairs, while contributions from other supporters have remained limited.

“The team need serious resources for mobility and food,” Griffiths said.

He added that the Maryland team is expected to be at the quizzing hall today to watch matches involving other counties.

Head Coach Edwin Lawal also appealed to Marylanders and other well-wishers to support the team as the competition continues.

“Your one cent means a lot for us. While encouraging our players, your support as a county is the most right now,” Lawal said.

Maryland is competing in Group C, alongside Grand Bassa, Bong and Nimba counties.

The team is now appealing to Maryland lawmakers, county authorities, businesses, Marylanders at home and abroad, and other well-wishers for assistance with food, transportation, suitable accommodation and financial support for the players as they continue their quest for national glory.

The team is led by MaSU president Eastman K. Toe, Head Coach Edwin Lawal, Captain Leo Dickson, amongst other.
